questions.explanation:

A private hosted zone must be associated with the VPC that hosts the inbound endpoint for that endpoint to resolve records in the zone. Sharing Resolver rules through AWS Resource Access Manager lets the application VPCs use the centralized outbound DNS-forwarding configuration.

A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company recently had a network security breach. A network engineer needs to collect and analyze logs containing the client IP address, target IP address, target port, and user agent for every user who accesses the application.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Configure the ALB to store logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Download the files from Amazon S3, and use a spreadsheet application to analyze the logs.
Configure the ALB to push logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the logs.

Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to stream data from the ALB to Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service). Use search operations in Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) to analyze the data.
Configure the ALB to store logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to analyze the logs in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer access logs are delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket and include the `client:port`, `target:port`, and `user_agent` fields. Amazon Athena can query those logs directly in Amazon S3 using SQL, avoiding manual file downloads and avoiding the operational overhead of an unsupported direct ALB-to-Kinesis ingestion design.

**Learn more:** [Access logs for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html) · [Query Application Load Balancer logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/application-load-balancer-logs.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Network Firewall to protect outbound traffic for multiple VPCs in the same AWS account. Each VPC contains Amazon EC2 instances that host the company’s applications. Every EC2 instance is tagged with the name of the application that it hosts. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups.  
  
A Network Firewall stateful rule group must stay current even when an Auto Scaling group launches or terminates EC2 instances.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** implementation and administrative effort?

options.text: Create a network ACL for each application. Reference the network ACL in the stateful rule group.
Create a prefix list for each application. Reference the prefix list in the stateful rule group.
Create an AWS Lambda function that queries the EC2 instance tags for each application name and then updates the stateful rule group with the IP address of each instance.
Create a resource group for each application name. Reference the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the resource groups in the stateful rule group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall tag-based resource groups can group EC2 instances by their application-name tag and be referenced by a stateful rule group. Network Firewall automatically updates the rule group with the IP addresses of matching resources as instances are added, changed, or removed, so Auto Scaling lifecycle changes require no custom update automation.

**Learn more:** [Using tag-based resource groups in Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/resource-groups.html) · [Settings for the resource groups that you use in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/resource-group-settings.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating applications from a data center to AWS. Many applications will need to exchange data with the company’s on-premises mainframe.  
  
The company must achieve transfer speeds of 4 Gbps to satisfy peak traffic demands. A network engineer must design a highly available solution that maximizes resiliency. The solution must withstand the loss of circuits or routers.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Order four 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections that are evenly spread over two locations. Terminate one connection from each Direct Connect location to a router at the company location. Terminate the other connection from each Direct Connect location to a different router at the company location.
Order two 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections that are evenly spread over two locations. Terminate the connection from each Direct Connect location to a different router at the company location.

Order four 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections that are evenly spread over two locations. Terminate one connection from each Direct Connect location to a router at the company location. Terminate the other connection from each Direct Connect location to a different router at the company location.
Order two 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections that are evenly spread over two locations. Terminate the connection from each Direct Connect location to a different router at the company location.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect maximum resiliency uses separate connections that terminate on separate devices in more than one Direct Connect location, protecting against device, connectivity, and complete-location failures. Four 10-Gbps connections across two locations and two on-premises routers preserve far more than 4 Gbps of capacity after a circuit or router failure while maintaining redundancy at every layer.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect Resiliency Toolkit](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/resiliency_toolkit.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an AWS environment containing multiple VPCs connected through a transit gateway. The company has chosen AWS Site-to-Site VPN to establish connectivity between its on-premises network and its AWS environment.  
  
The company does not have a static public IP address for its on-premises network. A network engineer must implement a solution that initiates the VPN connection from the AWS side for traffic from the AWS environment to the on-premises network.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to establish VPN connectivity between the transit gateway and the on-premises network? (Choose three.)

options.text: Configure the Site-to-Site VPN tunnel options to use Internet Key Exchange version 1 (IKEv1).
Configure the Site-to-Site VPN tunnel options to use Internet Key Exchange version 2 (IKEv2).
Use a private certificate authority (CA) from AWS Private Certificate Authority to create a certificate.
Use a public certificate authority (CA) from AWS Private Certificate Authority to create a certificate.
Create a customer gateway. Specify the current dynamic IP address of the customer gateway device’s external interface.
Create a customer gateway without specifying the IP address of the customer gateway device.

questions.explanation:
AWS-side IKE initiation is supported only for IKEv2. AWS also requires the public IP address of the customer gateway device to initiate IKE, so the customer gateway must specify its current external IP address even if that address is dynamic. Certificate-based Site-to-Site VPN authentication uses a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority.

**Learn more:** [AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel initiation options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels.html) · [AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel authentication options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-tunnel-authentication-options.html)

Recently, the owner of VPC-A added an additional CIDR range to the VPC. The VPC-A owner created workloads that use the added CIDR range.  
  
The company's on-premises network cannot reach the new workloads. The network engineer must resolve the network connectivity issue and ensure that connectivity is not affected if more VPC CIDR ranges are added to the VPC in the future.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Configure route propagation for VPC-A to the VPN attachment route table.
Manually update the VPN attachment route table to include the new CIDR range.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the rule to matches an update to the VPC-A CIDR range. Configure the Lambda function to update the VPN attachment route table.

Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function when there is an update to the VPC-A CIDR range. Configure the Lambda function to update the VPN attachment route table. Restart the VPN tunnels.

questions.explanation:
For a dynamically routed Site-to-Site VPN, the transit gateway advertises routes from the route table associated with the VPN attachment to the customer gateway through BGP. Enabling propagation of VPC-A's attachment to that route table automatically installs VPC-A CIDR routes, including subsequently added non-overlapping CIDR ranges, so they can be advertised without manual route updates or automation.

A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). To increase application availability, a solutions architect added EC2 instances in a second Availability Zone and added those instances to the NLB target group.  
  
The company’s operations team observes that traffic is routed only to the instances in the first Availability Zone.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution to resolve this problem?

options.text: Enable the new Availability Zone on the NLB
Create a new NLB for the instances in the second Availability Zone
Enable proxy protocol on the NLB
Create a new target group with the instances in both Availability Zones

questions.explanation:
An NLB must have an Availability Zone enabled, with a subnet selected, before it creates a load balancer node there and routes requests to registered targets in that zone. Registering targets alone does not enable routing to an otherwise disabled Availability Zone. Enabling the second Availability Zone on the existing NLB is therefore sufficient and avoids unnecessary new load balancers or target groups.

**Learn more:** [Update the Availability Zones for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/availability-zones.html) · [How Elastic Load Balancing works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)

questions.explanation:

options.text: Configure only the Firewall Manager administrator account to join the organization.
Configure all the accounts to join the organization.
Set an account as the Firewall Manager administrator account.
Set an account as the Firewall Manager child account.
Set up AWS Config for all the accounts and all the Regions where the company has resources.
Set up AWS Config for only the organization's management account.

questions.explanation:
AWS Firewall Manager centrally applies and monitors policies across accounts that belong to an AWS Organization. A Firewall Manager administrator account must be designated, and AWS Config must be enabled for every organization member account, including the administrator, in every Region containing resources to protect so Firewall Manager can evaluate policy compliance.

A network engineer must implement a solution that establishes connectivity between the existing VPC and the new VPC. The solution must also provide IPv6 support for the new VPC. New on-premises resources must connect to VPC resources by using IPv6 addresses.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new virtual private gateway in us-east-1. Attach the new virtual private gateway to the new VPC. Create two new Site-to-Site VPN connections to the new virtual private gateway with IPv4 and IPv6 support. Configure routing between the VPCs by using VPC peering.

Create a transit gateway in us-east-1 and in us-east-2. Attach the existing VPC and the new VPC to each transit gateway. Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection to each transit gateway with IPv4 and IPv6 support. Configure transit gateway peering. Configure routing between the VPCs and the on-premises environment.

Create a new virtual private gateway in us-east-2. Attach the new virtual private gateway to the new VPCreate two new Site-to-Site VPN connections to the new virtual private gateway with IPv4 and IPv6 support. Configure routing between the VPCs by using VPC peering.

Create a transit gateway in us-east-1. Attach the existing VPC and the new VPC to the transit gateway. Create two new Site-to-Site VPN connections to the transit gateway with IPv4 and IPv6 support. Configure transit gateway peering. Configure routing between the VPCs and the on-premises environment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections that use a virtual private gateway do not support IPv6 traffic; a transit gateway supports IPv6 traffic in VPN tunnels. Because AWS Transit Gateway is a Regional service, connecting VPCs in `us-east-1` and `us-east-2` requires a transit gateway in each Region and an inter-Region transit gateway peering connection. IPv4 and IPv6 traffic require separate Site-to-Site VPN connections, with routing configured between the VPCs and the on-premises environment.

An international company provides early warnings about tsunamis. The company plans to use IoT devices to monitor sea waves worldwide. Data collected by the IoT devices must reach the company’s infrastructure on AWS as quickly as possible. The company uses three operations centers around the world. Each operations center connects to AWS through its own AWS Direct Connect connection. Each operations center connects to the internet through at least two upstream internet service providers.  
  
The company owns provider-independent (PI) address space. The IoT devices use TCP protocols to reliably transmit the data that they collect. The IoT devices have both landline and mobile internet connectivity. The infrastructure and solution will be deployed in multiple AWS Regions. The company will use Amazon Route 53 for DNS services.  
  
A network engineer must design connectivity between the IoT devices and the services running in the AWS Cloud.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **HIGHEST** availability?

options.text: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with origin failover. Create an origin group for each Region where the solution is deployed.
Set up Route 53 latency-based routing. Add latency alias records. For the latency alias records, set the value of Evaluate Target Health to Yes.
Set up an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure Regional endpoint groups and health checks.
Set up Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) addresses. Use the same PI addresses for each Region where the solution is deployed.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides anycast static IP entry points that accept traffic at an AWS edge location near each client and carries it across the redundant AWS global network. A standard accelerator supports TCP listeners, regional endpoint groups, and endpoint health checks; it directs new connections to healthy endpoints in the optimal Region based on client location and endpoint health. This provides fast global ingress and regional failover without relying on DNS caching or public-internet routing for the full path.

Which solution will resolve this issue with the **LEAST** administrative overhead for future expansion efforts?

A company runs its IT services in a multi-site hybrid infrastructure. The company deploys resources on AWS in the `us-east-1` Region and the `eu-west-2` Region. It also deploys resources in its own data centers in the United States (US) and the United Kingdom (UK). In both AWS Regions, the company uses a transit gateway to interconnect 15 VPCs. The company has established a transit gateway peering connection between the two transit gateways. The VPC CIDR blocks do not overlap with one another or with IP addresses used in the data centers. The VPC CIDR prefixes can be aggregated either at a Regional level or across the company's entire AWS environment.  
  
The data centers connect to each other through a private WAN connection. IP routing information is dynamically exchanged through Interior BGP (iBGP) sessions. The data centers retain connectivity to AWS by using one AWS Direct Connect connection in the US and one Direct Connect connection in the UK. Each Direct Connect connection terminates on a Direct Connect gateway and is associated with its local transit gateway through a transit VIF.  
  
Traffic takes the shortest geographic path from source to destination. For example, packets from the UK data center that target resources in `eu-west-2` traverse the local Direct Connect connection. For cross-Region data transfers, such as from the UK data center to VPCs in `us-east-1`, the private WAN connection must be used to minimize AWS costs. A network engineer has configured each transit gateway association on the Direct Connect gateway to advertise VPC-specific CIDR IP prefixes only for the local Region. Routes to the other Region must be learned through BGP from routers in the other data center in their original, non-aggregated form.  
  
The company recently had a cross-Region data-transfer issue because of problems with its private WAN connection. The network engineer must modify the routing configuration to avoid similar disruptions in the future. The solution must not change the original traffic-routing goal during normal operation.  
  
Which modifications meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Remove all the VPC CIDR prefixes from the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection. Add the company's entire AWS environment aggregate route to the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection.

Add the CIDR prefixes from the other Region VPCs and the local VPC CIDR blocks to the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection. Configure data center routers to make routing decisions based on the BGP communities received.
Add the aggregate IP prefix for the other Region and the local VPC CIDR blocks to the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection.
Add the aggregate IP prefix for the company's entire AWS environment and the local VPC CIDR blocks to the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection.

Remove all the VPC CIDR prefixes from the list of subnets advertised through the local Direct Connect connection. Add both Regional aggregate IP prefixes to the list of subnets advertised through the Direct Connect connection on both sides of the network. Configure data center routers to make routing decisions based on the BGP communities received.

questions.explanation:
During normal operation, cross-Region traffic must keep using the private WAN (to avoid inter-Region charges over the transit gateway peering), so the Direct Connect + TGW-peering path may only be a failover. Both correct answers rely on Regional aggregation, not entire-environment aggregation. Option C uses longest-prefix match: advertise the other Region's aggregate over the local Direct Connect while the WAN still carries the original, more-specific (non-aggregated) prefixes, so the specific WAN routes always win and the aggregate is used only if the WAN fails. Option E uses BGP communities: advertise both Regional aggregates on both Direct Connect sides and have the data-center routers prefer WAN-learned routes via community-based policy, falling back to Direct Connect when the WAN drops. Options A and D are wrong because aggregating across the company's entire AWS environment also covers the local Region and can hairpin local traffic across Regions; B abandons aggregation and just advertises specifics.

**Learn more:** [Allowed prefixes for Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/allowed-to-prefixes.html) · [Direct Connect gateway and transit gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in the VPC. Use Traffic Mirroring by specifying the NAT gateway as the source and the EC2 instance as the destination. Analyze the captured traffic by using open-source tools to identify the AWS resources that are generating the suspicious traffic.

Use VPC flow logs. Launch a security information and event management (SIEM) solution in the VPC. Configure the SIEM solution to ingest the VPC flow logs. Run queries on the SIEM solution to identify the AWS resources that are generating the suspicious traffic.

Which architecture solution will optimize this workload?

A company has five VPCs in the `us-east-1` Region. It hosts an internal web application in `us-east-1`. One company VPC, named VPC-A, must connect to an external partner's AWS environment. The partner environment is in the same AWS Region, where the partner hosts a new version of the company's web application in a VPC named VPC-B.  
  
The company has Amazon EC2 instances in VPC-A that must connect to the web application in VPC-B. A network engineer discovers that the partner's VPC-B and the company's VPC-A use the same IP space. The network engineer needs a solution that allows the EC2 instances to connect to the web application without negatively affecting the existing environment of either the company or the partner.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Establish a VPC peering connection between VPC-A to VPC-B.
Ensure the partner creates a VPC endpoint service that uses a Network Load Balancer in VPC-B.
Deploy a VPC endpoint in VPC-A that uses a VPC endpoint service that is shared by the partner.
Deploy a new routable VPC CIDR block as a secondary CIDR block to both VPC-A and VPC-B. Deploy a public NAT gateway in VPC-A.
Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink supports private, service-specific connectivity even when the consumer and provider VPCs have overlapping IP address ranges. The partner must publish the application through a VPC endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer, and the company must create an interface VPC endpoint in VPC-A to consume that shared service. VPC peering cannot be established between VPCs with overlapping CIDR blocks.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink in a multi-VPC network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/aws-privatelink.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an AWS environment containing multiple VPCs connected through a transit gateway. The company wants to use a certificate-based AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to establish connectivity between an on-premises environment and the AWS environment. The company does not have a static public IP address for its on-premises environment.  
  
Which combination of steps should the company perform to establish VPN connectivity between the transit gateway and the on-premises environment? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
Create a private certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
Configure the Site-to-Site VPN tunnels to use the pre-shared key (PSK).
Create a customer gateway. Specify the current dynamic IP address of the customer gateway device's external interface.
Create a customer gateway. Do not specify the IP address of the customer gateway device.

questions.explanation:
Certificate-based AWS Site-to-Site VPN authentication uses a private certificate from a subordinate CA in AWS Private CA, available through AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). With that private certificate configured on the customer gateway, AWS does not require a customer gateway device IP address, allowing the device’s dynamic public IP address to change without reconfiguring the VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel authentication options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-tunnel-authentication-options.html) · [Customer gateway options for AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/cgw-options.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB serves as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company wants to implement a custom authentication system that provides a token to authenticated customers.  
  
Before delivering content, the web application must ensure that GET/POST requests originate from authenticated customers. A network engineer must design a solution that enables the web application to identify authorized customers.  
  
What is the **MOST operationally efficient** solution that satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Use the ALB to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Use an AWS Lambda function to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.

Integrate AWS WAF with the ALB to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Configure the ALB listener to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.

Use an AWS Lambda@Edge function to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Use the Lambda@Edge function also to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.

Set up an EC2 instance that has a third-party packet inspection tool to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Configure the tool to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.

questions.explanation:
Lambda@Edge can inspect an authorization token in a CloudFront request, including a request body when the Include Body option is enabled, and add a custom request header before CloudFront forwards the request to the ALB origin. The application can trust that header to identify authenticated requests, while authentication processing occurs at the edge without operating additional inspection infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Ways to use Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-ways-to-use.html) · [Lambda@Edge event structure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-event-structure.html)

A company is building an application in which IoT devices will send measurements to the AWS Cloud. The application will support millions of end users. The company finds that the IoT devices do not support DNS resolution. The company must implement an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling solution so the IoT devices can connect to an application endpoint without DNS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer (ALB)-type target group for a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the ALB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the NLB.

Use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with an Application Load Balancer (ALB) endpoint. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the ALSet up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the accelerator.
Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the NLB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the NLB.

Use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) endpoint. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the NLB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the accelerator.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer supports static IP addresses and can use an instance target group attached to an EC2 Auto Scaling group, which automatically registers newly launched instances. Devices can therefore use the NLB IP addresses directly while the backend scales dynamically. AWS Global Accelerator would add separate hourly and traffic charges, and an additional ALB is unnecessary when no Layer 7 routing capability is required.

**Learn more:** [What is a Network Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html) · [Target groups for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company recently provisioned several AWS resources in the eu-central-1 Region in a single VPC near its users in that area. The network engineer must connect the eu-central-1 resources to the on-premises data center and to the eu-west-2 resources. The solution must minimize changes to the Direct Connect connection."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should the network engineer do to meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new virtual private gateway. Attach the new virtual private gateway to the VPC in eu-central-1. Use a transit VIF to connect the VPC and the Direct Connect router.","B":"Create a new transit gateway in eu-central-1. Create a peering attachment request to the transit gateway in eu-west-2. Add a static route in the transit gateway route table in eu-central-1 to point to the transit gateway peering attachment. Accept the peering request. Add a static route in the transit gateway route table in eu-west-2 to point to the new transit gateway peering attachment.","C":"Create a new transit gateway in eu-central-1. Use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to peer both transit gateways. Add a static route in the transit gateway route table in eu-central-1 to point to the transit gateway VPN attachment. Add a static route in the transit gateway route table in eu-west-2 to point to the new transit gateway peering attachment.","D":"Create a new virtual private gateway. Attach the new virtual private gateway to the VPC in eu-central-1. Use a public VIF to connect the VPC and the Direct Connect router."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"AWS Transit Gateway inter-Region peering connects transit gateways through the AWS global network. Creating a transit gateway in eu-central-1, attaching the new VPC, peering it with the existing eu-west-2 transit gateway, and routing both transit gateway route tables to their peering attachments extends connectivity to the existing eu-west-2 VPCs and their Direct Connect-attached on-premises network without altering the Direct Connect connection.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transit Gateway?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html) · [Allowed prefixes interactions for Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/allowed-to-prefixes.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"504a5b3f-8af0-4c92-8229-7f76154f6b36","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company has Amazon EC2 instances in VPC-A that must connect to the web application in VPC-B. A network engineer discovers that the partner's VPC-B and the company's VPC-A use the same IP space. The network engineer needs a solution that allows the EC2 instances to connect to the web application without negatively affecting the existing environment of either the company or the partner."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to meet these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Establish a VPC peering connection between VPC-A to VPC-B.","B":"Ensure the partner creates a VPC endpoint service that uses a Network Load Balancer in VPC-B.","C":"Deploy a VPC endpoint in VPC-A that uses a VPC endpoint service that is shared by the partner.","D":"Deploy a new routable VPC CIDR block as a secondary CIDR block to both VPC-A and VPC-B. Deploy a public NAT gateway in VPC-A.","E":"Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between VPC-A and VPC-B."},"correctAnswer":"BC","explanation":"AWS PrivateLink supports private, service-specific connectivity even when the consumer and provider VPCs have overlapping IP address ranges. The partner must publish the application through a VPC endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer, and the company must create an interface VPC endpoint in VPC-A to consume that shared service. VPC peering cannot be established between VPCs with overlapping CIDR blocks.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink in a multi-VPC network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/aws-privatelink.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"f79de316-31d0-43f2-a9e8-e41099c549e5","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
51:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company has an AWS environment containing multiple VPCs connected through a transit gateway. The company wants to use a certificate-based AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to establish connectivity between an on-premises environment and the AWS environment. The company does not have a static public IP address for its on-premises environment."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps should the company perform to establish VPN connectivity between the transit gateway and the on-premises environment?"]}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a public certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).","B":"Create a private certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).","C":"Configure the Site-to-Site VPN tunnels to use the pre-shared key (PSK).","D":"Create a customer gateway. Specify the current dynamic IP address of the customer gateway device's external interface.","E":"Create a customer gateway. Do not specify the IP address of the customer gateway device."},"correctAnswer":"BE","explanation":"Certificate-based AWS Site-to-Site VPN authentication uses a private certificate from a subordinate CA in AWS Private CA, available through AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). With that private certificate configured on the customer gateway, AWS does not require a customer gateway device IP address, allowing the device’s dynamic public IP address to change without reconfiguring the VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel authentication options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-tunnel-authentication-options.html) · [Customer gateway options for AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/cgw-options.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"a503bb22-992c-4a26-9a9e-b7af6a8ccaba","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB serves as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company wants to implement a custom authentication system that provides a token to authenticated customers."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Before delivering content, the web application must ensure that GET/POST requests originate from authenticated customers. A network engineer must design a solution that enables the web application to identify authorized customers."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["What is the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"MOST operationally efficient"}]," solution that satisfies these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use the ALB to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Use an AWS Lambda function to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.","B":"Integrate AWS WAF with the ALB to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Configure the ALB listener to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.","C":"Use an AWS Lambda@Edge function to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Use the Lambda@Edge function also to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request.","D":"Set up an EC2 instance that has a third-party packet inspection tool to inspect the authorized token inside the GET/POST request payload. Configure the tool to insert a customized header to inform the web application of an authenticated customer request."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Lambda@Edge can inspect an authorization token in a CloudFront request, including a request body when the Include Body option is enabled, and add a custom request header before CloudFront forwards the request to the ALB origin. The application can trust that header to identify authenticated requests, while authentication processing occurs at the edge without operating additional inspection infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Ways to use Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-edge-ways-to-use.html) · [Lambda@Edge event structure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-event-structure.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"012af5c2-a095-43ee-aa5a-3cf46af7abfc","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
53:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is building an application in which IoT devices will send measurements to the AWS Cloud. The application will support millions of end users. The company finds that the IoT devices do not support DNS resolution. The company must implement an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling solution so the IoT devices can connect to an application endpoint without DNS."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?"}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use an Application Load Balancer (ALB)-type target group for a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the ALB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the NLB.","B":"Use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with an Application Load Balancer (ALB) endpoint. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the ALSet up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the accelerator.","C":"Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the NLB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the NLB.","D":"Use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) endpoint. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the NLB. Set up the IoT devices to connect to the IP addresses of the accelerator."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"A Network Load Balancer supports static IP addresses and can use an instance target group attached to an EC2 Auto Scaling group, which automatically registers newly launched instances. Devices can therefore use the NLB IP addresses directly while the backend scales dynamically. AWS Global Accelerator would add separate hourly and traffic charges, and an additional ALB is unnecessary when no Layer 7 routing capability is required.

**Learn more:** [What is a Network Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/introduction.html) · [Target groups for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"776a54d2-a6e5-41ef-96ea-bb166afcc6a9","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
A company must manage Amazon EC2 instances through command-line interfaces from Linux and Windows hosts. The EC2 instances run in an environment with no route to the internet. The company must implement role-based access control for managing the instances. The company has a standalone on-premises environment.  
  
Which approach satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** maintenance overhead?

options.text: Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises environment and the VPC where the instances are deployed. Configure routing, security groups, and ACLs. Connect to the instances by using the Direct Connect connection.
Deploy and configure AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) on each instance. Deploy VPC endpoints for Systems Manager Session Manager. Connect to the instances by using Session Manager.

Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises environment and the VPC where the instances are deployed. Configure routing, security groups, and ACLs. Connect to the instances by using the Site-to-Site VPN connection.

Deploy an appliance to the VPC where the instances are deployed. Assign a public IP address to the appliance. Configure security groups and ACLs. Connect to the instances by using the appliance as an intermediary.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager uses SSM Agent to provide interactive command-line access to managed EC2 instances. Systems Manager interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) allow the agent to communicate privately with Systems Manager without an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or Direct Connect connection. IAM policies centrally control which users or roles can start sessions to which managed nodes, avoiding the operational overhead of managing network connectivity, bastion hosts, or an intermediary appliance.

**Learn more:** [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html) · [Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-create-vpc.html)

A company plans to move both its DNS registrar and DNS hosting to Amazon Route 53. Its website receives tens of thousands of visits daily, and its current DNS provider cannot handle the load. The company needs to migrate as quickly as possible but cannot accept any downtime.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Transfer the domain name to Route 53. Create a Route 53 private hosted zone, and copy all the existing DNS records. Update the name servers on the domain to use the name servers that are specified in the newly created private hosted zone.

Copy all DNS records from the existing DNS servers to a Route 53 private hosted zone. Update the name servers with the existing registrar to use the private hosted zone name servers. Transfer the domain name to Route 53. Ensure that all the changes have propagated.

Transfer the domain name to Route 53. Create a Route 53 public hosted zone, and copy all the existing DNS records. Set the TTL value on each record to 1 second. Update the name servers on the domain to use the name servers that are specified in the newly created public hosted zone.

Copy all DNS records from the existing DNS servers to a Route 53 public hosted zone. Update the name servers with the existing registrar to use the Route 53 name servers for the hosted zone. When the changes have propagated, perform a domain name transfer to Route 53.

questions.explanation:
A public Route 53 hosted zone is required for Internet DNS resolution. Recreate the existing records in that zone, change the name servers at the current registrar to the Route 53 name servers, and allow the DNS change to propagate before transferring the domain registration. This keeps DNS service available throughout the registrar transfer; AWS specifically advises migrating DNS service before transferring registration when the current registrar might stop providing DNS service.

**Learn more:** [Making Route 53 the DNS service for a domain that's in use](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/migrate-dns-domain-in-use.html) · [Making Amazon Route 53 the DNS service for an existing domain](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/MigratingDNS.html)

A company has deployed its AWS environment in one AWS Region. The environment includes a few hundred application VPCs, a shared services VPC, and a VPN connection to the company’s on-premises environment. A network engineer must implement a transit gateway with these requirements:  
  
- Application VPCs must remain isolated from one another.  
- Bidirectional communication must be permitted between the application VPCs and the on-premises network.  
- Bidirectional communication must be permitted between the application VPCs and the shared services VPC.  
  
The network engineer creates the transit gateway with the default route table association and default route table propagation options disabled. The network engineer also creates the VPN attachment for the on-premises network and the VPC attachments for the application VPCs and the shared services VPC.  
  
The network engineer must satisfy all transit gateway requirements by designing a solution that uses the fewest transit gateway route tables.  
  
Which combination of actions should the network engineer take to achieve this goal? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure a separate transit gateway route table for on premises. Associate the VPN attachment with this transit gateway route table. Propagate all application VPC attachments to this transit gateway route table.

Configure a separate transit gateway route table for each application VPC. Associate each application VPC attachment with its respective transit gateway route table. Propagate the shared services VPC attachment and the VPN attachment to this transit gateway route table.

Configure a separate transit gateway route table for all application VPCs. Associate all application VPCs with this transit gateway route table. Propagate the shared services VPC attachment and the VPN attachment to this transit gateway route table.

Configure a separate transit gateway route table for the shared services VPC. Associate the shared services VPC attachment with this transit gateway route table. Propagate all application VPC attachments to this transit gateway route table.

Configure a separate transit gateway route table for on premises and the shared services VPC. Associate the VPN attachment and the shared services VPC attachment with this transit gateway route table. Propagate all application VPC attachments to this transit gateway route table.

questions.explanation:
A transit gateway attachment can be associated with only one route table, and an attachment’s propagated routes are added to the selected propagation route table. Associating every application VPC attachment with one route table that receives only the VPN and shared-services routes permits application-to-on-premises and application-to-shared-services traffic while omitting routes to other application VPCs. Associating both the VPN and shared-services attachments with a second route table that receives routes from all application VPC attachments provides the required return paths. This design uses the minimum of two transit gateway route tables.

**Learn more:** [AssociateTransitGatewayRouteTable API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_AssociateTransitGatewayRouteTable.html) · [EnableTransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_EnableTransitGatewayRouteTablePropagation.html)

A network engineer is designing a hybrid architecture that uses a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the company data center and two AWS Regions: us-east-1 and eu-west-1. The VPCs in us-east-1 are connected by a transit gateway and require access to several on-premises databases. Under company policy, only one VPC in eu-west-1 may connect to one on-premises server. The on-premises network separates traffic between the databases and the server.  
  
How should the network engineer configure the Direct Connect connection to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create one hosted connection. Use a transit VIF to connect to the transit gateway in us-east-1. Use a private VIF to connect to the VPC in eu-west-1. Use one Direct. Connect gateway for both VIFs to route from the Direct Connect locations to the corresponding AWS Region along the path that has the lowest latency.

Create one hosted connection. Use a transit VIF to connect to the transit gateway in us-east-1. Use a private VIF to connect to the VPC in eu-west-1. Use two Direct Connect gateways, one for each VIF, to route from the Direct Connect locations to the corresponding AWS Region along the path that has the lowest latency.

Create one dedicated connection. Use a transit VIF to connect to the transit gateway in us-east-1. Use a private VIF to connect to the VPC in eu-west-1. Use one Direct Connect gateway for both VIFs to route from the Direct Connect locations to the corresponding AWS Region along the path that has the lowest latency.

Create one dedicated connection. Use a transit VIF to connect to the transit gateway in us-east-1. Use a private VIF to connect to the VPC in eu-west-1. Use two Direct Connect gateways, one for each VIF, to route from the Direct Connect locations to the corresponding AWS Region along the path that has the lowest latency.

questions.explanation:
A 1 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection supports the required bandwidth. A transit VIF connects the us-east-1 transit gateway through a Direct Connect gateway, while the eu-west-1 VPC requires a private VIF path. AWS prohibits associating a Direct Connect gateway with a transit gateway when that Direct Connect gateway is already associated with a virtual private gateway or attached to a private VIF; therefore, separate Direct Connect gateways are required for the transit and private VIFs. This keeps the database and server traffic paths segmented.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [AWS Direct Connect connection options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

A company must capture and log traffic for Nitro-based Amazon EC2 instances to meet regulatory requirements. The company's network team has prepared a solution that enables VPC traffic mirroring and directs traffic to a second group of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group.  
  
The network team has placed a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the EC2 instances that will receive the traffic. However, the solution does not deliver any mirrored traffic to the EC2 instances behind the NLB.  
  
How should the network team configure traffic mirroring to use the NLB endpoint?

options.text: Select the NLB as a source for traffic mirroring. Use a UDP listener.
Select the NLB as a target for traffic mirroring. Use a TCP listener and a UDP listener.
Select the NLB as a target for traffic mirroring. Use a TCP listener.
Select the NLB as a target for traffic mirroring. Use a UDP listener.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer used for VPC Traffic Mirroring must be configured as the traffic mirror target and must have a UDP listener. Mirrored traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated and sent using UDP port 4789, so TCP listeners do not receive this traffic.

**Learn more:** [Understand traffic mirror target concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-targets.html) · [How Traffic Mirroring works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) spanning multiple Availability Zones, with AWS Lambda functions as its ALB targets. The web application also uses Amazon CloudWatch metrics for monitoring.  
  
Users report that some parts of the web application are not loading correctly. A network engineer must troubleshoot the issue and enables access logging for the ALB.  
  
What should the network engineer do next to identify which errors the ALB is receiving?

options.text: Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Review the ALB logs in CloudWatch Insights to determine which error messages the ALB is receiving.
Configure the Amazon S3 bucket destination. Use Amazon Athena to determine which error messages the ALB is receiving.

Configure the Amazon S3 bucket destination. After Amazon CloudWatch Logs pulls the ALB logs from the S3 bucket automatically, review the logs in CloudWatch Logs to determine which error messages the ALB is receiving.
Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use the Amazon Athena CloudWatch Connector to determine which error messages the ALB is receiving.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer access logs are written as compressed files to a specified Amazon S3 bucket. Amazon Athena can query those S3-resident ALB log files using SQL, including request and error-related fields, to identify the errors received by the load balancer.

**Learn more:** [Access logs for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-access-logs.html) · [Query Application Load Balancer logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/application-load-balancer-logs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a workload in one VPC on AWS. Its architecture includes several interface VPC endpoints for AWS services, including Amazon CloudWatch Logs and AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). The endpoints are set up to use a shared security group. That security group is not used by any other workloads or resources.  
  
Following a security review of the environment, the company found that the shared security group is more permissive than required. The company needs to restrict the security group rules. The rule changes must not stop VPC resources from accessing AWS services through interface VPC endpoints, while preventing unnecessary access.  
  
The security group currently has these rules:  
  
- **Inbound – Rule 1**  
  - Protocol: TCP  
  - Port: 443  
  - Source: 0.0.0.0/0  
  
- **Inbound – Rule 2**  
  - Protocol: TCP  
  - Port: 443  
  - Source: VPC CIDR  
  
- **Outbound – Rule 1**  
  - Protocol: All  
  - Port: All  
  - Destination: 0.0.0.0/0  
  
Which rule or rules should the company remove to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Outbound - Rule 2
Inbound - Rule 1 and Outbound - Rule 1
Inbound - Rule 2 and Outbound - Rule 1
Outbound - Rule 1

questions.explanation:
An interface endpoint security group needs an inbound TCP 443 rule from the VPC resources that use the endpoint, which the VPC CIDR rule provides. The public inbound rule is not needed. Security groups are stateful, so return traffic for an allowed inbound HTTPS connection is permitted regardless of outbound rules; the unrestricted outbound rule can therefore be removed.

**Learn more:** [Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-interface-endpoint.html) · [Amazon EC2 security groups for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s VPC contains Amazon EC2 instances that communicate with AWS services through the public internet. The company must change this connectivity so the communication does not traverse the public internet.  
  
The company deploys AWS PrivateLink endpoints in the VPC. After deploying the PrivateLink endpoints, the EC2 instances can no longer communicate with the required AWS services.  
  
Which combination of steps should a network engineer take to restore communication with the AWS services? (Choose two.)

options.text: In the VPC route table, add a route that has the PrivateLink endpoints as the destination.
Ensure that the enableDnsSupport attribute is set to True for the VPC. Ensure that each VPC endpoint has DNS support enabled.
Ensure that the VPC endpoint policy allows communication.
Create an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for all services.
Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone that includes a custom name for each service.

questions.explanation:
Interface VPC endpoints rely on private DNS so standard AWS service DNS names resolve to the endpoints’ private IP addresses; this requires VPC DNS resolution support and private DNS enabled for the endpoint. Endpoint policies are resource-based policies that control which principals may use an endpoint to access an AWS service, so the policy must allow the required communication. Interface endpoints are reached through their private DNS records rather than by adding a route-table destination for the endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Configure an interface endpoint - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/interface-endpoints.html) · [Control access to VPC endpoints using endpoint policies - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-access.html)

A network engineer needs to develop an AWS CloudFormation template that creates a virtual private gateway, a customer gateway, a VPN connection, and static routes in a route table. During template testing, the network engineer observes that the CloudFormation template encounters an error and rolls back.  
  
What should the network engineer do to resolve the error?

options.text: Change the order of resource creation in the CloudFormation template.
Add the DependsOn attribute to the resource declaration for the virtual private gateway. Specify the route table entry resource.
Add a wait condition in the template to wait for the creation of the virtual private gateway.
Add the DependsOn attribute to the resource declaration for the route table entry. Specify the virtual private gateway resource.

questions.explanation:
A static route that uses a virtual private gateway must be created only after the virtual private gateway is provisioned. The route-table entry is the dependent resource, so it must use `DependsOn` to reference the virtual private gateway. `DependsOn` explicitly controls CloudFormation resource-creation order.

**Learn more:** [DependsOn attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-dependson.html) · [Get started with AWS Site-to-Site VPN - AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/SetUpVPNConnections.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates two on-premises data center locations. Each data center has a company-managed router. Each location has a dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to a Direct Connect gateway through a private virtual interface. The router at the first location advertises 110 routes to the Direct Connect gateway using BGP, and the router at the second location advertises 60 routes to the Direct Connect gateway using BGP. The Direct Connect gateway is attached to a company VPC by using a virtual private gateway.  
  
A network engineer receives reports that VPC resources cannot be reached from various locations in either data center. The engineer checks the VPC route table and finds that the routes from the first data center location are not populating the route table. The engineer must resolve the issue in the most operationally efficient way.  
  
What should the network engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Remove the Direct Connect gateway, and create a new private virtual interface from each company router to the virtual private gateway of the VPC.
Change the router configurations to summarize the advertised routes.
Open a support ticket to increase the quota on advertised routes to the VPC route table.
Create an AWS Transit Gateway. Attach the transit gateway to the VPC, and connect the Direct Connect gateway to the transit gateway.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect private virtual interfaces support a maximum of 100 advertised routes per IPv4 or IPv6 BGP session; advertising more can cause the BGP session to go idle. Also, a VPC route table can contain at most 100 propagated routes, and that quota cannot be increased. Summarizing the on-premises prefixes reduces the advertisements to within these limits while retaining the existing Direct Connect design.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect quotas - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/limits.html) · [Troubleshoot routing issues - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/ts-routing.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has 30 VPCs in total. Three AWS Regions contain 10 VPCs each. The company has attached the VPCs in every Region to a transit gateway in that Region. It has also configured inter-Region peering connections between the transit gateways.  
  
The company wants to use AWS Direct Connect to provide access from its on-premises location to only four VPCs across the three Regions. The company has provisioned four Direct Connect connections at two Direct Connect locations.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create four virtual private gateways. Attach the virtual private gateways to the four VPCs.
Create a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the four virtual private gateways with the Direct Connect gateway.
Create four transit VIFs on each Direct Connect connection. Associate the transit VIFs with the Direct Connect gateway.
Create four transit VIFs on each Direct Connect connection. Associate the transit VIFs with the four virtual private gateways.
Create four private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway.
Create an association between the Direct Connect gateway and the transit gateways.

questions.explanation:
Virtual private gateways attached only to the four required VPCs limit Direct Connect reachability to those VPCs. A Direct Connect gateway is a global resource that can associate with virtual private gateways in multiple Regions, and private virtual interfaces connect the Direct Connect connections to that gateway. Associating the Direct Connect gateway with the existing transit gateways would instead provide a path to all VPCs attached to those transit gateways.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro.html) · [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A real estate company is developing an internal application that lets real estate agents upload photos and videos of different properties. The application will store the photos and videos as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket and will store related metadata in Amazon DynamoDB. The S3 bucket will be configured to publish every PUT event for new object uploads to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.  
  
A compute cluster of Amazon EC2 instances will poll the SQS queue to learn about newly uploaded objects. The cluster will retrieve the new objects, perform proprietary image and video recognition and classification, update metadata in DynamoDB, and replace the objects with new watermarked objects. The company does not want the EC2 instances to have public IP addresses.  
  
Which networking design solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way as application usage grows?

options.text: Place the EC2 instances in a public subnet. Disable the Auto-assign Public IP option while launching the EC2 instances. Create an internet gateway. Attach the internet gateway to the VPC. In the public subnet's route table, add a default route that points to the internet gateway.

Place the EC2 instances in a private subnet. Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet in the same Availability Zone. Create an internet gateway. Attach the internet gateway to the VPC. In the public subnet's route table, add a default route that points to the internet gateway
Place the EC2 instances in a private subnet. Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Create gateway VPC endpoints for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.
Place the EC2 instances in a private subnet. Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon SQS. Create interface VPC endpoints for Amazon S3 and DynamoDB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS requires an interface VPC endpoint for private connectivity from resources in a VPC. Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB support gateway VPC endpoints, which provide private connectivity without an internet gateway or NAT device and have no additional charge. Using an interface endpoint for SQS plus gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB keeps the EC2 instances private while avoiding NAT gateway costs and unnecessary billed interface endpoints as usage increases.

**Learn more:** [Internetwork traffic privacy in Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-internetwork-traffic-privacy.html) · [Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

A company is moving an existing application to a new AWS account. It will deploy the application in one AWS Region, using a single VPC and multiple Availability Zones. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances, with several EC2 instances in each Availability Zone. The EC2 instances will reside in private subnets.  
  
The company's clients will access the application in a web browser by using HTTPS. Incoming connections must be distributed across the Availability Zones and EC2 instances. Every connection in the same client session must reach the same EC2 instance. The company must supply end-to-end encryption for every connection between clients and the application by using the application SSL certificate.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer. Create a target group. Set the protocol to TCP and the port to 443 for the target group. Turn on session affinity (sticky sessions). Create an Application Load Balancer. Create a target group. Set the protocol to HTTP and the port to 80 for the target group. Turn on session affinity (sticky sessions) with an application-based cookie policy. Register the EC2 instances as targets. Create an HTTPS listener. Set the default action to forward to the target group. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate for the listener.

Create a Network Load Balancer. Create a target group. Set the protocol to TLS and the port to 443 for the target group. Turn on session affinity (sticky sessions). Register the EC2 instances as targets. Create a listener. Set the protocol to TLS and the port to 443 for the listener. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a certificate for the application.

Create an Application Load Balancer. Create a target group. Set the protocol to HTTPS and the port to 443 for the target group. Turn on session affinity (sticky sessions) with an application-based cookie policy. Register the EC2 instances as targets. Create an HTTP listener. Set the port to 443 for the listener. Set the default action to forward to the target group.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer configured with TCP on port 443 is a TLS pass-through load balancer: it forwards encrypted traffic to the EC2 instances without decrypting it. Installing the application SSL certificate on each instance therefore provides encryption from the client through to the application. A Network Load Balancer TCP target group can use source-IP stickiness to route a client's subsequent connections to the same target while distributing traffic across healthy targets in enabled Availability Zones.

In `us-east-1`, the AWS account has an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a Resolver rule.  
  
As part of an expansion, the company creates another AWS account for a new business unit that operates in `us-east-1`. The new account has VPCs attached to the transit gateway and uses the existing Direct Connect connection to connect to the on-premises location. Applications running in the new account’s VPCs must also access the on-premises location by using the `corp.example.com` DNS name.  
  
A network engineer must identify a solution to resolve the `corp.example.com` DNS name from the new account.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create a hosted transit VIF for the new account on the existing Direct Connect connection. In the new account, create a new Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Also in the new account, create a new Resolver rule that specifies FORWARD as the value for RuleType. Associate the new rule with the VPCs in the new account.
Share the Resolver rule from the existing account with the new account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Associate the shared rule with the VPCs in the new account.

Share the Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint from the existing account with the new account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). In the new account, create a new Resolver rule that specifies FORWARD as the value for RuleType. Associate the new rule with the VPCs in the new account.

questions.explanation:

A shared forwarding rule continues to use its configured outbound Resolver endpoint, so one endpoint and centrally managed rule can serve VPCs in multiple accounts in the same Region without creating another outbound endpoint or connection.

options.text: Create an accelerator in Account-В. Use a cross-account role from Account-A to grant the networking team access to manage the accelerator.

questions.explanation:

Which additional CIDR block can the network engineer associate with the VPC?
questions.explanation:
For a VPC with an existing CIDR in the `172.16.0.0/12` private range, AWS permits an additional CIDR from that same range, provided its prefix length is from `/16` through `/28` and it is not otherwise restricted. `172.17.0.0/16` meets these requirements. AWS restricts associating CIDRs from the other RFC 1918 ranges (`10.0.0.0/8` and `192.168.0.0/16`) in this case.\

A company uses Amazon Route 53 for its DNS requirements. The company’s security team wants to update the DNS infrastructure to deliver the latest security posture.  
  
The security team has configured DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) for the domain. The team wants a network engineer to explain who is responsible for rotating DNSSEC keys.  
  
Which explanation should the network administrator give to the security team?

options.text: AWS rotates the zone-signing key (ZSK). The company rotates the key-signing key (KSK).
The company rotates the zone-signing key (ZSK) and the key-signing key (KSK).
AWS rotates the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key and the key-signing key (KSK).
The company rotates the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. AWS rotates the key-signing key (KSK).

questions.explanation:
For Route 53 DNSSEC signing, Route 53 performs ZSK management and rotation. Each KSK is based on a customer-owned, customer-managed asymmetric AWS KMS key; the customer is responsible for KSK management, including rotation when needed.

**Learn more:** [Configuring DNSSEC signing in Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec.html) · [KMS key and ZSK management in Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec-zsk-management.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses custom DNS servers running BIND for name resolution in its VPCs. The VPCs are deployed across multiple AWS accounts that belong to the same AWS Organizations organization. All VPCs are connected to a transit gateway. The BIND servers run in a central VPC and are configured to forward every query for an on-premises DNS domain to DNS servers hosted in an on-premises data center. To make sure that every VPC uses the custom DNS servers, a network engineer has configured a VPC DHCP options set in every VPC that specifies the custom DNS servers as the domain name servers.  
  
Multiple development teams in the company want to use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). A development team created a new EFS file system but cannot mount it to one of its Amazon EC2 instances. The network engineer finds that the EC2 instance cannot resolve the IP address for the EFS mount point `fs-33444567d.efs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com`. The network engineer must implement a solution so development teams throughout the organization can mount EFS file systems.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the BIND DNS servers in the central VPC to forward queries for efs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com to the Amazon provided DNS server (169.254.169.253).
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint in the central VPC. Update all the VPC DHCP options sets to use AmazonProvidedDNS for name resolution.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the central VPUpdate all the VPC DHCP options sets to use the Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the central VPC for name resolution.

Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver rule to forward queries for the on-premises domain to the on-premises DNS servers. Share the rule with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Associate the rule with all the VPCs.

Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the efs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com domain. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC where the EC2 instance is deployed. Create an A record for fs-33444567d.efs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com in the private hosted zone. Configure the A record to return the mount target of the EFS mount point.

questions.explanation:
AmazonProvidedDNS uses the Route 53 Resolver built into each VPC, which resolves AWS-provided private DNS names, including EFS mount-point names. A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule for the on-premises domain preserve hybrid DNS resolution by forwarding only matching on-premises queries to the on-premises DNS servers. Sharing that rule through AWS RAM and associating it with the VPCs lets multiple accounts use the central outbound endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Amazon DNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/AmazonDNS-concepts.html) · [Forwarding outbound DNS queries to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-outbound-queries.html)

A consulting company manages AWS accounts for its customers. One customer needs to add intrusion prevention to its environment without re-architecting that environment. The customer’s environment includes five VPCs across two AWS Regions in the United States. VPC-to-VPC connectivity is provided through VPC peering. The customer does not intend to increase the number of VPCs during the next 2 years. The solution must support unencrypted traffic.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure VPC security groups and network ACLs.
Use an AWS Network Firewall centralized deployment model in each VPC.
Use an AWS Network Firewall distributed deployment model in each VPC.
Deploy AWS Shield in each VPC.

questions.explanation:
A distributed AWS Network Firewall deployment places firewall endpoints in every protected VPC, enabling stateful traffic inspection and intrusion-prevention rules close to the workloads while retaining the existing VPC structure. A centralized Network Firewall model uses a centralized inspection VPC and AWS Transit Gateway, so it would require a connectivity redesign from the existing VPC-peering architecture.

**Learn more:** [Deployment models for AWS Network Firewall](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/deployment-models-for-aws-network-firewall/) · [AWS Network Firewall FAQs](https://aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/faqs/)
