A network engineer deployed an Amazon EC2 instance into a private subnet in a VPC. The VPC contains no public subnet. The EC2 instance runs application code that sends messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The subnet uses the default network ACL without modifications. The EC2 instance uses the default security group without modifications.  
  
The SQS queue is not receiving messages.  
  
Which of the following could cause this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: The EC2 instance is not attached to an IAM role that allows write operations to Amazon SQS.
The security group is blocking traffic to the IP address range used by Amazon SQS
There is no interface VPC endpoint configured for Amazon SQS
The network ACL is blocking return traffic from Amazon SQS
There is no route configured in the subnet route table for the IP address range used by Amazon SQS

questions.explanation:
An SQS producer must be authorized to perform `sqs:SendMessage`; lacking an IAM role with the required write permission can deny the send operation. An Amazon SQS interface VPC endpoint provides private connectivity from a VPC to SQS without requiring an internet gateway or NAT device, so without public egress, the absence of that endpoint can prevent connectivity. The default network ACL allows inbound and outbound traffic, and the default security group allows outbound traffic.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS API permissions reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-api-permissions-reference.html) · [Tutorial: Sending a message to an Amazon SQS queue from Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-sending-messages-from-vpc.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer is planning hybrid connectivity using AWS Direct Connect and AWS Transit Gateway. A transit gateway is associated with a Direct Connect gateway and with 19 VPCs in different AWS accounts. Two additional VPCs are being associated with the transit gateway. The IP address administrator assigned `10.0.32.0/21` to the first VPC and `10.0.40.0/21` to the second VPC. The prefix list has capacity for only one more CIDR block before it reaches its maximum-entry quota.  
  
What should the network engineer do to advertise the routes from AWS to the on-premises environment while meeting these requirements?

options.text: Add 10.0.32.0/21 and 10.0.40.0/21 to both AWS managed prefix lists.
Add 10.0.32.0/21 and 10.0.40.0/21 to the allowed prefix list.
Add 10.0.32.0/20 to both AWS managed prefix lists.
Add 10.0.32.0/20 to the allowed prefix list.

questions.explanation:
For a transit gateway association, the Direct Connect gateway advertises only the prefixes in its allowed prefix list to the on-premises network. `10.0.32.0/20` is a valid aggregate that encompasses both `10.0.32.0/21` and `10.0.40.0/21`, so it advertises reachability for both VPCs while using one remaining entry.

**Learn more:** [Allowed prefixes interactions for Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/allowed-to-prefixes.html) · [Associate or disassociate Direct Connect with a Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/associate-tgw-with-direct-connect-gateway.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a software solution on Amazon EC2 instances in a cluster placement group. The solution’s UI consists of one HTML page. The HTML file is 1,024 bytes in size. The software processes files larger than 1,024 MB. When requested, it shares files with clients over the network. The files are shared with the Don't Fragment flag enabled. The EC2 instances’ elastic network interfaces are configured for jumbo frames.  
  
The UI is consistently reachable from every permitted source IP address, whether those addresses are in a VPC, on the internet, or on premises. However, clients occasionally do not receive requested files because the files fail to travel successfully from the software to the clients.  
  
Which options could be a root cause of these failures? (Choose two.)

options.text: The source IP addresses are from on-premises hosts that are routed over AWS Direct Connect.
The source IP addresses are from on-premises hosts that are routed over AWS Site-to-Site VPN.
The source IP addresses are from hosts that connect over the public internet.
The security group of the EC2 instances does not allow ICMP traffic.
The operating system of the EC2 instances does not support jumbo frames.

questions.explanation:
Traffic through an internet gateway and traffic over VPN connections have a 1,500-byte MTU limit. Jumbo-frame packets that exceed that limit cannot be fragmented when the Don't Fragment flag is set, so they are dropped. AWS Site-to-Site VPN does not support jumbo frames, while Direct Connect can support them when its virtual interface is configured accordingly.

**Learn more:** [Network maximum transmission unit (MTU) for your EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/network_mtu.html) · [AWS Site-to-Site VPN quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer is designing the architecture for a healthcare company’s workload that is being migrated to the AWS Cloud. All data traveling to and from the on-premises environment must be encrypted in transit. All traffic must also be inspected in the cloud before it is permitted to leave the cloud for the on-premises environment or the internet.  
  
The company will expose workload components to the internet so patients can reserve appointments. The architecture must secure these components and protect them from DDoS attacks. It must also protect against financial liability for services that scale out during a DDoS event.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to satisfy all these workload requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use Traffic Mirroring to copy all traffic to a fleet of traffic capture appliances.
Set up AWS WAF on all network components.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to create Deny rules in security groups to block malicious IP addresses.
Use AWS Direct Connect with MACsec support for connectivity to the cloud.
Use Gateway Load Balancers to insert third-party firewalls for inline traffic inspection.
Configure AWS Shield Advanced and ensure that it is configured on all public assets.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect with MACsec provides Layer 2 encryption between the customer edge device and the Direct Connect device. Gateway Load Balancer enables third-party firewall appliances to inspect traffic inline, including traffic between workload VPCs, on-premises networks, and the internet. AWS Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection for supported public assets and offers cost-protection opportunities for DDoS-related usage spikes.

**Learn more:** [Encryption in AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/encryption-in-transit.html) · [Implementing inline traffic inspection using third-party security appliances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/inline-traffic-inspection-third-party-appliances/welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates across multiple AWS Regions and has deployed transit gateways in every Region. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts within one organization.  
  
The company must capture all VPC flow log data whenever a new VPC is created and must send the flow logs to a specified Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative effort?

options.text: Update IAM permissions for each user to include a condition that ensures users can create VPCs only when VPC Flow Logs is enabled and configured correctly.
Create a custom AWS Config rule with automatic remediation that verifies VPC Flow Logs is enabled and configured correctly. Apply the AWS Config rule to the organization.
Enable VPC Flow Logs on each transit gateway. Configure VPC Flow Logs to send flow logs to the specified S3 bucket.
Deploy a serverless application that uses AWS CloudTrail to monitor for VPC creation events in each account. Configure the application to apply the correct VPC Flow Logs configuration.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Config rule with automatic remediation can detect a VPC that lacks the required flow-log configuration and automatically configure flow logs to publish to the designated Amazon S3 bucket. Applying the control across the organization provides centralized, scalable enforcement for member accounts and avoids maintaining per-user IAM restrictions or deploying and operating custom event-processing applications in every account. AWS guidance for cross-account VPC flow-log centralization identifies an AWS Config rule with remediation as an automation option.

**Learn more:** [Configure VPC Flow Logs for centralization across AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/configure-vpc-flow-logs-for-centralization-across-aws-accounts.html) · [Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/setup-autoremediation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Fargate to deploy many containerized web applications into a VPC. Every application must be accessible through different DNS names on the standard HTTPS port. The company uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to manage traffic to each application.  
  
The company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to automate deployment. It uses two types of CDK stacks: one common stack to create the VPC and other shared infrastructure, and a collection of application-specific stacks containing the details and logic for each application.  
  
The company needs to allocate ALB-related resources correctly between these two stack types.  
  
Which combination of solutions provides a repeatable allocation of resources to the common stack and application-specific stacks? (Choose three.)

options.text: ALB listener in the common stack
ALB listener in the application-specific stacks
ALB listener host header rule in the common stack
ALB listener host header rule in the application-specific stacks
ALB target group in the common stack
ALB target group in the application-specific stacks

questions.explanation:
An ALB listener accepts client connections on a configured protocol and port, so one shared HTTPS listener on port 443 is common infrastructure. Host-header listener rules route requests by DNS host name and forward matching traffic to a target group. Because the hostname, routing rule, and Fargate task targets belong to each individual application, each application-specific stack should define its own host-header rule and target group.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [Condition types for listener rules](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-condition-types.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed an AWS Network Firewall firewall in a VPC. A network engineer must implement a solution to deliver Network Firewall flow logs to the company’s Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster in the least possible time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to load logs into the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster. Enable Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notifications on the S3 bucket to invoke the Lambda function. Configure flow logs for the firewall. Set the S3 bucket as the destination.

Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that includes the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster as the destination. Configure flow logs for the firewall Set the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream as the destination for the Network Firewall flow logs.
Configure flow logs for the firewall. Set the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster as the destination for the Network Firewall flow logs.

Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream that includes the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster as the destination. Configure flow logs for the firewall. Set the Kinesis data stream as the destination for the Network Firewall flow logs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall can deliver flow logs to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Firehose supports Amazon OpenSearch Service as a delivery destination, so configuring a Firehose stream for the OpenSearch cluster and selecting that stream as the firewall log destination is the supported direct solution. Network Firewall does not support Amazon OpenSearch Service or Kinesis Data Streams as direct log destinations.

**Learn more:** [Sending AWS Network Firewall logs to Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/logging-kinesis.html) · [AWS Network Firewall logging destinations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-logging-destinations.html)

options.text: Decrease the BGP hello timer to 5 seconds.
Add a VPN connection to the connectivity solution. Implement fast failover.
Configure Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on the on-premises router.
Decrease the BGP hold-down timer to 5 seconds.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect uses a default BGP hold timer of 90 seconds, which accounts for the observed interruption. Configuring Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on the on-premises router activates BFD for the Direct Connect virtual interface and provides much faster liveness detection; AWS supports a minimum BFD interval of 300 ms with a minimum multiplier of 3.

**Learn more:** [BGP-specific settings - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/bgp-specific-settings.html) · [Direct Connect connection options - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

A company operates a data center in the us-west-1 Region with a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Two private VIFs from the same data center location in us-west-1 are attached to that same Direct Connect gateway.  
  
VIF 1 advertises `172.16.0.0/16` with an AS_PATH attribute value of `65000`. VIF 2 advertises `172.16.1.0/24` with an AS PATH attribute value of `65000 65000 65000`.  
  
How will AWS route traffic to the data center when the destination address is within the `172.16.1.0/24` network range?

options.text: AWS will route all traffic by using VIF 1.
AWS will route all traffic by using VIF 2.
AWS will use both VIFs for routing by using a round-robin policy.
AWS will use flow control to balance the traffic between the two VIFs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect private VIF routing evaluates the longest prefix match before AS_PATH length. The `172.16.1.0/24` advertisement is more specific than `172.16.0.0/16`, so traffic destined for that /24 range is routed through VIF 2.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html) · [Direct Connect private virtual interface routing example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/private-transit-vif-example.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution configured with an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as its origin. A network engineer must implement a solution that ensures all inbound traffic to the ALB originates from CloudFront. The network engineer must implement the solution at the network layer, rather than at the application layer.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Add an inbound rule to the ALB's security group to allow the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront.
Add an inbound rule to the network ACLs that are associated with the ALB's subnets. Use the AWS managed prefix list for CloudFront as the source in the rule.
Configure CloudFront to add a custom HTTP header to the requests that CloudFront sends to the ALB.
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALB. Configure the AWS WAF rules to allow traffic from the CloudFront IP set. Automatically update the CloudFront IP set by using an AWS Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
An ALB security group can allow inbound traffic from the AWS-managed CloudFront origin-facing prefix list, preventing non-CloudFront traffic from reaching the ALB at Layer 3 or Layer 4. AWS maintains this prefix list as CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges change, avoiding manual IP-set updates. [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html)

**Learn more:** [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html) · [Use the CloudFront managed prefix list](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/LocationsOfEdgeServers.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has VPCs in 50 AWS accounts and uses AWS Organizations. The company wants to implement web filtering, with identical traffic-filtering requirements for every VPC. A network engineer plans to use AWS Network Firewall and must implement a solution that minimizes the number of firewall policies and rule groups required for this web filtering.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a firewall policy or rule group in each account.
Use SCPs to share the firewall policy or rule group.
Create a firewall policy or rule group in the management account
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the firewall policy or rule group.
Enable sharing within Organizations.
Create OUs to share the firewall policy or rule group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall firewall policies and rule groups can be created centrally and shared with other AWS accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Sharing them with accounts in AWS Organizations requires enabling sharing within Organizations. This permits the same policy or rule groups to be reused across all accounts, rather than creating duplicates per account.

**Learn more:** [Sharing AWS Network Firewall resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/sharing.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company registers a public domain, `example.com`, in an AWS account by using Amazon Route 53. A central services group administers that account. The company wants to create the `test.example.com` subdomain in a different AWS account to provide name services for Amazon EC2 instances hosted in that account. The company does not want to move the parent domain to the subdomain account.  
  
A network engineer creates a new Route 53 hosted zone for the subdomain in the second account.  
  
Which combination of actions must the network engineer take to finish the task? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add records for the hosts of the new subdomain to the new Route 53 hosted zone.
Update the DNS service for the parent domain by adding name server (NS) records for the subdomain.
Update the DNS service for the subdomain by adding name server (NS) records for the parent domain.
Create an alias record from the parent domain that points to the hosted zone for the subdomain in the second account.
Add a start of authority (SOA) record in the parent domain for the subdomain.

questions.explanation:
A delegated subdomain requires its resource records to be created in the subdomain’s hosted zone and an NS delegation record for that subdomain to be created in the parent domain’s hosted zone. The parent NS record directs resolvers to the authoritative name servers assigned to the `test.example.com` hosted zone.

**Learn more:** [Routing traffic for subdomains - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-routing-traffic-for-subdomains.html) · [Creating a subdomain that uses Amazon Route 53 as the DNS service without migrating the parent domain](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/CreatingNewSubdomain.html)

",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Decrease the BGP hello timer to 5 seconds.","B":"Add a VPN connection to the connectivity solution. A company recently adopted a security policy that prevents developers from launching VPC network infrastructure. The policy requires the company's network security team to receive an immediate alert and terminate any NAT gateway launched in a VPC. The network security team must implement a solution that can be deployed across AWS accounts with the least possible administrative overhead. The solution must also give the network security team a simple way to view compliance history.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Develop a script that programmatically checks for NAT gateways in an AWS account, sends an email alert, and terminates the NAT gateway if a NAT gateway is detected. Deploy the script on an Amazon EC2 instance in each account. Use a cron job to run the script every 5 minutes. Log the results of the checks to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database.

Create an AWS Lambda function that programmatically checks for NAT gateways in an AWS account, sends an email alert, and terminates the NAT gateway if a NAT gateway is detected. Deploy the Lambda function to each account by using AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) templates. Store the results of the checks on an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster in each account.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the Behavior:EC2/NATGatewayCreation GuardDuty finding type. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Step Functions state machine to send an email alert and terminate a NAT gateway if a NAT gateway is detected. Store the runtime log as a text file in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Create a custom AWS Config rule that checks for NAT gateways in an AWS account. Configure the AWS Config rule to perform an AWS Systems Manager Automation remediation action to send an email alert and terminate the NAT gateway if a NAT gateway is detected. Deploy the AWS Config rule and the Systems Manager runbooks to each account by using AWS CloudFormation StackSets

questions.explanation:
AWS Config custom rules evaluate resources for compliance and retain compliance-state changes in a timeline. AWS Config remediation can invoke AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to alert and terminate a noncompliant NAT gateway. CloudFormation StackSets deploy the same resources across multiple AWS accounts from one template and operation, reducing administration.

**Learn more:** [Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/remediation.html) · [Viewing Compliance History for AWS Resources with AWS Config](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/view-manage-resource-console.html)

A company operates a highly available application across multiple VPCs and two on-premises data centers. All VPCs are in the same AWS Region. Every VPC needs connectivity to every other VPC and to the on-premises data centers to transfer files that are multiple gigabytes in size.  
  
A network engineer is designing an AWS Direct Connect solution that connects the on-premises data centers to each VPC.  
  
Which architecture meets the company’s requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure a virtual private gateway and a private VIF in each VPC in the Region. Configure a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the VIF of every VPC with the Direct Connect gateway. Create a new private VIF that connects the Direct Connect gateway to each on-premises data center. Configure the new private VIF to exchange BGP routes with the on-premises data centers and to have an MTU of 9001. Use VPC peering between each VPC. Configure static routing in each VPC to provide inter-VPC routing.

Configure a virtual private gateway and a private VIF in each VPC in the Region. Configure a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the VIF of every VPC with the Direct Connect gateway. Create a new private VIF that connects the Direct Connect gateway to each on-premises data center. Configure the new private VIF to exchange BGP routes with the on-premises data centers and to have an MTU of 8500. Use VPC peering between each VPC. Configure static routing in each VPC to provide inter-VPC routing.

Configure a transit gateway in the same Region of each VPAttach each VPC to the transit gateway. Configure a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway. Associate a new transit VIF with each Direct Connect connection. Configure the new transit VIF to exchange BGP routes and to have an MTU of 9001. Configure route propagation between each VPC and the transit gateway.

Configure a transit gateway in the same Region of each VPC. Attach each VPC to the transit gateway. Configure a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway. Associate a new transit VIF with each Direct Connect connection. Configure the new transit VIF to exchange BGP routes and to have an MTU of 8500. Configure route propagation between each VPC and the transit gateway.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway centralizes and simplifies routing between multiple VPCs and on-premises networks, eliminating the operational burden of a full mesh of VPC peering connections and static inter-VPC routes. A Direct Connect gateway associates with the transit gateway, and Direct Connect connectivity is provided through transit virtual interfaces. A transit virtual interface supports jumbo frames with an MTU of 8500; 9001 is not a supported transit-VIF MTU.

**Learn more:** [Connect your VPC to other VPCs and networks using a transit gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/extend-tgw.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-vif.html)

An IoT company gathers data from thousands of sensors deployed in the United States and South Asia. The sensors use a proprietary UDP-based communication protocol to transmit data to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The instances, Auto Scaling group, and NLB are deployed in the `us-west-2` Region.  
  
Occasionally, sensor data from South Asia is lost while in transit across the internet and never reaches the EC2 instances.  
  
Which solutions will resolve this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use AWS Global Accelerator with the existing NLB.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Specify the existing NLB as the origin.
Create a second deployment of the EC2 instances and the NLB in the ap-south-1 Region. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to resolve to the Region that provides the least latency.
Create a second deployment of the EC2 instances and the NLB in the ap-south-1 Region. Use an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy to resolve to an alternate Region in case packets are dropped.
Turn on enhanced networking on the EC2 instances by using the most recent Elastic Network Adapter (ENA) drivers.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator can use a Network Load Balancer as an endpoint and accepts traffic at nearby AWS edge locations, carrying it over the AWS global network to reduce the unreliable public-internet portion of the path. Deploying the workload and NLB in `ap-south-1` and using Route 53 latency-based routing directs sensors to the AWS Region with the lowest latency. CloudFront only proxies HTTP/HTTPS traffic to custom origins, while a Route 53 failover policy addresses unhealthy endpoints rather than packet loss on a healthy route; EC2 enhanced networking does not improve the preceding internet path.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html)

The company uses AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the transit gateway, allowing users in other accounts to connect to multiple VPCs in the same AWS Region. AWS Account B has a VPC (`10.0.0.0/16`) with subnet `10.0.0.0/24` in the `us-west-2a` Availability Zone and subnet `10.0.1.0/24` in the `us-west-2b` Availability Zone. Resources in these subnets can communicate with other VPCs.  
  
A network engineer creates two additional subnets: `10.0.2.0/24` in the `us-west-2b` Availability Zone and `10.0.3.0/24` in the `us-west-2c` Availability Zone. All subnets use one route table. The default route, `0.0.0.0/0`, points to the transit gateway. Resources in subnet `10.0.2.0/24` can communicate with other VPCs, but resources in subnet `10.0.3.0/24` cannot communicate with other VPCs.  
  
What should the network engineer do so that resources in subnet `10.0.3.0/24` can communicate with other VPCs?

options.text: In Account B, add 10.0.2.0/24 and 10.0.3.0/24 as the destinations to the route table. Use the transit gateway as the target.
In Account B, update the transit gateway attachment. Attach the new subnet ID that is associated with us-west-2c to Account B's VPC.
In Account A, create a static route for 10.0.3.0/24 in the transit gateway route tables.
In Account A, recreate propagation for 10.0.0.0/16 in the transit gateway route tables.

questions.explanation:
For a VPC attachment, AWS Transit Gateway requires an attachment subnet in every Availability Zone from which resources must reach the transit gateway. The existing attachment covers `us-west-2a` and `us-west-2b`, but not `us-west-2c`; adding the `us-west-2c` subnet to the attachment enables resources in that Availability Zone to use the existing route to the transit gateway.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)

The company must implement a load-balancing solution that receives HTTPS traffic from thousands of external users. The solution must distribute traffic across the web servers in AWS and those in the on-premises data center. No matter where a web server is located, HTTPS requests must be sent to the same web server for the entire session.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the production VPC. Create a target group. Specify ip as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target group Enable connection draining on the NLB

Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the production VPC. Create a target group Specify ip as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target group. Enable application-based session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the production VPCreate a target group. Specify instance as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target group. Enable session affinity (sticky sessions) on the NLB.

Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the production VPC. Create a target group. Specify instance as the target type Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target group Enable application-based session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer supports IP target groups, which can register on-premises resources connected through AWS Direct Connect as well as EC2 targets by private IP address. Application-based stickiness binds a user's session to one target, ensuring that its requests continue to reach the same web server. Instance target groups accept instance IDs and therefore cannot include on-premises servers.

A company is at an early stage of adopting the AWS Cloud. It has an application running in an on-premises data center in Asia and must deploy new applications in the `us-east-1` Region. The cloud applications require connectivity to the on-premises data center.  
  
The company must establish a communication channel between AWS and the data center. The solution must improve latency, reduce the risk of performance effects from transcontinental routing across the public internet, and encrypt data in transit.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with acceleration turned on. Create a virtual private gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN connection to the virtual private gateway. Attach the virtual private gateway to the VPC where the applications will be deployed.

Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with acceleration turned on. Create a transit gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. Create a transit gateway attachment to the VPC where the applications will be deployed.

Create an AWS Direct Connect connection. Create a virtual private gateway. Create a public VIF and a private VIF that use the virtual private gateway. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the public VIF.

Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with acceleration turned off. Create a transit gateway. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. Create a transit gateway attachment to the VPC where the applications will be deployed.

questions.explanation:
An accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses AWS Global Accelerator to bring traffic onto the congestion-free AWS global network close to the customer gateway, optimizing the path and helping avoid public-internet disruptions. Site-to-Site VPN provides IPsec encryption in transit and can be deployed faster than a Direct Connect connection. VPN acceleration is supported only for Site-to-Site VPN connections attached to a transit gateway; virtual private gateways do not support it.

**Learn more:** [Accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/accelerated-vpn.html) · [Time to deploy – Hybrid Connectivity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/hybrid-connectivity/time-to-deploy.html)

A company must connect its on-premises network to a VPC in the `us-east-1` Region. The connection must support a maximum transmission unit (MTU) of 9,000 bytes and must provide high availability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner?

options.text: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to create two VPNs. Use two connections to two virtual private gateways that are in the same VPC.
Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to create two VPNs. Use two connections to a single transit gateway that has a VPC attachment.
Create a multi-site, nonredundant AWS Direct Connect deployment. Use two Direct Connect connections to two separate Direct Connect locations.
Create a multi-site, redundant AWS Direct Connect deployment. Use two Direct Connect connections to one Direct Connect location and two connections to a second Direct Connect location.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect private virtual interfaces support jumbo frames with an MTU of 9,001 bytes. Two single Direct Connect connections at separate Direct Connect locations provide high resiliency against connection, device, and location failures, while requiring fewer connections than a maximum-resiliency four-connection design.

**Learn more:** [Resilience in AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html)

The company must be notified whenever a new route is advertised to AWS from on premises over Direct Connect.  
  
What should a network engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Enable Amazon CloudWatch metrics on Direct Connect to track the received routes. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to send notifications when routes change.
Onboard Transit Gateway Network Manager to Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) to send notifications when routes change.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to periodically check the routes on the Direct Connect gateway and to send notifications when routes change.
Enable Amazon CloudWatch Logs on the transit VIFs to track the received routes. Create a metric filter Set an alarm on the filter to send notifications when routes change.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Manager for Transit Gateways emits routing update events when a route is installed or uninstalled in a transit gateway route table. After the global network is onboarded to CloudWatch Logs Insights, Amazon EventBridge rules can match these events and send notifications. Routes learned through the Direct Connect transit VIF are propagated to the transit gateway route table, so this provides notification when newly advertised on-premises routes appear.

The network engineer configures Amazon CloudWatch Internet Monitor for the application. The engineer needs to send the internet health events to a third-party target.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** implementation effort?

options.text: Create a third-party API endpoint in Amazon EventBridge. Configure internet Monitor to send the events to the third-party API endpoint in EventBridge.
Create a third-party API endpoint in Amazon EventBridge. Create a rule in EventBridge that uses Internet Monitor as the source and the third-party API endpoint in EventBridge as the destination.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch Internet Monitor publishes health events directly to Amazon EventBridge with the event source `aws.internetmonitor`. An EventBridge rule can match that source and deliver the matching events to an EventBridge API destination, which invokes a third-party HTTPS endpoint. This provides the required forwarding without intermediate storage or custom code.

An Australian ecommerce company runs all its services in the AWS Cloud and wants to expand its customer base into the United States (US). The company is targeting the western US for this expansion.  
  
The company’s current AWS architecture includes four AWS accounts with multiple VPCs deployed in the `ap-southeast-2` Region. Every VPC is attached to a transit gateway in `ap-southeast-2`. There are dedicated VPCs for each application service, along with VPCs for centralized security capabilities such as proxies, firewalls, and logging.  
  
The company plans to replicate the infrastructure from `ap-southeast-2` in the `us-west-1` Region. A network engineer must establish connectivity between the various applications across the two Regions. The solution must maximize bandwidth, minimize latency, and minimize operational overhead.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create VPN attachments between the two transit gateways. Configure the VPN attachments to use BGP routing between the two transit gateways.
Peer the transit gateways in each Region. Configure routing between the two transit gateways for each Region's IP addresses.
Create a VPN server in a VPC in each Region. Update the routing to point to the VPN servers for the IP addresses in alternate Regions.
Attach the VPCs in us-west-1 to the transit gateway in ap-southeast-2.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway inter-Region peering directly connects transit gateways in different Regions through the AWS Global Infrastructure. Static routes in each transit gateway route table direct the remote Region’s CIDR ranges through the peering attachment. This preserves the regional hub-and-spoke design, avoids VPN tunnel management and its lower MTU characteristics, and provides high-bandwidth private connectivity between the two multi-VPC environments.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateway peering attachments in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-peering.html) · [What is AWS Transit Gateway for Amazon VPC?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company intends to run a computationally intensive data-processing application on AWS. The data is highly sensitive. The VPC must not have direct internet access, and the company has implemented strict network security to control access.  
  
Data scientists will transfer data from the company's on-premises data center to the instances through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The on-premises data center uses the network range `172.31.0.0/20`, and the application VPC will use the network range `172.31.16.0/20`.  
  
The data scientists report that they can launch new application instances but cannot transfer data from the on-premises data center. A network engineer enables VPC flow logs and sends a ping to an instance to test reachability. The flow logs show the following:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783842542302-jingdau4.png)  
  
The network engineer must recommend a solution that enables the data scientists to transfer data from the on-premises data center.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Modify the security group for the application. Add an inbound rule to allow traffic from the on-premises data center network range to the application.
Modify the network ACLs for the VPC subnet. Add an inbound rule to allow traffic from the on-premises data center network range to the VPC subnet range.
Modify the network ACLs for the VPC subnet. Add an outbound rule to allow traffic from the VPC subnet range to the on-premises data center network range.
Modify the security group for the application. Add an outbound rule to allow traffic from the application to the on-premises data center network range.

questions.explanation:
Network ACLs are stateless and evaluate inbound and outbound traffic separately. The inbound ICMP request from `172.31.8.29` to `172.31.18.139` is allowed, but the response in the reverse direction is rejected. Adding an outbound network ACL rule that allows traffic from the VPC subnet range to the on-premises `172.31.0.0/20` range permits the return traffic needed for connectivity and data transfers. AWS documents this exact pattern: an NACL that permits inbound ICMP but not outbound ICMP produces an accepted request and rejected response in VPC Flow Logs.

Which combination of steps will satisfy this requirement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create new Direct Connect connections while requesting MACsec ports.
Create a MACsec Connectivity Association Key Name (CKN) and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) pair. Associate the pair with each new connection.
Update the on-premises routers to use MACsec and the shared Connectivity Association Key Name (CKN) and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) pair.
Create a shared key for an IPsec connection.
Configure a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate the shared key with the new Direct Connect gateway.
Set up IPsec on the on-premises router. Associate the shared key with the IPsec configuration.

questions.explanation:
MACsec provides Layer 2 confidentiality, integrity, and origin authentication for a dedicated Direct Connect connection. It must be enabled on the dedicated connection, the CKN/CAK pair must be associated with that connection, and the on-premises MACsec-capable router must use the same key pair. AWS Direct Connect documentation specifies these as the setup steps for MACsec on dedicated connections.

**Learn more:** [Get started using MACsec on a dedicated Direct Connect connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-macsec-dedicated.html) · [MAC Security in Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html)

Create new accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections to the transit gateway.
Advertise the on-premises prefix to AWS with the same BGP AS_PATH attribute across all the Site-to-Site VPN connections.

Verify that the transit gateway attachments are present in the Availability Zones of the test VPC.
Verify that the on-premises location is sending traffic by using multiple lows.

Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

Which solution meets these requirements?

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Network Load Balancer (NLB) that has a target group of the existing EC2 instances. Configure TLS connections to terminate on the EC2 instances that use a public certificate. Configure an AWS WAF web ACL. Associate the web ACL with the NLB.

A data analytics company operates a 100-node high performance computing (HPC) cluster for parallel data processing in a VPC in the AWS Cloud. As part of its data-processing workflow, the HPC cluster must make several DNS queries to resolve and connect to Amazon RDS databases, Amazon S3 buckets, and on-premises data stores that are reachable through AWS Direct Connect. The HPC cluster can grow by five to seven times during the company’s peak event at the end of the year.  
  
The company uses two Amazon EC2 instances as the VPC’s primary DNS servers. The EC2 instances forward queries to the default VPC resolver for Amazon Route 53 hosted domains and to the on-premises DNS servers for other on-premises hosted domain names. The company observes job failures and determines that DNS queries from the HPC cluster nodes failed when the nodes attempted to resolve RDS and S3 bucket endpoints.  
  
Which architectural change should a network engineer implement to deliver the DNS service in the **MOST** scalable way?

options.text: Scale out the DNS service by adding two additional EC2 instances in the VPC. Reconfigure half of the HPC cluster nodes to use these new DNS servers. Plan to scale out by adding additional EC2 instance-based DNS servers in the future as the HPC cluster size grows.

Scale up the existing EC2 instances that the company is using as DNS servers. Change the instance size to the largest possible instance size to accommodate the current DNS load and the anticipated load in the future.

Create Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints. Create Route 53 Resolver rules to forward queries to on-premises DNS servers for on premises hosted domain names. Reconfigure the HPC cluster nodes to use the default VPC resolver instead of the EC2 instance-based DNS servers. Terminate the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Route 53 VPC Resolver is the managed DNS resolver for resources in a VPC and can resolve AWS service names without routing queries through self-managed EC2 DNS servers. An outbound Resolver endpoint with forwarding rules conditionally forwards the specified on-premises hosted domains to reachable on-premises DNS servers over Direct Connect, while all other names, including Amazon RDS and Amazon S3 endpoints, are resolved by the default VPC resolver. This removes the EC2 forwarder scaling bottleneck. Inbound Resolver endpoints are for DNS queries that originate in the on-premises network and need resolution in a VPC.

A company plans to host external websites on AWS. The websites will contain multiple tiers, including web servers, application logic services, and databases. The company wants to use AWS Network Firewall, AWS WAF, and VPC security groups for network security.  
  
The company must ensure that Network Firewall firewalls are deployed appropriately in the applicable VPCs. It needs the ability to centrally manage policies deployed to Network Firewall and AWS WAF rules. The company must also let application teams manage their own security groups while ensuring that those security groups do not permit overly permissive access.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Define Network Firewall firewalls, AWS WAFV2 web ACLs. Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups in code. Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy the objects and initial policies and rule groups. Use CloudFormation to update the AWS WAFv2 web ACLs. Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups. Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for overly permissive rules.

Define Network Firewall firewalls. AWS WAFV2 web ACLs, Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups in code. Use the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI to manage the AWS WAFv2 web ACLs. Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups. Use Amazon GuardDuly to invoke an AWS Lambda function to evaluate the configured rules and remove any overly permissive rules.

Deploy AWS WAFv2 IP sets and AWS WAFv2 web ACLs with AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS Firewall Manager to deploy Network Firewall firewalls and VPC security groups where required and to manage the AWS WAFv2 web ACLs, Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups.

Define Network Firewall firewalls, AWS WAFv2 web ACLS, Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups in code. Use AWS CloudFarmation to deploy the objects and initial policies and rule groups. Use AWS Firewall Manager to manage the AWS WAFV2 web ACLS, Network Firewall policies, and VPC security groups. Use Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for overly permissive rules.

questions.explanation:
AWS Firewall Manager centrally applies and manages AWS Network Firewall policies, including firewall deployment in VPCs within policy scope, and AWS WAF policies across an AWS organization. Its VPC security group policies can audit security-group contents for noncompliant rules and optionally remediate them, allowing application teams to retain their own security groups while enforcing centrally defined access constraints.

**Learn more:** [Using AWS Network Firewall policies in Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/network-firewall-policies.html) · [Using AWS WAF policies with Firewall Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-policies.html)

A company operates in the `us-east-1` Region and the `us-west-1` Region. The company is designing a solution to connect an on-premises data center to its AWS environment in `us-east-1`. The solution uses two AWS Direct Connect connections.  
  
Traffic from `us-west-1` to the data center must traverse the Direct Connect connections. A network engineer needs to configure active-passive functionality across the two Direct Connect connections by using a Direct Connect gateway to influence inbound traffic from VPCs in `us-west-1` to the data center.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: At the data center, set the local preference for the primary connection to be higher than the local preference for the secondary connection.
Use AS path prepending to set the AS path on the primary connection to be longer than the AS path on the secondary connection.

Use local preference BGP community tags to apply the 7224:7300 local preference BGP community tag to the prefixes for the primary connection. Apply the 7224:7100 local preference BGP community tag to the prefixes for the secondary connection.

Use local preference BGP community tags to apply the 7224:9300 local preference BGP community tag to the prefixes for the primary connection. Apply the 7224:9100 local preference BGP community tag to the prefixes for secondary connection.

questions.explanation:
For private and transit virtual interfaces, AWS Direct Connect local-preference BGP communities control the preferred AWS-to-on-premises path. Community `7224:7300` is high preference and `7224:7100` is low preference; assigning them to the primary and secondary advertised prefixes, respectively, creates active-passive failover. AWS documents this exact high/low community pattern for active-passive Direct Connect configurations.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses third-party firewall appliances to monitor and inspect on-premises traffic and wants to use the same approach on AWS. The company has one VPC with an internet gateway. The VPC contains a fleet of web servers running on Amazon EC2 instances managed by an Auto Scaling group.  
  
The network team must work with the security team to provide inline inspection for every packet sent to and from the web servers. The solution must scale as the virtual firewall appliance fleet scales.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network team take to implement this solution? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new VPC, and deploy a fleet of firewall appliances. Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Add the firewall appliances as targets.
Create a security group for use with the firewall appliances, and allow port 443. Allow a port for the Galeway Load Balancer to perform health checks.
Create a security group for use with the firewall appliances, and allow port 6081. Allow a port for the Gateway Load Balancer to perform health checks.
Deploy a fleet of firewall appliances to the existing VPC. Create a Gateway Load Balancer. Add the firewall appliances as targets.

Update the internet gateway route table and the web server route table to send traffic to and from the internet to the VPC endpoint ID of the Gateway Load Balancer. Update the subnet route table that is associated with the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint to direct internet traffic to the internet gateway.

Create a new route table inside the web server VPC. Create a new edge association with the internet gateway. Update the internet gateway route table and the web server route table to send traffic to and from the internet to the VPC endpoint ID of the Gateway Load Balancer. Update the subnet route table that is associated with the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint to direct internet traffic to the internet gateway.

questions.explanation:
A Gateway Load Balancer provides a transparent, scalable inspection path for virtual firewall appliances. Firewall targets exchange encapsulated traffic with the Gateway Load Balancer by using the GENEVE protocol on UDP port 6081. The firewall fleet and Gateway Load Balancer can be deployed in a separate provider VPC, while the existing web-server VPC uses a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint. An internet-gateway edge-associated route table must route inbound traffic for the web-server subnet to that endpoint; the web-server subnet routes outbound traffic to it, and the endpoint subnet routes internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/getting-started.html) · [What is a Gateway Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)

A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage many AWS accounts that host numerous VPCs and workloads. The company has an AWS Direct Connect connection between its data center and AWS. A transit gateway in a central network account connects the workload VPCs to the data center.  
  
The company needs to automatically tag each transit gateway attachment with information from tags attached to each requester-account VPC. The company provisions an IAM role in every account. It grants the IAM role permission to retrieve the required VPC tag data and configures a trust policy that allows principals in the central network account to invoke the IAM role.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to monitor the transit gateway for new attachments. Configure IAM Access Analyzer to invoke an AWS Systems Manager runbook that assumes the IAM role in the requester account and tags the attachment with the required information.
Configure an SCP to monitor the transit gateway for new attachments. Configure the SCP to invoke an AWS CloudFormation stack template in the account that requests an attachment to tag the attachment.

Configure Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) and register the transit gateway. Configure IPAM to run an AWS CDK function when a new IP address is requested from the transit gateway for a new attachment. Configure the CDK function to assume the IAM role in the requester account and to tag the attachment with the required information.

Configure AWS Network Manager and register the transit gateway. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to receive attachment notifications from Network with the required information. Manager and to invoke an AWS Lambda function that assumes the IAM role in the requester account. Configure the Lambda function to tag the attachment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Manager can register a transit gateway and track its VPC attachments. It publishes topology-change events, including VPC attachment creation, to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can invoke a Lambda function, which can assume the trusted role in the requester account to retrieve VPC tags and then tag the transit gateway attachment from the central network account.

**Learn more:** [Monitor your global network using EventBridge — AWS Network Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/tgwnm/monitoring-events.html) · [How AWS Global Networks for Transit Gateways works — AWS Network Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/tgwnm/how-gnw-works.html)

3e:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A financial trading company uses Amazon EC2 instances to operate its trading platform. A component of that platform is a third-party pricing service with which the EC2 instances communicate over UDP port 50000."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Recently, the company has experienced issues with the pricing service. Some responses from the pricing service seem to be improperly formatted and therefore are not processed successfully. The third-party vendor requests access to the data returned by the pricing service. The company forbids direct access to production systems and requires all log analysis to occur in a dedicated monitoring account."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which set of actions should a network engineer perform to capture the data and satisfy these requirements?"}],"

Configure a traffic mirror filter to capture the UDP data.2. Configure Traffic Mirroring to capture the traffic for the EC2 instance's elastic network interface.3. Configure a packet inspection package on a new EC2 instance in the production environment. Use the elastic network interface of the new EC2 instance as the target for the traffic mirror.4. Extract the data by using the packet inspection package.5. Provide the data to the third-party vendor.","C":"1. Configure a traffic mirror filter to capture the UDP data.2. Traffic mirror targets can be owned by a different AWS account, subject to the required sharing and network routing configuration. VPC Flow Logs would not provide the request and response payloads needed for debugging.

To satisfy security requirements, the company's accounts must use separate cloud infrastructure.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create one Direct Connect gateway in us-east-1. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Direct Connect gateway with each account. Create a transit VIF for Account Associate the four transit gateways in Account A to the Direct Connect gateway. Create a transit VIF for Account B. Associate the three transit gateways in Account В to the Direct Connect gateway.

Create one Direct Connect gateway in us-east-1 for Account A. Create a second Direct Connect gateway in us-east-1 for Account Create a transit VIF for Account A. Associate the four transit gateways in Account A to the Direct Connect gateway in Account A. Create a transit VIF for Account Associate the three transit gateways in Account В to the Direct Connect gateway in Account В.

questions.explanation:

A company has established hybrid connectivity between its VPCs and its on-premises data center. The company has configured the `on-premises.example.com` subdomain on its DNS server in the on-premises data center. The company uses the `aws.example.com` subdomain for workloads running on AWS across multiple VPCs and accounts. Resources in both environments can reach each other by using IP addresses. The company wants workloads in the VPCs to access on-premises resources by using `on-premises.example.com` DNS names.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MINIMUM** resource management?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Configure a Resolver rule that conditionally forwards DNS queries for on-premises.example.com to the on-premises DNS server. Associate the rule with the VPCs.

Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint and a Resolver outbound endpoint. Configure a Resolver rule that conditionally forwards DNS queries for on-premises.example.com to the on-premises DNS server. Associate the rule with the VPCs.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance. Install and configure BIND software to conditionally forward DNS queries for on-premises.example.com to the on-premises DNS server. Configure the EC2 instance's IP address as a custom DNS server in each VPC.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in each VPC. Install and configure BIND software to conditionally forward DNS queries for on-premises.example.com to the on-premises DNS server. Configure the EC2 instance's IP address as a custom DNS server in each VPC.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint enables VPC Resolver to forward DNS queries from one or more VPCs to DNS resolvers on a connected network. A forwarding rule for `on-premises.example.com` that targets the on-premises DNS server and is associated with the VPCs centrally provides the required resolution. An inbound endpoint serves the opposite direction—DNS queries originating on premises for VPC resources—and is unnecessary here.

**Learn more:** [Forwarding outbound DNS queries to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-outbound-queries.html) · [How Resolver endpoints forward DNS queries from your VPCs to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-forward-vpc-to-network.html)

A network engineer needs to add safeguards that protect encrypted data at Application Load Balancers (ALBs) by using a unique random session key.  
  
What should the network engineer do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Change the ALB security policy to a policy that supports TLS 1.2 protocol only
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt session keys
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the ALBs. and create a security rule to enforce forward secrecy (FS)
Change the ALB security policy to a policy that supports forward secrecy (FS)

questions.explanation:
Forward Secrecy (FS) security policies provide the additional protection of a unique random session key, preventing captured encrypted data from being decoded even if the long-term secret key is compromised. An Application Load Balancer must use a security policy that supports FS to provide this protection.

**Learn more:** [Security policies for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/describe-ssl-policies.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a new application that is deployed in multiple VPCs across multiple AWS Regions. The VPCs are connected by using AWS Transit Gateway. The VPCs include private and public subnets.  
  
All outbound internet traffic from the private subnets must be audited and logged. The company's network engineer plans to use AWS Network Firewall and must ensure that all traffic that passes through Network Firewall is fully logged for auditing and alerting.  
  
How should the network engineer configure Network Firewall logging to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure Network Firewall logging in Amazon CloudWatch to capture all alerts. Send the logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Configure Network Firewall logging in Network Firewall to capture all alerts and flow logs.
Configure Network Firewall logging by configuring VPC Flow Logs for the firewall endpoint. Send the logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Configure Network Firewall logging by configuring AWS CloudTrail to capture data events.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall flow logs capture network traffic that is forwarded to its stateful rules engine, and alert logs capture traffic that matches stateful rules that generate alerts. Enabling both log types provides traffic-audit records and alert records; alert logging alone does not log all flows.

**Learn more:** [Logging network traffic from AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-logging.html) · [Updating an AWS Network Firewall logging configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-update-logging-configuration.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs its IT infrastructure in an on-premises data center and plans to migrate that infrastructure to the AWS Cloud in phases. A network engineer needs to establish a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection between the on-premises data center and VPCs. The company’s network provider requires 3 months to provision the Direct Connect connection.  
  
Meanwhile, the network engineer deploys a temporary AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection that terminates on a virtual private gateway. Despite using a powerful customer gateway device, the engineer finds that the Site-to-Site VPN connection bandwidth is limited to 1.25 Gbps.  
  
What should the network engineer do to increase VPN connection bandwidth before the Direct Connect connection is implemented?

options.text: Contact AWS Support to request a bandwidth quota increase for the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection.
Discuss the issue with the hardware vendor. Buy a bigger and more powerful customer gateway device that has faster encryption and decryption capabilities.
Create several additional Site-to-Site VPN connections that terminate on the same virtual gateway. Configure equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing to use all the VPN connections simultaneously.

Create a transit gateway. Attach the VPCs to the transit gateway. Create several additional Site-to-Site VPN connections that terminate on the transit gateway. Configure equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing to use all the VPN connections simultaneously.

questions.explanation:
Standard AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnels are limited to up to 1.25 Gbps and this limit is not adjustable. Higher aggregate VPN bandwidth can be achieved by terminating multiple Site-to-Site VPN connections on an AWS Transit Gateway and using dynamic-routing ECMP to distribute traffic across the tunnels. A virtual private gateway does not provide this ECMP aggregation capability.

**Learn more:** [AWS Site-to-Site VPN quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-limits.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway + AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-transit-gateway-vpn.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys a new web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application operates in private subnets across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Security auditors mandate encryption for all connections. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS and AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to automate SSL/TLS certificate provisioning. The ALB terminates SSL/TLS connections.  
  
The company tests the application using a single EC2 instance and sees no issues. However, after the production deployment, users report that they can log in but cannot use the application. Each new web request causes the login process to restart.  
  
What should a network engineer do to resolve this issue?

options.text: Modify the ALB listener configuration. Edit the rule that forwards traffic to the target group. Change the rule to enable group-level stickiness. Set the duration to the maximum application session length.

Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer. Create a TLS listener. Create a new target group with the protocol type set to TLS Register the EC2 instances. Modify the target group configuration by enabling the stickiness attribute.
Modify the ALB target group configuration by enabling the stickiness attribute. Use an application-based cookie. Set the duration to the maximum application session length.
Remove the ALB. Create an Amazon Route 53 rule with a failover routing policy for the application name. Configure ACM to issue certificates for each EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer normally distributes requests independently among healthy targets. When an application keeps login-session state locally on an EC2 instance, subsequent requests can reach a different instance and appear unauthenticated. Enabling application-based cookie stickiness on the ALB target group maintains affinity between the client and the instance that created the application session for the configured session duration.

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application VPC and a networking VPC that are connected by VPC peering. The networking VPC contains a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The application VPC contains Amazon EC2 instances that run an application. The EC2 instances belong to a target group associated with the NLB in the networking VPC.  
  
The company configures a third VPC and peers it with the networking VPC. The new VPC contains a new version of the existing application. This new application version runs on new EC2 instances in an application subnet. The new application version runs in a different Availability Zone from the original application version.  
  
The company needs to establish connectivity between the NLB and the new version of the application.  
  
Which combination of steps meets this requirement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Register the new application EC2 instances with the NLB by using the instance IDs.
Register the new application EC2 instances with the NLB by using instance IP addresses.
Configure the NLB in the Availability Zone where the new application EC2 instances run.
Configure the NLB to use zonal shift.
Configure the network ACL for the application subnet in the new VPC to allow outbound connections.
Configure the network ACL for the application subnet in the new VPC to allow inbound connections and outbound connections.

questions.explanation:
EC2 instances in a VPC peered with the Network Load Balancer VPC must be registered as IP-address targets rather than by instance ID. The NLB must enable the Availability Zone containing the registered targets; targets in a non-enabled Availability Zone do not receive traffic. Because network ACLs are stateless, the application subnet must permit both inbound and outbound traffic for load balancer communication, health checks, and response traffic.

**Learn more:** [Target groups for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html) · [Register targets for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/target-group-register-targets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a global network and uses transit gateways to link AWS Regions. The company discovers that two Amazon EC2 instances in separate Regions cannot communicate. A network engineer must troubleshoot this connectivity problem.  
  
What should the network engineer do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer to analyze routes in the transit gateway route tables and in the VPC route tables. Use VPC flow logs to analyze the IP traffic that security group rules and network ACL rules accept or reject in the VPC.

Use AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer to analyze routes in the transit gateway route tables. Verify that the VPC route tables are correct. Use AWS Firewall Manager to analyze the IP traffic that security group rules and network ACL rules accept or reject in the VPC.

Use AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer to analyze routes in the transit gateway route tables. Verify that the VPC route tables are correct. Use VPC flow logs to analyze the IP traffic that security group rules and network ACL rules accept or reject in the VPC.

Use VPC Reachability Analyzer to analyze routes in the transit gateway route tables. Verify that the VPC route tables are correct. Use VPC flow logs to analyze the IP traffic that security group rules and network ACL rules accept or reject in the VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer analyzes routing in transit gateway route tables only, so VPC route tables require separate verification. It does not evaluate security group or network ACL rules. VPC Flow Logs capture accepted and rejected IP traffic and can be used to diagnose traffic affected by security groups and network ACLs.

Which solution meets these requirements?

Use Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall. Add a rule to a rule group to use the AWSManagedDomainsBotnetCommandandControl managed domain list with an action to block botnet traffic.
Use AWS WAF Bot Control. Configure a managed rule group that uses an AWS managed rule set to block botnet traffic.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying third-party firewall appliances in its VPC to provide traffic inspection and NAT capabilities. The VPC contains private subnets and public subnets. The company must deploy the firewall appliances behind a load balancer.  
  
Which architecture meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer with the firewall appliances as targets. Configure the firewall appliances with a single network interface in a private subnet. Use a NAT gateway to send the traffic to the internet after inspection.

Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer with the firewall appliances as targets. Configure the firewall appliances with two network interfaces: one network interface in a private subnet and another network interface in a public subnet. Use the NAT functionality on the firewall appliances to send the traffic to the internet after inspection.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer with the firewall appliances as targets. Configure the firewall appliances with a single network interface in a private subnet. Use a NAT gateway to send the traffic to the internet after inspection.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer with the firewall appliances as targets. Configure the firewall appliances with two network interfaces: one network interface in a private subnet and another network interface in a public subnet. Use the NAT functionality on the firewall appliances to send the traffic to the internet after inspection.

questions.explanation:
Gateway Load Balancer is purpose-built to deploy and scale third-party virtual appliances, including firewalls, as transparent inline targets. A two-interface firewall deployment can use the appliances’ own NAT capability to reach the internet after inspection, eliminating the need for separately billed NAT gateways. AWS notes that third-party appliances that support SNAT and two-arm overlay routing can remove the need for NAT gateways and reduce cost.

To support the application’s growing demand, the company has two redundant 10 GB AWS Direct Connect connections between AWS and its on-premises network.  
  
The company already encrypts traffic between its on-premises network and the colocation. Within the next few months, it must encrypt traffic between AWS and the edge routers in the colocation while maintaining its current bandwidth.  
  
What should a network engineer do to satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy a new public VIF with encryption on the existing Direct Connect connections. Reroute traffic through the new public VIF.
Create a virtual private gateway Deploy new AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from on premises to the virtual private gateway Reroute traffic from the Direct Connect private VIF to the new VPNs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect MACsec supplies Layer 2 point-to-point encryption between a customer edge device and the Direct Connect device. What should a network engineer do to resolve this issue?

options.text: Modify the transit gateway VPC attachment on the shared services VPC by enabling cross-Availability Zone load balancing.
Modify the transit gateway VPC attachment on the shared services VPC by enabling appliance mode support.
Modify the transit gateway by selecting VPN equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing support.
Modify the transit gateway by selecting multicast support.

questions.explanation:
Stateful IDS appliances must receive both directions of a flow through the same appliance path. Enabling appliance mode support on the Transit Gateway VPC attachment for the shared-services inspection VPC maintains Availability Zone and network-interface affinity for the lifetime of the flow, ensuring symmetric routing across Availability Zones and preventing stateful inspection from dropping return traffic.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is setting up connectivity between its on-premises site and an existing VPC on AWS to satisfy a new security requirement. Which combination of steps should a network engineer perform to configure the architecture to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

Create a system rule for the domain name amazonaws.com.

Which combination of steps should the network engineer take next to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

questions.explanation:
