lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s network engineer must design a new solution to troubleshoot and identify network anomalies. The engineer has configured Traffic Mirroring, but the mirrored traffic is overwhelming the Amazon EC2 instance serving as the traffic mirror target. This EC2 instance hosts tools that the company’s security team uses to analyze the traffic.  
  
The network engineer needs a highly available solution that can scale to handle the demand from the mirrored traffic.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) as the traffic mirror target. Behind the NLB. deploy a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use Traffic Mirroring as necessary.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as the traffic mirror target. Behind the ALB, deploy a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use Traffic Mirroring only during non-business hours.
Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer (GLB) as the traffic mirror target. Behind the GLB. deploy a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use Traffic Mirroring as necessary.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with an HTTPS listener as the traffic mirror target. Behind the ALB. deploy a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use Traffic Mirroring only during active events or business hours.

questions.explanation:
A single EC2 traffic-mirror target cannot scale, so the target must be a Network Load Balancer fronting an Auto Scaling group of analysis instances. AWS explicitly recommends mirroring to a Network Load Balancer (with a UDP 4789 listener, since mirrored packets are VXLAN-encapsulated) and running the capture/analysis tools on an Auto Scaled fleet behind it, which delivers both high availability (multi-AZ, cross-zone) and horizontal scale. An Application Load Balancer (B, D) is not a valid traffic-mirror target and only handles HTTP/HTTPS, not the VXLAN/UDP mirror traffic. A Gateway Load Balancer (C) is valid but is designed for GENEVE-based inline inspection appliances, not this out-of-band analysis pattern, and 'only during non-business hours' would fail the continuous requirement.

**Learn more:** [Traffic mirror targets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-targets.html) · [New – VPC Traffic Mirroring](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/new-vpc-traffic-mirroring/)

An application team at a startup is deploying a new multi-tier application in the AWS Cloud. The application will run on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a publicly accessible Network Load Balancer (NLB). The application requires clients to use both UDP and TCP traffic.  
  
In the near term, the application will serve users only in the same geographic location. The team plans to expand the application to a global audience and move the deployment into multiple AWS Regions worldwide to place the application closer to end users. The team wants to use the new Regions to deploy new application versions and be able to control how much traffic each Region receives during these rollouts. Additionally, the team must minimize first-byte latency and jitter (randomized delay) for end users.  
  
How should the application team design the application’s network architecture to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to align to each Regional deployment. Set the NLB for each Region as the origin for each CloudFront distribution. Use an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy to control traffic to the newer Regional deployments.

Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator and listeners for the required ports. Configure endpoint groups for each Region. Configure a traffic dial for the endpoint groups to control traffic to the newer Regional deployments. Register the NLBs with the endpoint groups.
Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for the application in each Region. Adjust the amount of traffic that each Region receives from the Transfer Acceleration endpoints to the Regional NLBs.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that includes an origin group. Set the NLB for each Region as the origins for the origin group. Use an Amazon Route 53 latency routing policy to control traffic to the new Regional deployments.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator supports TCP and UDP listeners, uses static anycast IP addresses that accept traffic at the AWS edge location nearest to each client, and routes it over the AWS global network to healthy regional endpoints. A standard accelerator can register Network Load Balancers as endpoints. Regional endpoint groups support traffic dials that control the percentage of traffic directed to a Region, including for blue/green testing and rollout deployments. This provides the required regional rollout control while reducing latency and jitter for globally distributed users.

A security team is auditing a company's AWS deployment. The team is concerned that two applications could be accessing resources that network ACLs and security groups should block. The applications run across two Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters that use the Amazon VPC Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin for Kubernetes. The clusters are in separate subnets in the same VPC and have a Cluster Autoscaler configured.  
  
The security team must identify which POD IP addresses communicate with which services across the VPC. The team wants to minimize the number of flow logs and inspect traffic from only the two applications.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create VPC flow logs in the default format. Create a filter to gather flow logs only from the EKS nodes. Include the srcaddr field and the dstaddr field in the flow logs.
Create VPC flow logs in a custom format. Set the EKS nodes as the resource Include the pkt-srcaddr field and the pkt-dstaddr field in the flow logs.
Create VPC flow logs in a custom format. Set the application subnets as resources. Include the pkt-srcaddr field and the pkt-dstaddr field in the flow logs.
Create VPC flow logs in a custom format. Create a filter to gather flow logs only from the EKS nodes. Include the pkt-srcaddr field and the pkt-dstaddr field in the flow logs.

questions.explanation:
With the VPC CNI plugin, pods receive VPC IP addresses as secondary IPs on the node ENIs, so to see the true pod-to-service addresses you need a custom-format flow log that includes the pkt-srcaddr and pkt-dstaddr fields (the plain srcaddr/dstaddr show the interface address, not the pod's packet address). Setting the flow log on the two application subnets captures exactly the two applications' traffic, minimizes the number of flow logs, and keeps working as the Cluster Autoscaler adds and removes nodes, giving the least operational overhead. Options A and D describe a 'filter to gather flow logs only from the EKS nodes,' which is not a VPC Flow Logs capability (you choose VPC, subnet, or ENI as the resource), and node/ENI-level logging must be reworked every time the autoscaler changes the fleet; A also uses the default format that lacks the pkt- fields.

How can the company enable the Lambda function to access the ticketing system?

options.text: Set up two NAT gateways. Place each NAT gateway in a different public subnet in separate Availability Zones (AZ2 and AZ3). Configure a route table for private subnets to route traffic to the virtual IP addresses of the two NAT gateways.

A company uses AWS Cloud WAN as its primary connectivity solution to enable communication among VPCs in a multi-account, multi-Region environment. The company has created an attachment-policy statement in the AWS Cloud WAN core network policy. The attachment policy requires approval for new VPC attachments, regardless of the segment with which each new VPC attachment must be associated.  
  
The company wants to automate approval of new VPC attachments according to specific conditions. The company creates an AWS Lambda function to evaluate those conditions. A network engineer must integrate the Lambda function into the company’s existing architecture.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective manner?

options.text: Update the AWS Cloud WAN core network policy to create a network function group. Select the require acceptance option. Create a service insertion segment action that targets the Lambda function.
Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match AWS Network Manager events for the VPC attachments. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function when the rule matches.
Use Amazon CloudWatch logs to stream AWS CloudTrail logs to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure an event source mapping to target the Lambda function to process the event stream.
Configure AWS Network Manager as a source for a pipe in Amazon EventBridge Pipes. Create a filter in the pipe for new VPC attachments. Set the Lambda function as the target of the pipe.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Manager sends Cloud WAN resource-change events to Amazon EventBridge, and EventBridge rules can filter matching events and invoke a Lambda function directly. The function can evaluate the attachment-specific conditions and accept eligible pending VPC attachments. This event-driven integration has no need for intermediary log streaming or Kinesis processing. Network function groups and service insertion control traffic routing through network functions; they do not automate attachment acceptance.

**Learn more:** [AWS Network Manager events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-networkmanager.html) · [Monitor with Amazon CloudWatch Events - AWS Network Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-cloudwatch-events.html)

A software-as-a-service (SaaS) company is moving its private SaaS application to AWS. The company has hundreds of customers that connect to multiple data centers through VPN tunnels. As its customer count has increased, the company has found it increasingly difficult to manage customer routing and segmentation with complex NAT rules.  
  
After the migration to AWS is finished, the company's AWS customers must be able to access the SaaS application directly from their VPCs. At the same time, the company's on-premises customers must still be able to connect by using IPsec-encrypted tunnels.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Connect the AWS customer VPCs to a shared transit gateway. Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections to the transit gateway for the on-premises customers
Use AWS PrivateLink to connect the AWS customers. Use a third-party routing appliance in the SaaS application VPC to terminate onpremises Site-to-Site VPN connections.
Peer each AWS customer's VPCs to the VPC that hosts the SaaS application. Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections on the SaaS VPC virtual private gateway.
Use Site-to-Site VPN tunnels to connect each AWS customer's VPCs to the VPC that hosts the SaaS application. Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to connect the on-premises customers.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway provides centralized hub-and-spoke connectivity for many VPCs and Site-to-Site VPN connections. Transit gateway route tables and attachment associations enable customer-specific routing and network segmentation at scale, while AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections to the transit gateway provide IPsec-encrypted connectivity for on-premises networks.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-transit-gateway-vpn.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates 10 Amazon EC2 instances running web server software in a production VPC. The company also operates 10 web servers in an on-premises data center. A 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection links the on-premises data center to the production VPC. The data center uses the `10.100.0.0/20` CIDR block.  
  
The company must implement a load-balancing solution that accepts HTTPS traffic from thousands of external users. The solution must distribute traffic across the web servers in AWS and the web servers in the data center. No matter where a web server is located, HTTPS requests must be routed to the same web server throughout the session.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the production VPC. Create one target group for the EC2 Instances and a second target group for the on-premises servers. Specify IP as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target groups. Enable connection draining on the NLB.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the production VPC. Create one target group for the EC2 Instances and a second target group for the on-premises servers. Specify IP as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target groups. Enable application-based sticky sessions on the ALB.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in the production VPCreate one target group for the EC2 Instances and a second target group for the on-premises servers. Specify instance as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target groups. Enable sticky sessions on the NLB.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the production VPC. Create one target group for the EC2 Instances and a second target group for the on-premises servers. Specify instance as the target type. Register the EC2 instances and the on-premises servers with the target groups. Enable application-based sticky sessions on the ALB.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer can terminate HTTPS traffic and use application-based cookie stickiness to bind a user session to one target. An IP target group supports registered private IP addresses for both EC2 instances and on-premises resources connected through AWS Direct Connect; `10.100.0.0/20` is within the supported `10.0.0.0/8` private range. Network Load Balancer sticky sessions are not supported for TLS listeners, and an instance target type cannot represent the on-premises servers.

**Learn more:** [Target groups for your Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html) · [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

A company operates applications in two VPCs located in separate AWS Regions. One VPC is in the `us-east-1` Region, and the other VPC is in the `us-west-1` Region. The company must establish connectivity between the two VPCs. It must also connect both VPCs to applications running in an on-premises data center.  
  
The current traffic requirement between the VPCs is 50 ТВ per month, and the company anticipates that VPC-to-VPC traffic will grow. Traffic from the VPCs to the on-premises data center is 10 ТВ per month, and the company expects traffic between the VPCs and the data center to remain constant.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements **MOST cost-effectively**?

options.text: Create a transit gateway in each Region. Create VPN connections from the transit gateways to the on-premises firewall. Create a peering connection between the transit gateways.

Create a virtual private gateway in each Region. Create VPN connections from the on-premises firewall to the virtual private gateways. Configure the on-premises firewall to route the traffic between the two VPCs.
Create a virtual private gateway in each Region. Create VPN connections from the on-premises firewall to the virtual private gateways. Create a VPC peering connection between the two VPCs.
Create a virtual private gateway in each Region. Create VPN connections from the on-premises firewall to the virtual private gateways. Create a VPN connection between the virtual private gateways.

questions.explanation:
A direct inter-Region VPC peering connection provides private, point-to-point connectivity between the two VPCs and is the lowest-cost, highest-performance option for inter-VPC communication. It avoids Transit Gateway data-processing and attachment charges, which is especially important for the 50 ТВ per month of traffic that is expected to increase. Because VPC peering does not permit transitive use of a VPC's VPN connection, each VPC needs its own virtual private gateway and VPN connection to the on-premises firewall.

**Learn more:** [VPC peering — Building a Scalable and Secure Multi-VPC AWS Network Infrastructure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/vpc-peering.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/transit-gateway/pricing/)

A company has a hybrid architecture with an AWS Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and AWS. It runs production applications both in the on-premises data center and in a VPC. The on-premises applications must communicate with the VPC applications. The company uses `corp.example.com` as the domain name for on-premises resources and uses an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for `aws.example.com` to host VPC resources.  
  
The company uses an open-source recursive DNS resolver in a VPC subnet and a DNS resolver in the on-premises data center. Its on-premises DNS resolver has a forwarder that sends requests for the `aws.example.com` domain name to the DNS resolver in the VPC. The DNS resolver in the VPC has a forwarder that sends requests for the `corp.example.com` domain name to the DNS resolver in the on-premises data center. The company has decided to replace the open-source recursive DNS resolver with Amazon Route 53 Resolver endpoints.  
  
Which combination of steps should a network engineer take to perform this replacement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver rule to forward aws.example.com domain queries to the IP addresses of the outbound endpoint.
Configure the on-premises DNS resolver to forward aws.example.com domain queries to the IP addresses of the inbound endpoint.
Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint and a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint.
Create a Route 53 Resolver rule to forward aws.example.com domain queries to the IP addresses of the inbound endpoint.
Create a Route 53 Resolver rule to forward corp.example.com domain queries to the IP address of the on-premises DNS resolver.
Configure the on-premises DNS resolver to forward aws.example.com queries to the IP addresses of the outbound endpoint.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint accepts DNS queries forwarded from the on-premises network into the VPC, so the on-premises resolver must forward `aws.example.com` to the inbound endpoint IP addresses. An outbound endpoint and a forwarding rule for `corp.example.com` route VPC-originated DNS queries to the on-premises DNS resolver. Resolver forwarding rules use outbound endpoints and target network DNS-resolver IP addresses; they do not target inbound or outbound endpoint IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Resolving DNS queries between VPCs and your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-DSN-queries-to-vpc.html) · [Forwarding outbound DNS queries to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-outbound-queries.html)

A company runs critical VPC workloads that connect to an on-premises data center using two redundant, active-passive AWS Direct Connect connections. However, a recent outage of one Direct Connect connection showed that traffic takes more than a minute to fail over to the secondary Direct Connect connection. The company wants to decrease failover time from minutes to seconds.  
  
Which solution provides the **LARGEST** reduction in BGP failover time?

options.text: Reduce the BGP hold-down timer that is configured on the BGP sessions on the Direct Connect connection VIFs.
Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the Direct Connect connection state to invoke an AWS Lambda function to fail over the traffic.
Configure Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on the Direct Connect connections on the AWS side.
Configure Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on the Direct Connect connections on the on-premises router.

questions.explanation:
Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) detects forwarding-path failures much faster than BGP hold timers. For AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces, asynchronous BFD is automatically enabled by AWS but takes effect only when it is configured on the customer router. AWS documents a 300-ms minimum BFD interval and a minimum multiplier of 3, enabling failure detection in seconds or less.

**Learn more:** [BGP-specific settings - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/bgp-specific-settings.html) · [Direct Connect connection options - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a global online game on AWS, and its popularity is increasing. Users are reporting issues with the game's responsiveness. Replay rates are declining, and the company is losing subscribers. The game servers are in the `us-west-2` Region and use an Elastic Load Balancer to distribute client traffic.  
  
The company has decided to deploy game servers in 11 additional AWS Regions to reduce the network-traffic round-trip times to game clients. A network engineer must design an Amazon Route 53 DNS solution that ensures user traffic is delivered to game servers with an optimal response time.  
  
What should the network engineer do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Route 53 records for the Elastic Load Balancers in each Region. Specify a weighted routing policy. Calculate the weight by using the number of clients in each Region.
Create Route 53 records for the Elastic Load Balancers in each Region. Specify a latency routing policy. Set the Region to the Region where the Elastic Load Balancer is deployed.
Create Route 53 records for the Elastic Load Balancers in each Region. Specify a multivalue answer routing policy. Test latency from the game client, and connect to the server with the best response.
Create Route 53 records for the Elastic Load Balancers in each Region. Specify a geolocation routing policy. Set the location to the Region where the Elastic Load Balancer is deployed.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the AWS Region with the lowest latency among the Regions represented by latency records. Creating a latency record for each Elastic Load Balancer and setting each record's Region to the load balancer's deployment Region provides the required lowest-latency regional endpoint selection.

**Learn more:** [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html) · [Values specific for latency records - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-values-latency.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has begun using AWS Cloud WAN with one edge location in the `us-east-1` Region. The company has a production segment and a security segment in AWS Cloud WAN, along with a default core network policy.  
  
The company created a production VPC for the production workload and an outbound inspection VPC to inspect internet-bound traffic from the production VPC. It attached the production VPC to the production segment and the outbound inspection VPC to the security segment. The company also created an AWS Network Firewall firewall in the outbound inspection VPC to inspect internet-based traffic.  
  
The company updated a route table for the production VPC to send all internet-bound traffic to the AWS Cloud WAN core network. It also updated a route table for the outbound inspection VPC so that Network Firewall inspects all outgoing and incoming traffic.  
  
During testing, an Amazon EC2 instance in the production VPC cannot access the internet. The company checks the Network Firewall rules and confirms that the rules are not blocking the traffic.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update the core network policy to configure segment sharing. Share the production segment with the security segment.
Update the core network policy to create a static route for the security segment. Specify 0.0.0.0/0 as the destination CIDR block. Specify the outbound inspection VPC as an attachment.
Update the core network policy to create a static route for the production segment. Specify 0.0.0.0/0 as the destination CIDR block. Specify the outbound inspection VPC as an attachment.
Update the core network policy to create a static route for the production segment. Specify 10.2.0.0/16 as the destination CIDR block. Specify the outbound inspection VPC as an attachment.
Create an attachment to attach the outbound inspection VPC to the production segment. Update the core network policy to turn on isolated attachment for the production segment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cloud WAN segments are isolated routing domains by default. Sharing the production segment with the security segment makes the outbound inspection VPC attachment reachable from the production segment. A static `0.0.0.0/0` route in the production segment targeted to that attachment then directs the production VPC’s internet-bound traffic through the inspection VPC, where Network Firewall can inspect it. AWS documents that segment sharing advertises attachment and return routes between shared segments, while a segment route creates a static CIDR route to selected attachments.

**Learn more:** [Add segment actions in an AWS Cloud WAN core network policy version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policy-network-actions-routes.html) · [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html)

A network engineer is undertaking a large migration from an on-premises data center to an AWS Control Tower-based, multi-account environment. A transit gateway is deployed in a central network services account. The central network services account is shared with an organization in AWS Organizations by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).  
  
A shared services account also exists in the environment. The shared services account hosts workloads that must be shared with the entire organization.  
  
The network engineer must create a solution that automates deployment of common network components throughout the environment. The solution must provision a VPC for application workloads in every new and existing member account. The VPCs must connect to the transit gateway in the central network services account.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy an AWS Lambda function to the shared services account. Program the Lambda function to assume a role in the new and existing member accounts to provision the necessary network infrastructure.
Update the existing accounts with an Account Factory Customization (AFC). Select the same AFC when provisioning new accounts.
Create an AWS CloudFormation template that describes the infrastructure that needs to be created in each account. Upload the template as an AWS Service Catalog product to the shared services account.

Deploy an Amazon EventBridge rule on a default event bus in the shared services account. Configure the EventBridge rule to react to AWS Control Tower CreateManagedAccount lifecycle events and to invoke the AWS Lambda function.
Create an AWSControlTowerBiueprintAccess role in the shared services account.F Create an AWSControlTowerBiueprintAccess role in each member account.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower Account Factory Customization applies a Service Catalog blueprint to existing accounts during account updates and to new accounts during provisioning, eliminating the need to operate custom event-driven automation. A CloudFormation template can define each account’s VPC and transit gateway attachment as the blueprint product. The shared services account can serve as the blueprint hub account, where it must contain the `AWSControlTowerBlueprintAccess` role; AWS Control Tower requires that role in the designated hub account to access and distribute the Service Catalog blueprint.

**Learn more:** [Customize accounts with Account Factory Customization (AFC)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/af-customization-page.html) · [Using identity-based policies for AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/access-control-managing-permissions.html)

A company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the company’s on-premises data center to a virtual private gateway in the AWS Cloud. Because of congestion, the company is encountering availability and performance problems while traffic traverses the internet before reaching AWS.  
  
A network engineer must reduce these issues for the connection as quickly as possible and with minimal administrative effort.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Edit the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection by enabling acceleration. Stop and start the VPN service on the customer gateway for the new setting to take effect.

Configure a transit gateway in the same AWS Region as the existing virtual private gateway. Create a new accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection. Connect the new connection to the transit gateway by using a VPN attachment. Update the customer gateway device to use the new Site to Site VPN connection. Delete the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection

Create a new accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection. Connect the new Site-to-Site VPN connection to the existing virtual private gateway. Update the customer gateway device to use the new Site-to-Site VPN connection. Delete the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection.

Create a new AWS Direct Connect connection with a private VIF between the on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud. Update the customer gateway device to use the new Direct Connect connection. Delete the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection.

questions.explanation:
AWS accelerated Site-to-Site VPN routes traffic through the AWS global network after it enters the nearest AWS edge location, reducing disruption and congestion associated with the public-internet path. Acceleration is supported only for Site-to-Site VPN connections attached to a transit gateway, not a virtual private gateway; creating a transit gateway and a new accelerated VPN attachment satisfies that constraint.

**Learn more:** [Accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/accelerated-vpn.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer must establish an encrypted connection between an on-premises data center and a VPC. The engineer attaches the VPC to a virtual private gateway and configures an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. After configuration, the VPN tunnel is **UP** and functioning. However, during the Phase 2 rekey of VPN negotiation, the customer gateway device receives parameters different from those it is configured to support.  
  
The engineer reviews the VPN tunnel IPsec configuration and finds that the customer gateway device is configured with the most secure encryption algorithms supplied by the AWS Site-to-Site VPN configuration file.  
  
What should the network engineer do to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

options.text: Check the native virtual private gateway logs. Restrict the VPN tunnel options to the specific VPN parameters that the virtual private gateway requires.
Check the native customer gateway logs. Restrict the VPN tunnel options to the specific VPN parameters that the customer gateway requires.
Check Amazon CloudWatch logs of the virtual private gateway. Restrict the VPN tunnel options to the specific VPN parameters that the virtual private gateway requires.
Check Amazon CloudWatch logs of the customer gateway. Restrict the VPN tunnel options to the specific VPN parameters that the customer gateway requires.

questions.explanation:
AWS VPN endpoints support rekeying and require agreement on the IPsec/IKE parameters. The customer gateway’s native logs reveal the proposal mismatch at the on-premises endpoint. Configuring the VPN tunnel options to permit only the specific algorithms and parameters supported by the customer gateway ensures that AWS does not select another default-supported proposal during Phase 2 rekeying.

**Learn more:** [Configure tunnel options for AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/tunnel-configure.html) · [Requirements for an AWS Site-to-Site VPN customer gateway device](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/CGRequirements.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses the `us-east-1` Region and the `ap-south-1` Region for its business units (BUs). The BUs are named BU-1 and BU-Z. Each BU has two VPCs in `us-east-1` and one VPC in `ap-south-1`.  
  
Because of workload-isolation requirements, resources can communicate within the same BU but cannot communicate with resources in the other BU. The company plans to add more BUs and expand into additional Regions.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Configure an AWS Cloud WAN network that operates in the required Regions. Attach all BU VPCs to the AWS Cloud WAN core network. Update the AWS Cloud WAN segment actions to configure new routes to deny traffic between the different BU segments.

Configure a transit gateway in each Region. Configure peering between the transit gateways. Attach the BU VPCs to the transit gateway in the corresponding Region. Configure the transit gateway and VPC route tables to isolate traffic between BU VPCs.

Configure an AWS Cloud WAN network that operates in the required Regions. Attach all BU VPCs to the AWS Cloud WAN core network. Update the core network policy by setting the isolate-attachments parameter for each segment.
Configure an AWS Cloud WAN network that operates in the required Regions. Create AWS Cloud WAN segments for each BU Configure VPC attachments for each BU’s VPCs to the corresponding BU segment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cloud WAN segments are dedicated routing domains: attachments within a segment can communicate by default, while attachments in separate segments do not communicate unless routes are explicitly shared. Assigning each BU’s VPC attachments to that BU’s segment therefore permits intra-BU connectivity across Regions and prevents inter-BU connectivity. Cloud WAN centrally applies the segmentation across Regions, making it more operationally efficient as BUs and Regions grow.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Cloud WAN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/what-is-cloudwan.html) · [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html)

A company is rolling out a new application on AWS. The application uses dynamic multicasting. The company has five VPCs, all attached to a transit gateway. Amazon EC2 instances in every VPC must be able to dynamically register to receive a multicast transmission.  
  
How should a network engineer configure the AWS resources to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create a static source multicast domain within the transit gateway. Associate the VPCs and applicable subnets with the multicast domain. Register the multicast senders' network interface with the multicast domain. Adjust the network ACLs to allow UDP traffic from the source to all receivers and to allow UDP traffic that is sent to the multicast group address.

Create a static source multicast domain within the transit gateway. Associate the VPCs and applicable subnets with the multicast domain. Register the multicast senders' network interface with the multicast domain. Adjust the network ACLs to allow TCP traffic from the source to all receivers and to allow TCP traffic that is sent to the multicast group address.

Create an Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) multicast domain within the transit gateway. Associate the VPCs and applicable subnets with the multicast domain. Register the multicast senders' network interface with the multicast domain. Adjust the network ACLs to allow UDP traffic from the source to all receivers and to allow UDP traffic that is sent to the multicast group address.

Create an Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) multicast domain within the transit gateway. Associate the VPCs and applicable subnets with the multicast domain. Register the multicast senders' network interface with the multicast domain. Adjust the network ACLs to allow TCP traffic from the source to all receivers and to allow TCP traffic that is sent to the multicast group address.

questions.explanation:
An IGMPv2-enabled Transit Gateway multicast domain supports dynamic multicast membership: EC2 instances join and leave multicast groups through IGMP messages. Multicast application traffic is carried with UDP, and the relevant subnet network ACLs must allow UDP traffic from the source to receivers and UDP traffic sent to the multicast group address.

**Learn more:** [Multicast in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-multicast-overview.html) · [Example: Manage IGMP configurations using AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/multicast-configurations-igmp.html)

The company’s customer-facing application runs as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the us-west-2 Region. An Amazon CloudFront distribution is configured with the ALB as its origin. The company uses a third-party trusted certificate authority to provide its certificates.  
  
The company uses HTTPS to encrypt data in transit. It needs additional field-level encryption to keep sensitive data encrypted during processing so that only specific application components can decrypt the sensitive data.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Import the third-party certificate for the ALB. Associate the certificate with the ALB. Upload the certificate for the CloudFront distribution into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in us-west-2.

Import the third-party certificate for the ALB into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in us-west-2. Associate the certificate with the ALUpload the certificate for the CloudFront distribution into ACM in the us-east-1 Region.

Upload the private key that handles the encryption of the sensitive data to the CloudFront distribution. Create a field-level encryption profile and specify the fields that contain sensitive information. Create a field-level encryption configuration, and choose the newly created profile. Link the configuration to the appropriate cache behavior that is associated with sensitive POST requests.

Upload the public key that handles the encryption of the sensitive data to the CloudFront distribution. Create a field-level encryption configuration, and specify the fields that contain sensitive information. Create a field-level encryption profile, and choose the newly created configuration. Link the profile to the appropriate cache behavior that is associated with sensitive GET requests.

Upload the public key that handles the encryption of the sensitive data to the CloudFront distribution. Create a field-level encryption profile and specify the fields that contain sensitive information. Create a field-level encryption configuration, and choose the newly created profile. Link the configuration to the appropriate cache behavior that is associated with sensitive POST requests.

questions.explanation:
ACM certificates are regional: the certificate used by the ALB must be imported into ACM in us-west-2, and the viewer-facing certificate for a CloudFront distribution must be imported into ACM in us-east-1. CloudFront field-level encryption encrypts designated POST fields using an uploaded public key. A field-level encryption profile defines the sensitive fields, a configuration selects that profile, and the configuration is associated with the relevant cache behavior. Authorized origin components use the corresponding private key to decrypt the fields.

**Learn more:** [Requirements for using SSL/TLS certificates with CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/cnames-and-https-requirements.html) · [Use field-level encryption to help protect sensitive data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)

A company operates multiple firewalls and ISPs for its on-premises data center. It has one AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the on-premises data center to a transit gateway. One ISP services the Site-to-Site VPN connection. Multiple VPCs are attached to the transit gateway.  
  
A customer gateway used by the Site-to-Site VPN connection fails. Connectivity is entirely lost, but the company’s network team receives no notification.  
  
The network team must implement redundancy within a week in case a single customer gateway fails again. The team wants to use an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic if any tunnel of the Site-to-Site VPN connection fails.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Replace the existing customer gateway with a new router. Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. For each VPN connection, set up a CloudWatch TunnelState alarm for the VPN connection. Use a value of 0 for the alarm.

Use a second customer gateway and a second ISP. Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. For each VPN connection, set up a CloudWatch TunnelState alarm for the VPN connection. Use a value of less than 1 for the alarm.

Add an AWS Direct Connect connection to the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. For each VPN connection, set up a CloudWatch TunnelState alarm for the VPN connection. Use a value of failed for the alarm.

Use a second customer gateway with the existing ISP. Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway. For each VPN connection, set up a CloudWatch TunnelState alarm for the VPN connection. Use a value of unavailable for the alarm.

questions.explanation:
A second customer gateway and a second ISP, with a second Site-to-Site VPN connection to the same transit gateway, remove both the customer gateway and ISP single points of failure. AWS Site-to-Site VPN TunnelState is 1 when tunnel connectivity is up and is below 1 when at least one tunnel is not up, so an alarm for a value less than 1 provides notification of any tunnel failure.

**Learn more:** [Monitor AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnels using Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/monitoring-cloudwatch-vpn.html) · [AWS Site-to-Site VPN single and multiple VPN connection examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/VPC_Scenario4.html)

A company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances into private subnets in a VPC. The EC2 instances must be able to initiate all requests that leave the VPC, including requests to the company’s on-premises data center through an AWS Direct Connect connection. Resources outside the VPC must not be permitted to initiate communications directly with the EC2 instances.  
  
The on-premises data center’s customer gateway uses a stateful firewall device that filters inbound and outbound requests to and from multiple VPCs. The company also wants to use one IP match rule to permit all communication from the EC2 instances to its data center through a single IP address.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a VPN connection over the Direct Connect connection by using the on-premises firewall. Use the firewall to block all traffic from on premises to AWS. Allow a stateful connection from the EC2 instances to initiate the requests.
Configure the on-premises firewall to filter all requests from the on-premises network to the EC2 instances. Allow a stateful connection if the EC2 instances in the VPC initiate the traffic.

Deploy a NAT gateway into a private subnet in the VPC where the EC2 instances are deployed. Specify the NAT gateway type as private. Configure the on-premises firewall to allow connections from the IP address that is assigned to the NAT gateway.

Deploy a NAT instance into a private subnet in the VPC where the EC2 instances are deployed. Configure the on-premises firewall to allow connections from the IP address that is assigned to the NAT instance.

questions.explanation:
A private NAT gateway translates the source addresses of EC2-initiated traffic to its private IP address, allowing the on-premises firewall to allow-list a single address. NAT devices allow private-subnet resources to initiate communication with on-premises networks while preventing unsolicited inbound connection requests. A NAT gateway is AWS-managed and requires less administration than a NAT instance.

**Learn more:** [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html) · [NAT gateway use cases](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html)

A company plans to use Amazon S3 to archive financial data. The data is presently stored in an on-premises data center. The company uses AWS Direct Connect, along with a Direct Connect gateway and a transit gateway, to connect to its on-premises data center. The data must not traverse the public internet and must be encrypted while in transit.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Direct Connect public VIF. Set up an IPsec VPN connection over the public VIF to access Amazon S3. Use HTTPS for communication.

Create an IPsec VPN connection over the transit VIF. Create a VPC and attach the VPC to the transit gateway. In the VPC, provision an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Use HTTPS for communication.
Create a VPC and attach the VPC to the transit gateway. In the VPC, provision an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Use HTTPS for communication.
Create a Direct Connect public VIF. Set up an IPsec VPN connection over the public VIF to the transit gateway. Create an attachment for Amazon S3. Use HTTPS for communication.

questions.explanation:
Create a VPC, attach it to the existing transit gateway, provision an interface (PrivateLink) VPC endpoint for Amazon S3, and use HTTPS. Traffic then flows on-premises → Direct Connect transit VIF → Direct Connect gateway → transit gateway → VPC interface endpoint → S3, staying entirely on the AWS private network and never traversing the public internet, while HTTPS/TLS satisfies encryption in transit. The added IPsec VPN in option B is unnecessary complexity given the endpoint already keeps traffic private and HTTPS already encrypts it. Options A and D route over a public VIF and add VPN plumbing that the interface endpoint makes redundant.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html) · [Direct Connect + Transit Gateway + VPN connectivity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-direct-connect-aws-transit-gateway-vpn.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built an application on AWS to monitor vending-machine inventory levels and automatically start the restocking process. The company plans to integrate the application with vending machines and deploy those machines across several markets worldwide. The application is hosted in a VPC in the `us-east-1` Region. It consists of an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Communication from the vending machines to the application uses HTTPS.  
  
The company plans to use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator and configure the accelerator’s static IP addresses in the vending machines for application-endpoint access. The application must be reachable only through the accelerator, not through a direct internet connection to the ALB endpoint.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the ALB in a private subnet of the VPC. Attach an internet gateway without adding routes in the subnet route tables to point to the internet gateway. Configure the accelerator with endpoint groups that include the ALB endpoint. Configure the ALB’s security group to only allow inbound traffic from the internet on the ALB listener port.

Configure the ALB in a private subnet of the VPC. Configure the accelerator with endpoint groups that include the ALB endpoint. Configure the ALB's security group to only allow inbound traffic from the internet on the ALB listener port.

Configure the ALB in a public subnet of the VPAttach an internet gateway. Add routes in the subnet route tables to point to the internet gateway. Configure the accelerator with endpoint groups that include the ALB endpoint. Configure the ALB's security group to only allow inbound traffic from the accelerator's IP addresses on the ALB listener port.

Configure the ALB in a private subnet of the VPC. Attach an internet gateway. Add routes in the subnet route tables to point to the internet gateway. Configure the accelerator with endpoint groups that include the ALB endpoint. Configure the ALB's security group to only allow inbound traffic from the accelerator's IP addresses on the ALB listener port.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator supports an internal Application Load Balancer endpoint. To use an internal ALB endpoint, the VPC must have an internet gateway attached, but the ALB’s private subnets do not require routes to that gateway. Without those routes, the ALB has no direct internet path, while Global Accelerator can still route traffic to it. Application Load Balancer endpoints use client IP preservation, so the ALB security group must permit the client-originated HTTPS traffic rather than only the accelerator’s static IP addresses.

**Learn more:** [Secure VPC connections in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/secure-vpc-connections.html) · [Requirements for resources you add as accelerator endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints-caveats.html)

Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection between each company's transit gateway to establish reachability between the respective networks. Configure VPC Flow Logs for all VPCs. Publish the flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Use VPC Reachability Analyzer to monitor connectivity.

Configure a Site-to-Site VPN connection between each company's transit gateway to establish reachability between the respective networks. Configure VPC Flow Logs for all VPCs. questions.explanation:

questions.explanation:

A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances belong to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group.  
  
To meet new security standards, the company must capture all application access data, including server response codes, request paths, latency, and client IP addresses. The company also must query the captured data for performance analysis.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable VPC flow logs on the ALB subnets. Store the logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Query the logs in the S3 bucket by using Amazon Athena.

Configure Amazon VPC Traffic Mirroring on all EC2 elastic network interfaces. Deploy a third-party monitoring appliance from AWS Marketplace in a private subnet. Use Amazon Data Firehose to send all mirrored traffic to the monitoring appliance. Query the logs directly from the monitoring appliance.

Configure Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring on the EC2 instances Include all available logs. Use Amazon Data Firehose to send all the collected logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Query the data directly from the S3 bucket.
Enable access logs on the ALB. Store the logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Query the logs in the S3 bucket by using Amazon Athena.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer access logs capture detailed request information, including the client IP address, request URI, request/target/response processing times, and load balancer or target status codes. ALB can deliver these logs to Amazon S3, where Amazon Athena can query them for performance analysis.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global film-production company uses the AWS Cloud to encode and store video content before distribution. The company’s three global offices connect to the `us-east-1` Region through AWS Site-to-Site VPN links that terminate on a transit gateway with BGP routing enabled.  
  
The company recently began producing higher-resolution content for 8K streaming. Content files are now three times larger than files in the prior format. Uploading files to Amazon EC2 instances takes 10 times as long as it did with the previous format.  
  
Which actions should a network engineer recommend to decrease upload times? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a second VPN tunnel from each office location to the transit gateway. Activate equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing.
Modify the transit gateway to activate Jumbo MTU on the VPN tunnels to each office location.
Replace the existing VPN tunnels with new tunnels that have acceleration activated.
Upgrade each EC2 instance to a modern instance type. Activate Jumbo MTU in the operating system.
Replace the existing VPN tunnels with new tunnels that have IGMP activated.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway can use ECMP with dynamically routed Site-to-Site VPN connections to aggregate multiple VPN tunnels and provide greater VPN bandwidth. Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connections, which are supported when attached to a transit gateway, use AWS Global Accelerator to route traffic through the AWS global network from an edge location near the customer gateway and optimize the network path.

**Learn more:** [AWS Transit Gateway + AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-transit-gateway-vpn.html) · [Accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/accelerated-vpn.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s network engineer is setting up an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between a transit gateway and the company’s on-premises network. The Site-to-Site VPN connection is configured to use BGP across two tunnels in active/active mode, with equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing enabled on the transit gateway.  
  
When the network engineer tries to send traffic from the on-premises network to an Amazon EC2 instance, the traffic uses the first tunnel. However, return traffic arrives through the second tunnel and is dropped at the customer gateway. The network engineer must fix this problem without decreasing the overall VPN bandwidth.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the customer gateway to use AS PATH prepending and local preference to prefer one tunnel over the other.
Configure the Site-to-Site VPN options to set the first tunnel as the primary tunnel to eliminate asymmetric routing.
Configure the virtual tunnel interfaces on the customer gateway to allow asymmetric routing.
Configure the Site-to-Site VPN to use static routing in active/active mode to ensure that traffic flows over a preferred path.

questions.explanation:
ECMP on a transit gateway aggregates active VPN tunnels and can cause the two directions of a flow to traverse different tunnels. The customer gateway must therefore support and permit asymmetric routing so that it does not drop return traffic received on the other tunnel. AWS recommends customer gateway devices that support asymmetric routing; static-routing VPN connections do not support ECMP.

**Learn more:** [Route tables and AWS Site-to-Site VPN route priority](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/vpn-route-priority.html) · [Create a transit gateway in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/create-tgw.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has numerous VPCs in the `us-east-1` Region. The company uses a transit gateway to connect the VPCs with each other. The company recently acquired a smaller company that has one VPC named VPC-Z.  
  
A network engineer must onboard VPC-Z to the existing transit gateway. The network engineer identifies an IP address overlap between VPC-Z and VPC-A. The network engineer must provide outbound connectivity from VPC-Z to all the company’s other VPCs, including VPC-A.  
  
Which combination of solutions will meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a new non-overlapping CIDR block in VPC-Z. Create two subnets that use the new CIDR block.
Create a new non-overlapping CIDR block in VPC-A. Create two subnets that use the new CIDR block.
Create a private NAT gateway in VPC-Z in a non-overlapping subnet. Advertise only the non-overlapping VPC-Z CIDR block to the transit gateway route table.
Create a private NAT gateway in VPC-A in a non-overlapping subnet. Advertise only the non-overlapping VPC-A CIDR block to the transit gateway route table.
Create a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-Z.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway does not support routing between attached VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges. Assigning VPC-Z a secondary, non-overlapping CIDR with subnets creates a routable address space. A private NAT gateway in that non-overlapping VPC-Z subnet translates VPC-Z’s outbound source addresses to a unique private address, and advertising only the non-overlapping VPC-Z CIDR to the transit gateway prevents the conflicting CIDR from being propagated.

**Learn more:** [Amazon VPC attachments in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-vpc-attachments.html) · [NAT gateway use cases: Enable communication between overlapping networks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html)

options.text: Create a public hosted zone for example com in the staging account
Create a staging example.com NS record in the example.com domain. Populate the value with the name servers from the staging.example.com domain. Set the routing policy type to simple routing.
Create a private hosted zone for staging example com in the staging account.
Create an example com NS record in the staging example.com domain. Populate the value with the name servers from the example.com domain. Set the routing policy type to simple routing.
Create a public hosted zone for staging.example.com in the staging account.

questions.explanation:
A public hosted zone for `staging.example.com` provides an independently managed authoritative DNS zone in the staging account. An NS record named `staging.example.com` in the parent `example.com` public hosted zone, populated with the child zone’s Route 53 name servers, delegates public DNS authority for that subdomain to the staging zone. The developers can then create and delete records there without production-account access.

**Learn more:** [Routing traffic for subdomains - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-routing-traffic-for-subdomains.html)

A company is migrating its containerized application to AWS. Its architecture will include an ingress VPC with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) that distributes traffic to front-end pods in an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The application's front end will identify which user is requesting access and will route traffic to 1 of 10 services VPCs. Each services VPC will contain an NLB that distributes traffic to the service pods in an EKS cluster.  
  
The company is concerned about overall cost. User traffic will account for more than 10 TB of data transfer from the ingress VPC to services VPCs each month. A network engineer must recommend a design for communication between the VPCs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Create a transit gateway. Peer each VPC to the transit gateway. Use zonal DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs to minimize cross-AZ traffic from the ingress VPC to the services VPCs.
Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint in every Availability Zone in the ingress VPC. Each PrivateLink endpoint will point to the zonal DNS entry of the NLB in the services VPCs.

Create a VPC peering connection between the ingress VPC and each of the 10 services VPCs. Use zonal DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs to minimize cross-AZ traffic from the ingress VPC to the services VPCs.
Create a transit gateway. Peer each VPC to the transit gateway. Turn off cross-AZ load balancing on the transit gateway. Use Regional DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs.

questions.explanation:
VPC peering has no charge to create the connection, and traffic sent over a peering connection within the same Availability Zone is free. Direct peering between the ingress VPC and each services VPC, combined with the services NLB zonal DNS records, minimizes cross-AZ transfer and avoids the per-GB data-processing and attachment charges incurred by AWS Transit Gateway or the endpoint charges incurred by AWS PrivateLink.

**Learn more:** [What is VPC peering?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/what-is-vpc-peering.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/transit-gateway/pricing/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A US-based company is expanding its operations into Europe. A network engineer must extend the company’s network infrastructure by deploying a new hub-and-spoke architecture in the `eu-west-1` Region. The engineer uses a transit gateway peering connection to link the new `eu-west-1` resources with an existing environment in the `us-east-1` Region.  
  
The hub-and-spoke design in each AWS Region contains an inspection VPC that uses AWS Network Firewall to centralize traffic inspection for that Region. To lower costs, the engineer chooses to inspect inter-Region traffic by using the inspection VPC in the traffic-originating Region. The engineer configures the transit gateway route tables accordingly in each Region.  
  
When testing the new design, communication inside each Region works as expected. However, inter-Region communication does not work. The network engineer must resolve the inter-Region communication problem.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Configure Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing on the transit gateway peering connection to propagate the VPC CIDR blocks from each Region to the remote peer.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share access between the transit gateways. Enable the Allow sharing with anyone setting.
Prevent asymmetric routing in the inspection VPCs by ensuring that both requests and responses are inspected by the same inspection VPC
Enable Appliance mode on both the transit gateway attachments for the inspection VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall is stateful and requires symmetric traffic flow. Enabling appliance mode on each inspection VPC’s Transit Gateway attachment keeps a flow pinned to the same Availability Zone and Network Firewall endpoint for both directions, preventing stateful inspection from dropping inter-Region traffic. Transit Gateway peering relies on static routing and does not use OSPF.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateway attachment configuration for AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/vpc-config-tgw-multi-az.html) · [Avoiding asymmetric routing with AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/asymmetric-routing.html)

A real estate company uses Amazon WorkSpaces to deliver a corporately managed desktop service to real estate agents worldwide. These WorkSpaces are deployed across seven VPCs, with each VPC located in a different AWS Region.  
  
Under a new requirement, the company’s cloud-hosted security information and event management (SIEM) system must analyze DNS queries generated by the WorkSpaces to identify the target domains to which the WorkSpaces connect. The SIEM system supports both polling and push methods for collecting data and logs.  
  
Which solution should a network engineer implement to meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create VPC flow logs in each VPC that is connected to the Workspaces instances. Publish the log data to a central Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the SIEM system to poll the S3 bucket periodically.

Configure an Amazon CloudWatch agent to log all DNS requests in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure a subscription filter in CloudWatch Logs. Push the logs to the SIEM system by using Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
Configure VPC Traffic Mirroring to copy network traffic from each Workspace and to send the traffic to the SIEM system probes for analysis.
Configure Amazon Route 53 query logging. Set the destination as an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that is configured to push data to the SIEM system.

questions.explanation:
Route 53 Resolver query logging captures DNS queries originating in specified VPCs, including the requested DNS name. It can send those logs directly to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream, allowing push-based delivery to the SIEM without deploying agents or mirroring all network traffic. Resolver query logging must be configured in each Region that contains VPCs to be logged.

**Learn more:** [Resolver query logging - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-query-logs.html) · [Managing Resolver query logging configurations - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-query-logging-configurations-managing.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must temporarily scale out an on-premises application by deploying new servers on Amazon EC2 instances. A network engineer needs to design the networking solution for connectivity and for the application on AWS.  
  
The EC2 instances must share data with the existing servers in the on-premises data center. The servers must not be reachable from the internet. All internet traffic must be routed through the firewall in the on-premises data center. The servers must be able to access a third-party web application.  
  
Which configuration meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a VPC that has public subnets and private subnets. Create a customer gateway, a virtual private gateway, and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Create a NAT gateway in a public subnet. Create a route table, and associate the public subnets with the route table. Add a default route to the internet gateway. Create a route table, and associate the private subnets with the route table. Add a default route to the NAT gateway. Add routes for the data center subnets to the virtual private gateway. Deploy the application to the private subnets.

Create a VPC that has private subnets. Create a customer gateway, a virtual private gateway, and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Create a route table, and associate the private subnets with the route table. Add a default route to the virtual private gateway. Deploy the application to the private subnets.

Create a VPC that has public subnets. Create a customer gateway, a virtual private gateway, and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Create a route table, and associate the public subnets with the route table. Add a default route to the internet gateway. Add routes for the on-premises data center subnets to the virtual private gateway. Deploy the application to the public subnets.

Create a VPC that has public subnets and private subnets. Create a customer gateway, a virtual private gateway, and an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Create a route table, and associate the public subnets with the route table. Add a default route to the internet gateway. Create a route table, and associate the private subnets with the route table. Add routes for the on-premises data center subnets to the virtual private gateway. Deploy the application to the private subnets.

questions.explanation:
A private-subnet VPC connected to the on-premises network through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN lets the EC2 instances communicate privately with the data center. A default route to the virtual private gateway sends all nonlocal traffic, including traffic to the third-party web application, across the VPN to the on-premises firewall for internet egress and policy enforcement. With no internet gateway or NAT gateway route, the instances are not directly accessible from, or routed directly to, the internet.

**Learn more:** [Subnet route tables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/subnet-route-tables.html) · [Example routing options for Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/route-table-options.html)

The application's front end will identify which user is requesting access and will route traffic to 1 of 10 services VPCs. Each services VPC will contain an NLB that distributes traffic to the service pods in an EKS cluster."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company is concerned about overall cost. User traffic will account for more than 10 TB of data transfer from the ingress VPC to services VPCs each month. A network engineer must recommend a design for communication between the VPCs."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution meets these requirements at the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LOWEST"}]," cost?"]}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a transit gateway. Peer each VPC to the transit gateway. Use zonal DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs to minimize cross-AZ traffic from the ingress VPC to the services VPCs.","B":"Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint in every Availability Zone in the ingress VPC. Each PrivateLink endpoint will point to the zonal DNS entry of the NLB in the services VPCs.","C":"Create a VPC peering connection between the ingress VPC and each of the 10 services VPCs. Use zonal DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs to minimize cross-AZ traffic from the ingress VPC to the services VPCs.","D":"Create a transit gateway. Peer each VPC to the transit gateway. Turn off cross-AZ load balancing on the transit gateway. Use Regional DNS names for the NLB in the services VPCs."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"VPC peering has no charge to create the connection, and traffic sent over a peering connection within the same Availability Zone is free. Direct peering between the ingress VPC and each services VPC, combined with the services NLB zonal DNS records, minimizes cross-AZ transfer and avoids the per-GB data-processing and attachment charges incurred by AWS Transit Gateway or the endpoint charges incurred by AWS PrivateLink.

**Learn more:** [What is VPC peering?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/what-is-vpc-peering.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/transit-gateway/pricing/)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"ac062ea3-03bb-490c-9e5d-ca7df10477c1","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The hub-and-spoke design in each AWS Region contains an inspection VPC that uses AWS Network Firewall to centralize traffic inspection for that Region. ",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Configure Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) routing on the transit gateway peering connection to propagate the VPC CIDR blocks from each Region to the remote peer.","B":"Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share access between the transit gateways. Enabling appliance mode on each inspection VPC’s Transit Gateway attachment keeps a flow pinned to the same Availability Zone and Network Firewall endpoint for both directions, preventing stateful inspection from dropping inter-Region traffic. Transit Gateway peering relies on static routing and does not use OSPF.

A company has recently experienced an IP address exhaustion event in its VPCs. The event affected service capacity. The VPCs contain two or more subnets across different Availability Zones.  
  
A network engineer must develop a solution to monitor IP address usage across resources in the VPCs. The company must receive notifications about potential issues so that it can take action before an incident occurs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) with a new top-level pool. In the top-level pool, create a pool for each VPC. In each VPC pool, create a pool for each subnet in that VPC. Turn on the auto-import option for the VPC pools and the subnet pools. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the availability limit threshold is reached.

Set up a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for each subnet. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads each subnet's IP address usage and publishes metrics to the log group. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the availability limit threshold is reached.

Set up a custom Amazon CloudWatch metric for IP address usage for each subnet. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads each subnet's IP address usage and publishes a CloudWatch metric dimension. Schedule the Lambda function to run every 5 minutes. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the availability limit threshold is reached.

Set up Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) with a new top-level pool. In the top-level pool, create a pool for each VPC. In each VPC pool, create a pool for each subnet in that VPC. Turn on the auto-import option for the VPC pools and the subnet pools. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that monitors each pool availability limit threshold and sends an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification if the limit threshold is reached.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC IPAM automatically monitors IP address utilization for VPCs and subnets and publishes IPAM metrics in the `AWS/IPAM` CloudWatch namespace. Automatically importing the VPC and subnet CIDRs into IPAM pools enables managed monitoring without custom polling code. CloudWatch alarms can evaluate IPAM availability or utilization metrics and invoke Amazon SNS notifications when the configured threshold is reached.

**Learn more:** [IPAM resource utilization metrics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/ipam/cloudwatch-ipam-res-util.html) · [IPAM metrics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/ipam/cloudwatch-ipam-ip-address-usage.html)

A network engineer must enhance the network security of an existing AWS environment by adding an AWS Network Firewall firewall to control internet-bound traffic. The AWS environment contains five VPCs. Each VPC includes an internet gateway, NAT gateways, public Application Load Balancers (ALBs), and Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are deployed in private subnets. The architecture spans two Availability Zones.  
  
The network engineer must be able to configure rules for the public IP addresses in the environment, irrespective of traffic direction. The network engineer must add the firewall by implementing a solution that minimizes changes to the existing production environment. The solution must also provide high availability.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a centralized inspection VPC with subnets in two Availability Zones. Deploy Network Firewall in this inspection VPC with an endpoint in each Availability Zone.
Configure new subnets in two Availability Zones in each VPC. Deploy Network Firewall in each VPC with an endpoint in each Availability Zone.
Deploy Network Firewall in each VPUse existing subnets in each of the two Availability Zones to deploy Network Firewall endpoints.
Update the route tables that are associated with the private subnets that host the EC2 instances. Add routes to the Network Firewall endpoints.
Update the route tables that are associated with the public subnets that host the NAT gateways and the ALBs. Add routes to the Network Firewall endpoints.

questions.explanation:
A centralized inspection VPC provides a single location for Network Firewall inspection rather than requiring firewall deployment in every production VPC. Firewall endpoints in both Availability Zones provide availability across the two-zone architecture. Routing the public subnets that contain the NAT gateways and public ALBs through the firewall endpoints places public-facing ingress and egress traffic on the inspection path. Network Firewall stateful processing requires the forward and return traffic of a flow to traverse the firewall endpoint symmetrically.

**Learn more:** [Avoiding asymmetric routing with AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/asymmetric-routing.html) · [Infrastructure OU – Network account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/network.html)
