A company has multiple production applications in different AWS Cloud accounts. The company operates only in the us-east-1 Region. Only specified partner companies may access the applications. The applications run on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances are in private subnets and permit traffic only from the ALB. The ALB is in a public subnet and permits inbound traffic only from partner-network IP address ranges on port 80.  
  
When the company adds a partner, it must allow that partner network's IP address range in the security group associated with the ALB in every account. A network engineer must implement a solution to centrally manage the partner-network IP address ranges.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?

options.text: Create an Amazon DynamoDB table to maintain all IP address ranges and security groups that need to be updated. Update the DynamoDB table with the new IP address range when the company adds a new partner. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to read new IP address ranges and security groups from the DynamoDB table to update the security groups. Deploy this solution in all accounts.

Create a new prefix list. Add all allowed IP address ranges to the prefix list. Use Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rules to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update security groups whenever a new IP address range is added to the prefix list. Deploy this solution in all accounts.

Create a new prefix list. Add all allowed IP address ranges to the prefix list. Share the prefix list across different accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Update security groups to use the prefix list instead of the partner IP address range. Update the prefix list with the new IP address range when the company adds a new partner.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket to maintain all IP address ranges and security groups that need to be updated. Update the S3 bucket with the new IP address range when the company adds a new partner. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to read new IP address ranges and security groups from the S3 bucket to update the security groups. Deploy this solution in all accounts.

questions.explanation:
A customer-managed prefix list centrally groups the permitted partner CIDR ranges and can be used as the source of an inbound security-group rule. Sharing the prefix list through AWS Resource Access Manager lets other accounts reference the same list in their own security groups. Updates to the prefix list apply to every security group that references it, eliminating separate per-account data stores, Lambda functions, and security-group update workflows.

**Learn more:** [Consolidate and manage network CIDR blocks with managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/managed-prefix-lists.html) · [Share customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-managed-prefix-lists.html)

A company operates two AWS Direct Connect links. One Direct Connect link terminates in the `us-east-1` Region, and the other terminates in the `af-south-1` Region. The company uses BGP to exchange routes with AWS.  
  
How should a network engineer configure BGP so that `af-south-1` serves as the secondary link to AWS?

options.text: • On the Direct Connect link to us-east-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7100• On the Direct Connect link to af-south-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7300• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to us-east-1, set the local preference value to 200• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to af-south-1, set the local preference value to 50

• On the Direct Connect link to us-east-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7300• On the Direct Connect link to af-south-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7100• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to us-east-1, set the local preference value to 200• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to af-south-1, set the local preference value to 50

• On the Direct Connect link to us-east-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7100• On the Direct Connect link to af-south-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7300• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to us-east-1, set the local preference value to 50• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to af-south-1, set the local preference value to 200

• On the Direct Connect link to us-east-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7300• On the Direct Connect link to af-south-1, configure BGP peering to use community tag 7224:7100• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to us-east-1, set the local preference value to 50• On the Direct Connect BGP peer to af-south-1, set the local preference value to 200

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect uses BGP community `7224:7300` for high route preference and `7224:7100` for low route preference. An active/passive design therefore assigns `7224:7300` to the primary `us-east-1` virtual interface and `7224:7100` to the passive `af-south-1` virtual interface. Customer-side BGP local preference should likewise be higher for `us-east-1` (200) than for `af-south-1` (50), causing the primary path to be selected while the secondary path remains available for failover.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html)

Which traffic-flow sequence from a spoke VPC to the internet is correct?

A network engineer uses AWS Direct Connect connections and MACsec to encrypt data from a corporate data center to the Direct Connect location. The network engineer discovers that the MACsec secret key could have been compromised. The network engineer must update the connection with an uncompromised secure key.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Create a new MACsec secret key that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key. Associate the new pre-shared key, Connection Key Name (CKN), and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) with the connection.

Create a new MACsec secret key that uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. Associate the new pre-shared key, Connection Key Name (CKN), and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) with the connection.
Modify the existing MACsec secret key. Re-associate the existing pre-shared key, Connection Key Name (CKN), and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) with the connection.
Modify the existing MACsec secret key. Associate the new pre-shared key, Connection Key Name (CKN), and Connectivity Association Key (CAK) with the connection.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect encrypts MACsec pre-shared keys associated with connections by using AWS managed KMS keys. A MACsec secret key cannot be modified after it is associated with a connection; key rotation requires creation and association of a new CKN/CAK pair. [MAC Security in Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html) and [Associate a MACsec CKN/CAK with a Direct Connect connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/associate-key-connection.html).

**Learn more:** [MAC Security in Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html) · [Associate a MACsec CKN/CAK with a Direct Connect connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/associate-key-connection.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is rolling out a new stateless web application on AWS. The web application will run on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group. The web application includes a stateful management application for administration that will run on EC2 instances in a separate Auto Scaling group.  
  
The company wants to access the management application by using the same URL as the web application, with a `/management` path prefix. The protocol, hostname, and port number must remain the same for both the web application and the management application. Access to the management application must be limited to the company's on-premises IP address space. An SSL/TLS certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) will secure the web application.  
  
Which combination of steps should a network engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Insert a rule for the load balancer HTTPS listener. Configure the rule to check the path-pattern condition type for the /management prefix and to check the source-ip condition type for the on-premises IP address space. Forward requests to the management application target group if there is a match. Edit the management application target group and enable stickiness.

Modify the default rule for the load balancer HTTPS listener. Configure the rule to check the path-pattern condition type for the /management prefix and to check the source-ip condition type for the on-premises IP address space. Forward requests to the management application target group if there is not a match. Enable group-level stickiness in the rule attributes.

Insert a rule for the load balancer HTTPS listener. Configure the rule to check the path-pattern condition type for the /management prefix and to check the X-Forwarded-For HTTP header for the on-premises IP address space. Forward requests to the management application target group if there is a match. Enable group-level stickiness in the rule attributes.

Modify the default rule for the load balancer HTTPS listener. Configure the rule to check the path-pattern condition type for the /management prefix and to check the source-ip condition type for the on-premises IP address space. Forward requests to the web application target group if there is not a match.
Forward all requests to the web application target group. Edit the web application target group and disable stickiness.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer non-default listener rule can match both a path pattern and source IP CIDR, allowing only on-premises requests to `/management` to be forwarded to the management target group. Target-group stickiness keeps a stateful management session on the same target. The listener’s default action forwards all other requests to the stateless web target group, where stickiness is unnecessary and should be disabled. AWS documents that conditions such as `path-pattern` and `source-ip` are available on non-default listener rules, and that sticky sessions are enabled at the target-group level for applications that maintain state.

**Learn more:** [Condition types for listener rules - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-condition-types.html) · [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

Which combination of actions meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use ACM to create an SSL/TLS certificate in the us-east-1 Region for the new domain.
Set up latency-based routing in Amazon Route 53 for the new domain. Add the ALBs from all the Regions as targets.

questions.explanation:
A standard AWS Global Accelerator provides a single global entry point and routes traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal healthy Regional endpoint, reducing latency. Standard accelerators support Application Load Balancers as endpoints and TCP listeners. An Amazon Route 53 alias record can map the new domain to the accelerator's DNS name. ACM certificates are Regional resources, so an HTTPS-enabled ALB in each Region requires a certificate for the new domain in that same Region.

The company uses AWS Transit Gateway for inter-VPC connectivity across AWS accounts in a hub-and-spoke model. The network services team must manage all Amazon Route 53 zones and interface endpoints in a shared services AWS account. options.text: In the shared services account, create an interface endpoint for AWS KMS. Modify the interface endpoint by disabling the private DNS name. Create a private hosted zone in the shared services account with an alias record that points to the interface endpoint. Associate the private hosted zone with the spoke VPCs in each AWS account.

questions.explanation:

Configure VPC flow logs on each EC2 network interface. Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Create a third-party EC2 appliance. Configure a CloudWatch filter to send the flow logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to load the logs into the appliance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC Traffic Mirroring copies inbound and outbound traffic from EC2 elastic network interfaces to a traffic mirror target for monitoring and content inspection. A Network Load Balancer is a supported target and can distribute the mirrored traffic to a scalable, highly available fleet of third-party EC2 inspection appliances. VPC Flow Logs contain flow metadata rather than packet content, and Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is not a supported traffic mirror target.

A company maintains an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between its office and its VPC. Users report intermittent failures connecting to an application hosted within the VPC. A network engineer finds in the customer gateway logs that the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) session ends whenever the application connection fails.  
  
What should the network engineer do to bring the IKE session up if it goes down?

options.text: Set the dead peer detection (DPD) timeout action to Clear. Initiate traffic from the VPC to on premises.
Set the dead peer detection (DPD) timeout action to Restart. Initiate traffic from on premises to the VPC.
Set the dead peer detection (DPD) timeout action to None. Initiate traffic from the VPC to on premises.
Set the dead peer detection (DPD) timeout action to Cancel. Initiate traffic from on premises to the VPC.

questions.explanation:
For an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection, the `Restart` dead peer detection (DPD) timeout action restarts the IKE session after a DPD timeout. By default, the customer gateway initiates IKE negotiation by generating traffic, so traffic must be initiated from the on-premises network to the VPC. AWS documents the supported DPD actions and the default customer-gateway initiation behavior.

**Learn more:** [AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel initiation options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/initiate-vpn-tunnels.html) · [Configure tunnel options for AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/tunnel-configure.html)

A network engineer must establish an AWS Direct Connect connection between the company’s on-premises data center and the transit gateway to migrate a workload.  
  
The Direct Connect connection is **UP** according to the `ConnectionState` metric in Amazon CloudWatch, but the VIF is **DOWN**. The network engineer has verified the transit VIF and BGP configurations on the on-premises router and found no issues. However, the network engineer cannot ping the Amazon peer IP address.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer perform to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose three.)

options.text: Verify that the correct IP address and subnet mask are in use for the subinterface on the router.
Ensure that VLAN trunking is disabled on the router.
Verify that the router has a MAC address entry from the AWS endpoint in the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) table.
Verify that the optical signal that is received over the cross connect is optimal.
Ensure that the correct VLAN tag is applied on the subinterface configuration on the router.
Ensure that TCP port 179 is not being blocked at the on-premises router.

questions.explanation:
With an UP Direct Connect physical connection, a DOWN virtual interface, and no reachability to the Amazon peer IP, troubleshooting must focus on Layer 2 connectivity. The peer IP address and subnet mask must be configured on the appropriate VLAN subinterface, the router should learn the AWS endpoint MAC address through ARP, and the subinterface must apply the configured 802.1Q VLAN tag. TCP port 179 troubleshooting is relevant only after peer-IP connectivity exists and BGP establishment is being diagnosed.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot layer 2 (data link) issues - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/ts-layer-2.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html)

A company’s network engineer is designing a hybrid DNS solution for an AWS Cloud workload. Individual teams want to manage DNS hostnames for their applications in the development environment. The solution must integrate the application-specific hostnames with the centrally managed DNS hostnames on the on-premises network, provide bidirectional name resolution, and minimize management overhead.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint.
Modify the DHCP options set by setting a custom DNS server value.
Use an Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint.
Create DNS proxy servers.
Create Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones.
Set up a zone transfer between Amazon Route 53 and the on-premises DNS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoints enable on-premises DNS resolvers to forward queries to AWS and resolve records in associated Route 53 private hosted zones. Outbound endpoints enable VPC Resolver to conditionally forward queries for centrally managed on-premises names to on-premises DNS resolvers. Private hosted zones provide managed private DNS namespaces for application-specific records, avoiding the operational overhead of self-managed DNS proxy servers.

**Learn more:** [Resolving DNS queries between VPCs and your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-DSN-queries-to-vpc.html) · [Working with private hosted zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/hosted-zones-private.html)

The company must connect both VPCs to one on-premises data center to test the application. The application needs up to 800 Mbps of throughput. A network engineer must establish connectivity between the VPCs and the on-premises data center.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Order a 2 Gbps Direct Connect connection for the data center. Configure a virtual private gateway in each VPC. Create a private VIF for each virtual private gateway, and associate the virtual private gateways with the Direct Connect connection. Configure static routes in the VPC route tables and in the data center router.

Create a private VIF for each virtual private gateway, and associate the virtual private gateways with the Direct Connect connection. Configure a customer gateway and a virtual private gateway in each VPConfigure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the data center and each VPConfigure static routes in each VPC route table to point to the subnets in the data center.

questions.explanation:
A standard AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel supports up to 1.25 Gbps, satisfying an 800 Mbps requirement. BGP dynamically exchanges on-premises routes with each virtual private gateway, enables route propagation, and provides liveness detection and failover support, reducing manual route administration compared with static routing. Direct Connect private virtual interfaces use BGP, not OSPF; moreover, multi-Region VPC connectivity through Direct Connect requires a Direct Connect gateway.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an application running on premises. It must communicate with an application running in a VPC on AWS. questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN Private IP VPN encrypts traffic over Direct Connect without using public IP addresses or the public internet. The company must capture complete metadata, including source and destination IP addresses and protocol type. The company must also capture every network traffic flow and any DROP or ALERT actions that the firewall performs on traffic it processes. The Network Firewall endpoints are deployed in the appropriate subnets, and the VPC route tables send traffic through the Network Firewall endpoints on the route to and from the internet.  
  
How should a network engineer configure the firewall to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create a firewall policy to ensure that traffic is processed by stateless or stateful rules according to needs. Select Amazon CloudWatch Logs as the destination for the flow logs.

Create a firewall policy to ensure that traffic is processed by stateless or stateful rules according to needs. Configure Network Firewall logging for alert logs and flow logs.Select a destination for logs separately for stateful and stateless engines.

Create a firewall policy to ensure that a stateful engine processes all the traffic. Configure Network Firewall logging for alert logs and flow logs. Select a destination for alert logs and flow logs.
Create a firewall policy to ensure that a stateful engine processes all the traffic. Configure VPC flow logs for the subnets that the firewall protects. Select a destination for the flow logs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall logging is available for traffic sent to the stateful rules engine. FLOW logs record all traffic received by that engine and provide detailed network-flow metadata. ALERT logs record traffic that matches stateful rules with `ALERT`, `DROP`, or `REJECT` actions. Sending all traffic to the stateful engine and configuring both FLOW and ALERT log destinations therefore captures the required flow information and firewall actions. [AWS Network Firewall logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-logging.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS Network Firewall logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-logging.html) · [Updating an AWS Network Firewall logging configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewall-update-logging-configuration.html)

options.text: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to detect inconsistencies between the desired security group configuration and the current security group configuration. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to remediate noncompliant security groups.

Configure Amazon GuardDuty to detect inconsistencies between the desired security group configuration and the current security group configuration. Configure AWS OpsWorks for Chef to remediate noncompliant security groups.

Configure an AWS Config rule to detect inconsistencies between the desired security group configuration and the current security group configuration. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to remediate noncompliant security groups.

questions.explanation:
AWS Config rules can evaluate security group configurations for compliance with the required configuration. AWS Config can associate remediation actions with those rules and use AWS Systems Manager Automation documents (runbooks) to automatically remediate noncompliant resources. Amazon GuardDuty detects security threats rather than configuration drift, while AWS OpsWorks for Chef is not the AWS Config rule-remediation integration.

A company is moving critical applications to AWS. It has multiple accounts and VPCs that connect through a transit gateway.  
  
A network engineer must design a solution to perform deep packet inspection on all traffic that exits a VPC network boundary. All inspected traffic and the actions taken on it must be logged in a central log account.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Create a central network VPC that includes an attachment to the transit gateway. Update the VPC and transit gateway route tables to support the new attachment. Deploy an AWS Gateway Load Balancer that is backed by third-party, next-generation firewall appliances to the central network VPC. Create a policy that contains the rules for deep packet inspection. Attach the policy to the firewall appliances. Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the central log account. Configure the firewall appliances to capture and save the network flow logs to the S3 bucket.

Create a central network VPC that includes an attachment to the transit gateway. Update the VPC and transit gateway route tables to support the new attachment. Deploy an AWS Application Load Balancer that is backed by third-party, next-generation firewall appliances to the central network VPC. Create a policy that contains the rules for deep packet inspection. Attach the policy to the firewall appliances. Create a syslog server in the central log account. Configure the firewall appliances to capture and save the network flow logs to the syslog server.

Deploy network ACLs and security groups to each VPAttach the security groups to active network interfaces. Associate the network ACLs with VPC subnets. Create rules for the network ACLs and security groups to allow only the required traffic flows between subnets and network interfaces. Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the central log account. Configure a VPC flow log that captures and saves all traffic flows to the S3 bucket.

Create a central log VPC and an attachment to the transit gateway. Update the VPC and transit gateway route tables to support the new attachment. Deploy an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB) that is backed by third-party, next-generation intrusion detection system (IDS) security appliances to the central VPC. Activate rules on the security appliances to monitor for intrusion signatures. For each network interface, create a VPC Traffic Mirroring session that sends the traffic to the central VPC's NLB.

questions.explanation:
AWS Gateway Load Balancer supports centralized, inline traffic inspection by routing transit gateway traffic through a scalable fleet of third-party virtual firewall appliances in an inspection VPC. Those next-generation firewalls can enforce deep-packet-inspection policies, and their logs can be delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket in a central log account. This centralizes enforcement and logging without configuring inspection individually in every VPC or on every network interface. [AWS: Using Gateway Load Balancer with Transit Gateway for centralized network security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/using-gwlb-with-tg-for-cns.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS: Using Gateway Load Balancer with Transit Gateway for centralized network security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/using-gwlb-with-tg-for-cns.html) · [AWS: Monitor your Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/monitoring.html)

A company uses a shared services VPC containing two domain controllers. The domain controllers run in the company’s private subnets. The company is deploying a new application into a new VPC in the account. The application will run on an Amazon EC2 for Windows Server instance in the new VPC. The instance must join the existing Windows domain supported by the domain controllers in the shared services VPC.  
  
A transit gateway is attached to both the shared services VPC and the new VPC. The company has updated the route tables for the transit gateway, the shared services VPC, and the new VPC. The security groups for the domain controllers and the instance have been updated to permit traffic only on the ports required for domain operations. The instance cannot join the domain hosted on the domain controllers.  
  
Which combination of actions will help identify the cause of this issue with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use AWS Network Manager to perform a route analysis for the transit gateway network. Specify the existing EC2 instance as the source. Specify the first domain controller as the destination. Repeat the route analysis for the second domain controller.
Use port mirroring with the existing EC2 instance as the source and another EC2 instance as the target to obtain packet captures of the connection attempts.
Review the VPC flow logs on the shared services VPC and the new VPC.
Issue a ping command from one of the domain controllers to the existing EC2 instance.
Ensure that route propagation is turned off on the shared services VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Manager Route Analyzer can validate the route through transit gateway route tables from the EC2 instance’s VPC attachment to each domain controller’s VPC attachment, helping isolate transit-gateway routing problems. It does not inspect security groups or network ACLs; VPC Flow Logs complement it by recording accepted and rejected IP traffic in both VPCs, exposing filtering failures on required domain-operation connections. These managed diagnostic capabilities require less operational effort than provisioning packet mirroring and capture analysis.

**Learn more:** [Route Analyzer for AWS Network Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/tgwnm/route-analyzer.html) · [Flow log records](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-log-records.html)

A company observes VPC flow log data indicating that some company traffic is being sent to malicious websites. The company identifies the Amazon EC2 instance sending the traffic to the malicious websites and finds that the application running on the instance is compromised.  
  
Similar security events have occurred multiple times at the company previously. For earlier security events, the company responded by blocking the malicious websites. The company requires a scalable solution to prevent similar security events in the future.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up an EC2 instance to run firewall software in the VPC. Route all traffic through the firewall EC2 instance. Maintain a list of known malicious websites on the firewall instance. Disable the source and destination checks for the firewall instance.
Set up an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the problematic EC2 instance. Enable AWS WAF on the EC2 instance.
Set up an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the problematic EC2 instance. Enable AWS WAF on the ALB.

Set up an Amazon Route 53 DNS Firewall rule group. Create a domain list that contains only the domains the application must communicate with to function. Add the domain list to the rule group. Associate the rule group with the VPC.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall filters outbound DNS queries for an associated VPC. A domain allowlist that contains only the application’s required domains creates a scalable walled-garden control, so a compromised workload cannot resolve unapproved or newly malicious destinations. It avoids operating a firewall instance and is appropriate for controlling outbound domain access; an ALB with AWS WAF protects inbound web requests rather than this outbound traffic pattern.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with Resolver DNS Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-dns-firewall-getting-started.html) · [Using DNS Firewall to filter outbound DNS traffic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-dns-firewall.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to build a service that requires encryption in transit. Traffic must remain encrypted without being decrypted anywhere between the client and the service backend. The company will implement the service by using the gRPC protocol over TCP port 443. The service will scale to thousands of concurrent connections. The service backend will run on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler and Horizontal Pod Autoscaler configured. The company must use mutual TLS for two-way authentication between the client and the backend.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Install the AWS Load Balancer Controller for Kubernetes. Using that controller, configure a Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on port 443 to forward traffic to the IP addresses of the backend service Pods.

Install the AWS Load Balancer Controller for Kubernetes. Using that controller, configure an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener on port 443 to forward traffic to the IP addresses of the backend service Pods.
Create a target group. Add the EKS managed node group's Auto Scaling group as a target Create an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener on port 443 to forward traffic to the target group.
Create a target group. Add the EKS managed node group’s Auto Scaling group as a target. Create a Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener on port 443 to forward traffic to the target group.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer TCP listener operates at Layer 4 and passes encrypted traffic through to its targets without decrypting it. This preserves the end-to-end TLS connection and allows mutual TLS authentication directly between the client and the backend Pods. The AWS Load Balancer Controller supports Network Load Balancers with Pod IP targets, allowing the target set to track Pods as Kubernetes autoscaling changes capacity.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [Route TCP and UDP traffic with Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/network-load-balancing.html)

A company plans to migrate an internal application to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances in a single VPC. Users will reach the application from the company’s on-premises data center by using AWS VPN or AWS Direct Connect. Users will use private domain names for the application endpoint from a domain name that is explicitly reserved for use in the AWS Cloud.  
  
Each EC2 instance must automatically fail over to another EC2 instance in the same AWS account and VPC. A network engineer must design a DNS solution that does not expose the application to the internet.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Assign public IP addresses to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the AWS reserved domain name. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. Configure conditional forwarding in the on-premises DNS resolvers to forward all DNS queries for the AWS domain to the outbound endpoint IP address for Route 53 Resolver. In the private hosted zone, configure primary and failover records that point to the public IP addresses of the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric and alarm to monitor the application's health. Set up a health check on the alarm for the primary application endpoint.

Configure conditional forwarding in the on-premises DNS resolvers to forward all DNS queries for the AWS domain to the inbound endpoint IP address for Route 53 Resolver. In the public hosted zone, configure primary and failover records that point to the IP addresses of the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric and alarm to monitor the application's health. Set up a health check on the alarm for the primary application endpoint.

Place the EC2 instances in private subnets. Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the AWS reserved domain name. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPCreate a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. In the private hosted zone, configure primary and failover records that point to the IP addresses of the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric and alarm to monitor the application's health. Set up a health check on the alarm for the primary application endpoint.

Place the EC2 instances in private subnets. Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the AWS reserved domain name. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. Configure conditional forwarding in the on-premises DNS resolvers to forward all DNS queries for the AWS domain to the inbound endpoint IP address for Route 53 Resolver. In the private hosted zone, configure primary and failover records that point to the IP addresses of the EC2 instances. Set up Route 53 health checks on the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 private hosted zone associated with the VPC keeps the application DNS namespace private, and a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint lets on-premises DNS resolvers forward queries for that namespace over VPN or Direct Connect. Route 53 health checkers are outside the VPC and cannot directly health-check private IP endpoints. For EC2 instances that have only private IP addresses, a CloudWatch metric and alarm can provide the health signal for a Route 53 health check, enabling primary/failover DNS records without internet exposure.

**Learn more:** [Configuring failover in a private hosted zone](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-private-hosted-zones.html) · [Forwarding inbound DNS queries to your VPCs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-inbound-queries.html)

An online retail company runs a web application in the `us-wast-2` Region and serves consumers in the United States. The company plans to expand into several European countries and wants to deliver low latency to all users.  
  
The application must identify users’ IP addresses and deliver localized content according to users’ geographic location. It uses HTTP `GET` and `POST` methods for its functionality. The company must also create a health-check-based failover mechanism that works for both `GET` and `POST` methods. Failover must occur in less than 1 minute for all clients.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure a Network Load Balancer (NLB) for the application in each environment in the new AWS Regions. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator that has endpoint groups that point to the NLBs in each Region.

Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the application in each environment in the new AWS Regions. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator that has endpoint groups that point to the ALBs in each Region.
Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the application in each environment in the new AWS Regions. Create Amazon Route 53 public hosted zones that have failover routing policies.

Configure a Network Load Balancer (NLB) for the application in each environment in the new AWS Regions. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure an origin group with origin failover options.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS global network to healthy regional Application Load Balancer endpoints, providing low-latency routing and health-based cross-Region failover. An Application Load Balancer endpoint preserves the originating client IP for the web tier in the `X-Forwarded-For` header, and ALB supports HTTP GET and POST traffic. CloudFront origin failover does not fail over POST requests, while DNS-based Route 53 failover is subject to resolver caching and therefore cannot guarantee sub-minute client failover.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [How the client IP address is preserved in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/preserve-client-ip-address.headers.html)

A network engineer must deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall in an existing AWS environment. The environment includes the following:  
  
- A transit gateway to which all VPCs are attached  
- Several hundred application VPCs  
- A centralized egress internet VPC containing a NAT gateway and an internet gateway  
- A centralized ingress internet VPC that hosts public Application Load Balancers  
- On-premises connectivity by way of an AWS Direct Connect gateway attachment  
  
The application VPCs contain workloads across multiple Availability Zones in private subnets, with the VPC route tables’ default route (`0.0.0.0/0`) directed to the transit gateway. The Network Firewall firewall must inspect east-west (VPC-to-VPC) traffic and north-south (internet-bound and on-premises network) traffic by using Suricata-compatible rules.  
  
The network engineer must deploy the firewall with a solution that makes the fewest possible architectural changes to the existing production environment.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy Network Firewall in all Availability Zones in each application VPC.
Deploy Network Firewall in all Availability Zones in a centralized inspection VPC.
Update the HOME_NET rule group variable to include all CIDR ranges of the VPCs and on-premises networks.
Update the EXTERNAL_NET rule group variable to include all CIDR ranges of the VPCs and on-premises networks.
Configure a single transit gateway route table. Associate all application VPCs and the centralized inspection VPC with this route table.
Configure two transit gateway route tables. Associate all application VPCs with one transit gateway route table. Associate the centralized inspection VPC with the other transit gateway route table.

questions.explanation:
A centralized inspection VPC provides scalable inspection without adding Network Firewall endpoints to every application VPC. In a centralized deployment, `HOME_NET` must be overridden to include the protected application-VPC and on-premises CIDR ranges; `EXTERNAL_NET` is derived as the complement of `HOME_NET`. Two Transit Gateway route tables separate the application-VPC attachments from the inspection-VPC attachment so traffic is directed through the firewall and return traffic can be routed symmetrically, rather than allowing direct attachment-to-attachment paths.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshooting rules in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/troubleshooting-rules.html) · [Avoiding asymmetric routing with AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/asymmetric-routing.html)

A company is migrating an application to the AWS Cloud. The company has successfully provisioned and tested connectivity between AWS Direct Connect and the company’s on-premises data center. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The instances are part of an Auto Scaling group.  
  
The application uses HTTPS to communicate with a third-party vendor’s data service hosted in the company’s data center. The data service enforces a static ACL by explicitly allow-listing client IP addresses.  
  
A network engineer must design a network solution so the migrated application can continue accessing the vendor’s data service as the application scales.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** ongoing change to the vendor’s allow list?

options.text: Configure a private NAT gateway in the subnets for each Availability Zone that the application runs in. Configure the application to target the NAT gateways instead of the data service directly. Update the data service's allow list to include the IP addresses of the NAT gateways.

Configure an elastic network interface in the subnets for each Availability Zone that the application runs in. Associate the elastic network interfaces with the Auto Scaling group for the application. Update the data service's allow list to include the IP addresses of the elastic network interfaces.

Configure an elastic network interface in the subnets for each Availability Zone that the application runs in. Launch an EC2 instance into each subnet. Attach the respective elastic network interfaces to the new EC2 instances. In the application subnet route tables, configure the new EC2 instances as the next destination for the data service. Update the data service’s allow list to include the IP addresses of the elastic network interfaces.

Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the subnets for each Availability Zone that the application runs in. Configure an ALB-associated target group that contains a target that uses the IP address for the data service. Configure the application to target the ALB instead of the data service directly. Update the data service's allow list to include the IP addresses of the ALBs.

questions.explanation:
A private NAT gateway can route VPC traffic to an on-premises network and replaces each instance’s source address with the NAT gateway’s private IP address. Allow-listing the fixed NAT gateway IP addresses therefore supports a changing Auto Scaling fleet without updating the ACL for individual EC2 instances.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateway use cases – Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html) · [Connect to the internet or other networks using NAT devices – Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat.html)

A company operates multiple AWS accounts and VPCs within one AWS Region. The company needs to log all network traffic for Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS databases. It will use the log data to monitor and identify traffic flows during a security incident. The information must be retained for 12 months, but it will be accessed infrequently after the first 90 days. The company must be able to view metadata that includes the following fields:  
  
- `vpc-id`  
- `subnet-id`  
- `tcp-flags`  
  
Which solution meets these requirements at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Configure VPC flow logs with the default fields Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Configure Traffic Mirroring on all AWS resources to point to a Network Load Balancer that will send the mirrored traffic to monitoring instances.
Configure VPC flow logs with additional custom format fields Store the logs in Amazon S3.
Configure VPC flow logs with additional custom format fields Store the logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC Flow Logs can record IP traffic for VPC resources, including Amazon RDS network interfaces. The `vpc-id`, `subnet-id`, and `tcp-flags` fields require a custom flow-log format because they are not all present in the default version 2 format. Delivering those custom records to Amazon S3 provides lower-cost long-term storage than CloudWatch Logs and supports lifecycle transitions for data that becomes infrequently accessed after 90 days.

**Learn more:** [Flow log records - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-log-records.html) · [Flow logs basics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-basics.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to host a secure web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances. The application will have an associated DNS domain in an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone.  
  
The company wants to safeguard the domain against DNS poisoning attacks. The company also wants web browsers to authenticate to the application by using a trusted third party.  
  
Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure the Route 53 hosted zone to use DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC). Install self-signed X.509 certificates on the EC2 instances.
Configure a Name Authority Pointer (NAPTR) record in the Route 53 hosted zone. Install X 509 certificates that are signed by a public certificate authority on the EC2 instances.
Configure the Route 53 hosted zone to use DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC). Install X.509 certificates that are signed by a public certificate authority on the EC2 instances.
Configure a Name Authority Pointer (NAPTR) record in the Route 53 hosted zone. Install self-signed X.509 certificates on the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
DNSSEC signing enables DNS resolvers to validate that hosted-zone responses originate from Route 53 and have not been modified, which protects against DNS spoofing and poisoning. A publicly trusted certificate authority–signed X.509 certificate allows browsers to validate the website identity through their trusted CA roots; self-signed certificates do not provide that third-party trust.

**Learn more:** [Configuring DNSSEC signing in Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec.html) · [AWS Certificate Manager concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/acm-concepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A team of infrastructure engineers needs to automate deployment of Application Load Balancer (ALB) components by using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). The CDK application must deploy an infrastructure stack that remains reusable and consistent across multiple environments, AWS Regions, and AWS accounts.  
  
The project’s lead network architect has already bootstrapped the target accounts. The lead network architect has also deployed core network components, including VPCs and Amazon Route 53 private hosted zones, across the multiple environments and Regions. The infrastructure engineers must design the ALB components in the CDK application to use the existing core network components.  
  
Which combination of steps meets this requirement with the **LEAST** manual effort between environment deployments? (Choose two.)

options.text: Design the CDK application to read AWS CloudFormation parameters for the values that vary across environments and Regions. Reference these variables in the CDK stack for resources that require the variables.

Design the CDK application to read environment variables that contain account and Region details at runtime. Use these variables as properties of the CDK stack. Use context methods in the CDK stack to retrieve variable values.

Create a dedicated account for shared application services in the multi-account environment. Deploy a CDK pipeline to the dedicated account. Create stages in the pipeline that deploy the CDK application across different environments and Regions.
Write a script that automates the deployment of the CDK application across multiple environments and Regions. Distribute the script to engineers who are working on the project.

questions.explanation:

A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center in the United States (US) and workloads in the us-east-1 Region. The connection uses a transit VIF to connect the data center to a transit gateway in us-east-1.  
  
The company is opening a new office in Europe with a new on-premises data center in England. A Direct Connect connection will connect the new data center to some workloads running in a single VPC in the eu-west-2 Region. The company must connect the US data center and us-east-1 with the Europe data center and eu-west-2. A network engineer must establish complete connectivity between the data centers and Regions with the lowest possible latency.  
  
How should the network engineer design the network architecture to meet these requirements?

options.text: Connect the VPC in eu-west-2 with the Europe data center by using a Direct Connect gateway and a private VIF. Associate the transit gateway in us-east-1 with the same Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink for the transit VIF and the private VIF.

Connect the VPC in eu-west-2 to a new transit gateway. Connect the Europe data center to the new transit gateway by using a Direct Connect gateway and a new transit VIF. Associate the transit gateway in us-east-1 with the same Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink for both transit VIFs. Peer the two transit gateways.

Connect the VPC in eu-west-2 to a new transit gateway. Connect the Europe data center to the new transit gateway by using a Direct Connect gateway and a new transit VIF. Create a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate the transit gateway in us-east-1 with the new Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink for both transit VIFs. Peer the two transit gateways.

Connect the VPC in eu-west-2 with the Europe data center by using a Direct Connect gateway and a private VIF. Create a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate the transit gateway in us-east-1 with the new Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink for the transit VIF and the private VIF.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect gateway supports transit VIFs and associations with transit gateways in multiple Regions. When both on-premises connections use transit VIFs attached to that same Direct Connect gateway, SiteLink routes traffic directly between the Direct Connect points of presence over the shortest available AWS-network path, minimizing data-center-to-data-center latency. A transit gateway in eu-west-2 connects the European VPC, and inter-Region transit gateway peering supplies connectivity between the Regional transit-gateway domains. A Direct Connect gateway cannot be associated with a transit gateway when it is already associated with a virtual private gateway or attached to a private VIF.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html)

The company now requires firewall inspection of all internet traffic before that traffic reaches any EC2 instances. A security engineer has deployed and configured a Gateway Load Balancer (GLB) in a standalone VPC containing a fleet of third-party firewalls.  
  
How should a network engineer update the environment so that traffic passes through the firewall fleet?

options.text: Deploy a transit gateway. Attach a GLB endpoint to the transit gateway. Attach the application VPC to the transit gateway. Update the application subnet route table's default route destination to be the GLB endpoint. Ensure that the EC2 instances' security group allows traffic from the GLB endpoint.

Ensure that the EC2 instances' security group allows traffic from the GLB.

questions.explanation:

A company has two business units (BUs). It operates in the us-east-1 Region and the us-west-1 Region, and plans to expand into additional Regions in the future. Each BU has a VPC in each Region. Each Region contains a transit gateway with the BU VPCs attached, and the transit gateways in the two Regions are peered.  
  
The company will add several more BUs in the future and must isolate some BUs from the others. It wants to migrate to an architecture that supports additional Regions and BUs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Create a new transit gateway for each new BU in each Region. Peer the new transit gateways with the existing transit gateways. Update the route tables to control traffic between BUs.

Create an AWS Cloud WAN core network with an edge location in both Regions. Configure a segment for each BU with VPC attachments to the new BU VPCs. Use segment actions to control traffic between segments.

Create an AWS Cloud WAN core network with an edge location in both Regions. Configure a segment for each BU with VPC attachments to the new BU VPCs. Configure the segments to isolate attachments to control traffic between segments.
Attach new VPCs to the existing transit gateways. Update route tables to control traffic between BUs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cloud WAN provides a centrally managed, multi-Region core network whose edge locations can be expanded as needed. Each BU can use its own Cloud WAN segment, which is a separate routing domain. Attachments in different segments cannot communicate by default, while segment actions selectively share routes only between BUs that require connectivity. This provides scalable, globally consistent segmentation without maintaining transit gateway peering and route-table rules for every BU and Region. `isolate-attachments` is not appropriate because it also prevents attachments within the same segment from communicating.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Cloud WAN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/what-is-cloudwan.html) · [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html)

A company's development team has built a new product-recommendation web service. The web service runs in a VPC with CIDR block `192.168.224.0/19`. The company deployed the web service on Amazon EC2 instances and configured an Auto Scaling group as the target of a Network Load Balancer (NLB).  
  
The company wants to test whether users who receive product recommendations spend more money than users who do not receive product recommendations. The company has a major sales event in 5 days and must integrate its existing production environment with the recommendation engine by that time. The existing production environment runs in a VPC with CIDR block `192.168.128 0/17`.  
  
A network engineer must integrate the systems by designing a solution that causes the least possible disruption to the existing environments.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the web service VPC and the existing production VPC. Add a routing rule to the appropriate route table to allow data to flow to 192.168.224.0/19 from the existing production environment and to flow to 192.168.128.0/17 from the web service environment. Configure the relevant security groups and ACLs to allow the systems to communicate.
Ask the development team of the web service to redeploy the web service into the production VPC and integrate the systems there.
Create a VPC endpoint service. Associate the VPC endpoint service with the NLB for the web service. Create an interface VPC endpoint for the web service in the existing production VPC.

Create a transit gateway in the existing production environment. Create attachments to the production VPC and the web service VPC. Configure appropriate routing rules in the transit gateway and VPC route tables for 192.168.224.0/19 and 192.168.128.0/17. Configure the relevant security groups and ACLs to allow the systems to communicate.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink can publish an application behind a Network Load Balancer as a VPC endpoint service and expose it to consumers through interface VPC endpoints. It does not require VPC-to-VPC routing and supports connectivity when the provider and consumer VPCs have overlapping IP address ranges. The production VPC's `/17` range encompasses the recommendation VPC's `/19` range, preventing routing-based peering or transit-gateway connectivity between them.

A company uses AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections to encrypt traffic between the company's on-premises location and a single VPC. The Site-to-Site VPN connections use two 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections with public VIFs. The company intends to add 15 additional VPCs in the same AWS Region.  
  
The company must preserve the same encryption level that the current Site-to-Site VPN connections provide for every connection between the on-premises location and the new VPCs. The new connections must not use public IP addresses. Site-to-Site VPN bandwidth will remain below the currently provisioned speed.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a transit gateway and a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the transit gateway with the Direct Connect gateway. Attach all the new VPCs to the transit gateway.
For each new VPC, create a new Direct Connect private VIF to a Direct Connect gateway. Associate all VPCs with the Direct Connect gateway.
Assign a private IP CIDR block to the transit gateway.
Assign a public IP CIDR block to the transit gateway.
Create a transit VIF to the Direct Connect gateway. Create a Site-to-Site VPN private IP VPN connection.
Create a public VICreate a Site-to-Site VPN public IP VPN connection.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site Private IP VPN over Direct Connect provides IPsec encryption without public IP addresses. It uses a transit VIF connected through a Direct Connect gateway associated with a transit gateway. The private IP VPN attaches to the transit gateway, whose private CIDR block supplies the private VPN endpoint addressing, and the additional VPCs attach to that transit gateway for centralized connectivity and lower operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Private IP AWS Site-to-Site VPN with Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/private-ip-dx.html) · [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has extended its network into the AWS Cloud by using a hybrid architecture with multiple AWS accounts. The company has configured a shared AWS account for connectivity to its on-premises data centers and company offices. The workloads are private, web-based services for internal use. These services operate in separate AWS accounts. Office employees use these services through a DNS name in an on-premises DNS zone named `example.internal`.  
  
Registering a new service that runs on AWS currently requires a manual, complex change request to the internal DNS. The process involves multiple teams.  
  
The company wants to improve the DNS-registration process by giving service creators access that enables them to register their DNS records. A network engineer must design a solution that meets this objective. The solution must maximize cost-effectiveness and require the fewest possible configuration changes.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a record for each service in its local private hosted zone (serviceA.account1.aws.example.internal). Provide this DNS record to the employees who need access.

Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the shared account VPC. Create a conditional forwarder for a domain named aws.example.internal on the on-premises DNS servers. Set the forwarding IP addresses to the inbound endpoint's IP addresses that were created.
Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver rule to forward any queries made to onprem.example.internal to the on-premises DNS servers.
Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone named aws.example.internal in the shared AWS account to resolve queries for this domain.

Launch two Amazon EC2 instances in the shared AWS account. Install BIND on each instance. Create a DNS conditional forwarder on each BIND server to forward queries for each subdomain under aws.example.internal to the appropriate private hosted zone in each AWS account. Create a conditional forwarder for a domain named aws.example.internal on the on-premises DNS servers. Set the forwarding IP addresses to the IP addresses of the BIND servers.

Create a private hosted zone in the shared AWS account for each account that runs the service. Configure the private hosted zone to contain aws.example.internal in the domain (account1.aws.example.internal). Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC that runs the service and the shared account VPC.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint enables on-premises DNS resolvers to conditionally forward queries for the AWS subdomain to the VPC Resolver. Private hosted zones associated with the VPC that contains the inbound endpoint can answer those queries. Using a shared `aws.example.internal` namespace with separate account-specific private hosted zones, each associated with its workload VPC and the shared VPC, provides isolated DNS-record administration for service teams while avoiding self-managed BIND servers and unnecessary outbound forwarding.

**Learn more:** [Forwarding inbound DNS queries to your VPCs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-forwarding-inbound-queries.html) · [Considerations when creating inbound and outbound endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-choose-vpc.html)

A company has deployed a software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) solution to connect all of its offices. The company is moving workloads to AWS and must extend its SD-WAN solution to provide connectivity to those workloads.  
  
A network engineer plans to deploy AWS Transit Gateway Connect and two SD-WAN virtual appliances to provide this connectivity. Company policy requires that only one SD-WAN virtual appliance handle traffic from AWS workloads at any given time.  
  
How should the network engineer configure routing to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Add a static default route in the transit gateway route table to point to the secondary SD-WAN virtual appliance. Add routes that are more specific to point to the primary SD-WAN virtual appliance.
Configure the BGP community tag 7224:7300 on the primary SD-WAN virtual appliance for BGP routes toward the transit gateway.
Configure the AS_PATH prepend attribute on the secondary SD-WAN virtual appliance for BGP routes toward the transit gateway.
Disable equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing on the transit gateway for Transit Gateway Connect.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway Connect dynamically learns routes through BGP and selects between two Connect peers using the BGP AS_PATH attribute. AS_PATH prepending on the secondary appliance makes its advertised routes less preferred than the primary appliance’s routes, creating an active/standby design in which the secondary can take over if the primary route is withdrawn. Connect attachments do not support static routes, and their ECMP support is automatic rather than a configurable disable option.

**Learn more:** [Connect attachments and Connect peers in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-connect.html) · [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company’s network engineer is designing an active-passive connection to AWS from two on-premises data centers. The company has established AWS Direct Connect connections between the on-premises data centers and AWS. From each location, the company uses a transit VIF connected to a Direct Connect gateway that is associated with a transit gateway.  
  
The network engineer must ensure that traffic from AWS to the data centers is routed first to the primary data center. Traffic should be routed to the failover data center only if an outage occurs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the primary data center to 7224:7100. Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the failover data center to 7224:7300
Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the primary data center to 7224:7300. Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the failover data center to 7224:7100
Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the primary data center to 7224:9300. Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the failover data center to 7224:9100
Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the primary data center to 7224:9100. Set the BGP community tag for all prefixes from the failover data center to 7224:9300

questions.explanation:
For AWS Direct Connect private and transit virtual interfaces, BGP community `7224:7300` sets high local preference and `7224:7100` sets low local preference. Advertising the same prefixes with high preference from the primary data center and low preference from the failover data center makes AWS select the primary path, using the failover path only when the preferred path is unavailable.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A security company owns a domain with DNS records stored in an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone. The company has enabled Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) signing for the domain. The domain has no subdomains.  
  
A network engineer needs to disable DNSSEC signing for the domain without causing a DNS outage.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Disable DNSSEC signing. Delete the resource record signature (RRSIG) records. Wait for the TTL of the RSIG records to elapse. Deactivate the key-signing keys (KSKs).
Deactivate the key-signing keys (KSKs). Wait for the TTL of the KSK records to elapse. Disable DNSSEC signing.
Delete the designated signer (DS) record in the parent domain. Wait for the TTL of the DS record to elapse. Disable DNSSEC signing. Deactivate the key-signing keys (KSKs).
Deactivate the key-signing keys (KSKs). Delete the designated signer (DS) record of the domain. Wait for the TTL of the DS record to elapse. Disable DNSSEC signing.

questions.explanation:
A parent-zone DS record establishes the DNSSEC chain of trust. Removing that DS record and waiting for its TTL to expire ensures validating resolvers no longer expect signed responses from the hosted zone. DNSSEC signing can then be disabled and the KSK deactivated without causing validation failures. With no subdomains, no child-zone DS records must be removed.

**Learn more:** [Disabling DNSSEC signing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec-disable.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an AWS Direct Connect private VIF on a link aggregation group (LAG) comprising two 10 Gbps connections. The company’s security team has introduced a requirement that external network connections provide Layer 2 encryption. The network team intends to use Direct Connect MACsec support to satisfy this requirement.  
  
Which combination of actions should the network team perform to implement this capability? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new Direct Connect LAG with new circuits and ports that support MACsec.
Associate the MACsec Connectivity Association Key (CAK) and the Connection Key Name (CKN) with the new LAG.
Associate the Internet Key Exchange (IKE) with the existing LAG.
Configure the MACsec encryption mode on the existing LAG.
Configure the MACsec encryption mode on the new LAG.
Configure the MACsec encryption mode on each Direct Connect connection that makes up the existing LAG.

questions.explanation:
A MACsec-enabled Direct Connect LAG must consist of MACsec-capable dedicated connections of the same bandwidth. Create a new LAG with MACsec-capable circuits, associate its CKN/CAK key pair, and configure the MACsec encryption mode on that LAG. MACsec settings apply uniformly across the LAG’s member links; IKE is not part of MACsec setup.

**Learn more:** [MAC Security in Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html) · [Associate a MACsec CKN/CAK with a Direct Connect endpoint LAG](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/associate-key-lag.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a transit gateway in one AWS account and sends its transit gateway flow logs to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group.  
  
The company created an AWS Lambda function to analyze the logs. When a VPC produces traffic that the transit gateway drops, the Lambda function sends a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Each notification includes the account ID, VPC ID, and total number of dropped packets.  
  
The company wants to subscribe a new Lambda function to the SNS topic. For each notification, the new Lambda function must automatically stop the identified traffic from leaving a VPC by applying a network ACL to the transit gateway attachment subnets in the VPC that generated the traffic.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the existing Lambda function to add the destination IP addresses of the dropped traffic to each SNS notification. Configure the new Lambda function to create an outbound rule by using the destination IP addresses in the network ACL.

Configure the existing Lambda function to add the source IP addresses of the dropped traffic to each SNS notification. Configure the new Lambda function to create an inbound rule by using the source IP addresses in the network ACL.

Configure the existing Lambda function to add the source IP addresses of the dropped traffic to each SNS notification. Configure the new Lambda function to create an outbound rule by using the source IP addresses in the network ACL.

Configure the existing Lambda function to add the destination IP addresses of the dropped traffic to each SNS notification. Configure the new Lambda function to create an inbound rule by using the destination IP addresses in the network ACL.

questions.explanation:
The goal is to stop the offending flows from leaving the VPC, which is egress, so the new Lambda function must add an outbound network ACL rule. Network ACL outbound rules are evaluated against the destination of the traffic, so the existing Lambda function should include the destination IP addresses of the dropped packets in the SNS notification, and the new function should create an outbound deny rule keyed on those destination addresses. Options B and D create inbound rules, which govern traffic entering the VPC rather than leaving it, and option C tries to build an outbound rule from source IPs, which does not match how NACLs evaluate egress traffic.

**Learn more:** [Network ACLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html) · [Transit gateway flow logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-flow-logs.html)

AnyCompany has acquired Example Corp. AnyCompany's infrastructure is entirely on premises, while Example Corp's infrastructure is completely in the AWS Cloud. The companies use AWS Direct Connect with AWS Transit Gateway to establish connectivity with one another.  
  
Example Corp has deployed a new application across two Availability Zones in a VPC that has no internet gateway. The VPC CIDR range is `10.0.0.0/16`. Example Corp needs access to an application deployed on premises by AnyCompany. Due to compliance requirements, Example Corp must access the application through a limited, contiguous block of approved IP addresses (`10.1.0.0/24`).  
  
A network engineer must implement a highly available solution to accomplish this goal. The network engineer begins by updating the VPC to add a new CIDR range of `10.1.0.0/24`.  
  
What should the network engineer do next to satisfy the requirements?

options.text: In each Availability Zone in the VPC, create a subnet that uses part of the allowed IP address range. Create a public NAT gateway in each of the new subnets. Update the route tables that are associated with other subnets to route application traffic to the public NAT gateway in the corresponding Availability Zone. Add a route to the route table that is associated with the subnets of the public NAT gateways to send traffic destined for the application to the transit gateway.

In each Availability Zone in the VPC, create a subnet that uses part of the allowed IP address range. Create a private NAT gateway in each of the new subnets. Update the route tables that are associated with other subnets to route application traffic to the private NAT gateway in the corresponding Availability Zone. Add a route to the route table that is associated with the subnets of the private NAT gateways to send traffic destined for the application to the transit gateway.

In the VPC, create a subnet that uses the allowed IP address range. Create a private NAT gateway in the new subnet. Update the route tables that are associated with other subnets to route application traffic to the private NAT gateway. Add a route to the route table that is associated with the subnet of the private NAT gateway to send traffic destined for the application to the transit gateway.

In the VPC, create a subnet that uses the allowed IP address range. Create a public NAT gateway in the new subnet. Update the route tables that are associated with other subnets to route application traffic to the public NAT gateway. Add a route to the route table that is associated with the subnet of the public NAT gateway to send traffic destined for the application to the transit gateway.

questions.explanation:
A private NAT gateway translates the application instances' source addresses to private IP addresses from the approved `10.1.0.0/24` range and can route that traffic to an on-premises network through AWS Transit Gateway. Creating a private NAT gateway in an approved-range subnet in each Availability Zone provides high availability and avoids cross-AZ dependency. Public NAT gateways are intended for internet connectivity and require public-subnet/Internet Gateway configuration, which this VPC does not have. AWS documents this allow-listed on-premises-access pattern with a private NAT gateway and specifies routing on-premises-destined traffic from application subnets to the NAT gateway and from the NAT gateway subnet to the private network gateway.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateway use cases - Amazon VPC User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html) · [NAT gateways - Amazon VPC User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html)
