A company has exhausted IP address space in one of the Availability Zones in an AWS Region that it uses. The Availability Zone with no remaining space is assigned the `10.10.1.0/24` CIDR block. The company manages its networking configuration in an AWS CloudFormation stack. The company’s VPC is assigned the `10.10.0.0/16` CIDR block and has available capacity in the `10.10.1.0/22` CIDR block.  
  
How should a network specialist add additional IP address space to the existing VPC with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Update the AWS::EC2::Subnet resource for the Availability Zone in the CloudFormation stack. Change the CidrBlock property to 10.10.1.0/22.
Update the AWS::EC2::VPC resource in the CloudFormation stack. Change the CidrBlock property to 10.10.1.0/22.
Copy the CloudFormation stack. Set the AWS::EC2::VPC resource CidrBlock property to 10.10.0.0/16. Set the AWS::EC2::Subnet resource CidrBlock property to 10.10.1.0/22 for the Availability Zone.
Create a new AWS::EC2::Subnet resource for the Availability Zone in the CloudFormation stack. Set the CidrBlock property to 10.10.2.0/24.

questions.explanation:
A VPC can contain multiple subnets in the same Availability Zone. Creating a new, non-overlapping `10.10.2.0/24` subnet in that Availability Zone uses available address space in the existing VPC without replacing the exhausted subnet. In contrast, changing the `CidrBlock` of an `AWS::EC2::Subnet` requires CloudFormation to replace that subnet, creating greater disruption.

**Learn more:** [AWS::EC2::Subnet - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-subnet.html) · [VPC basics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-subnet-basics.html)

options.text: Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection that supports IPv6.
Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection to a self-managed Amazon EC2 instance that runs open source software.
Update the existing Site-to-Site VPN connections to support IPv6.
Update the on-premises customer gateway's public IP address from IPv4 to IPv6.

questions.explanation:
An existing IPv4 AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection cannot be modified to use IPv6. IPv6 traffic through a transit-gateway VPN requires a newly created VPN connection configured with IPv6 support. This uses the managed AWS VPN service and avoids the additional administration of a self-managed EC2 VPN appliance.

**Learn more:** [IPv4 and IPv6 traffic in AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/ipv4-ipv6.html)

An education agency is getting ready for its annual competition among schools. During the competition, students at schools nationwide solve math problems, complete puzzles, and write essays.  
  
The IP addressing plan for all schools is well known and centrally administered. The competition is hosted in the AWS Cloud and is not publicly accessible. All competition traffic must be encrypted in transit. Only authorized endpoints may access the competition. Every school has firewall policies that block ICMP traffic.  
  
A network engineer creates a solution in which all schools access the competition through AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections. The network engineer uses BGP as the routing protocol. The network engineer must implement a solution that notifies schools when they lose connectivity and must take action on their premises to resolve the issue.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner? (Choose two.)

options.text: Monitor the state of the VPN tunnels by using Amazon CloudWatch. Create a CloudWatch alarm that uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify people at the affected school if the tunnels are down.

Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that pings each school's on-premises customer gateway device. Configure the Lambda function to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to people at the affected school if the ping fails.

Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function that uses the VPC Reachability Analyzer API to verify the connectivity. Configure the Lambda function to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to people at the affected school if failure occurs.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for each school to show all CloudWatch metrics for each school's Site-to-Site VPN connection. Share each dashboard with the appropriate school.

Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function to monitor the existence of each school's routes in the VPC route table where VPN routes are propagated. Configure the Lambda function to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to people at the affected school if failure occurs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN publishes the `TunnelState` CloudWatch metric automatically; for BGP VPNs, it indicates whether the BGP session is established. A CloudWatch alarm can invoke Amazon SNS to notify the affected school's contacts when the VPN tunnels are down. With dynamic routing, prefixes advertised through BGP by the customer gateway are propagated into the VPC route table while the VPN connection is up. Monitoring the expected propagated routes and notifying the relevant school if they disappear provides an automated indication of loss of that school's advertised connectivity. ICMP probing cannot work because ICMP is blocked, and dashboards provide visibility but no notification.

**Learn more:** [Monitor AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnels using Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/monitoring-cloudwatch-vpn.html) · [Get started with AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/SetUpVPNConnections.html)

A company’s security guidelines require that all outbound traffic from a VPC to the company’s on-premises data center pass through a security appliance. The security appliance runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. A network engineer must improve network performance between the on-premises data center and the security appliance.  
  
Which actions should the network engineer take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use an EC2 instance that supports enhanced networking.
Send outbound traffic through a transit gateway.
Increase the EC2 instance size.
Place the EC2 instance in a placement group within the VPC.
Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to the EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
Enhanced networking uses SR-IOV to provide higher bandwidth, higher packets-per-second performance, and lower latency on supported EC2 instance types. EC2 also applies network bandwidth limits based on instance type and size; increasing the instance size can increase the available network bandwidth. These changes improve the security appliance’s capacity to process traffic to and from the on-premises data center.

**Learn more:** [Enhanced networking on Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/enhanced-networking.html) · [Amazon EC2 instance network bandwidth](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-instance-network-bandwidth.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Cloud WAN with one edge location in the `us-east-1` Region and another edge location in the `us-west-1` Region. A shared services segment is present at both edge locations. Each shared services segment has a VPC attachment to each inspection VPC in its Region. The inspection VPCs use AWS Network Firewall to inspect WAN traffic.  
  
The company creates a segment for a new business unit (BU) at the `us-east-1` edge location. The new BU has three VPCs attached to its new BU segment. To meet regulatory requirements, the BU VPCs must not communicate with one another. All internet-bound traffic must be inspected in the inspection VPC.  
  
The company updates the VPC route tables so that all internet-bound traffic is sent to the AWS Cloud WAN core network.  
  
The company expects to add more VPCs for the new BU in the future. All future VPCs must meet the regulatory requirements.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient way? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update the network policy to share the shared services segment with the BU segment.
Create a network policy to share the inspection service segment with the BU segment.
Set the isolate-attachments field to True for the BU segment.
Set the isolate-attachments field to False for the BU segment.
Update the network policy to add static routes for the BU segment. Configure the shared services segment to route traffic related to VPC CIDR blocks to each respective VPC attachment.

questions.explanation:
Setting `isolate-attachments` to `true` stops attachments within the BU segment from communicating directly, so the restriction automatically applies to VPCs added to that segment later. A segment share with the existing shared services segment exposes the inspection VPC attachment routes to the BU segment, allowing its internet-bound traffic to reach the inspection path. AWS Cloud WAN segment sharing provides connectivity between segments, while isolated attachments require shared routes or static routes to reach resources outside their segment.

**Learn more:** [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html) · [Add segment actions in an AWS Cloud WAN core network policy version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policy-network-actions-routes.html)

A company is developing its website on AWS in one VPC. The VPC contains public and private subnets across two Availability Zones. The website includes static content, such as images, and the company uses Amazon S3 to store that content.  
  
The company has deployed a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances as web servers in a private subnet. The EC2 instances are in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances will serve traffic and must retrieve content from an S3 bucket to render the webpages. The company uses AWS Direct Connect with a public VIF for on-premises connectivity to the S3 bucket.  
  
A network engineer observes that traffic between the EC2 instances and Amazon S3 is being routed through a NAT gateway. As traffic grows, the company's costs are rising. The network engineer must change the connectivity to reduce NAT gateway costs caused by traffic between the EC2 instances and Amazon S3.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Direct Connect private VIF. Migrate the traffic from the public VIF to the private VIF.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN tunnel over the existing public VIF.
Implement interface VPC endpoints for Amazon S3. Update the VPC route table.
Implement gateway VPC endpoints for Amazon S3. Update the VPC route table.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint associates with the private-subnet route table and routes S3-destined traffic to the endpoint rather than the NAT gateway. Gateway endpoints provide S3 access without an internet gateway or NAT device and have no additional endpoint charge, eliminating NAT gateway data-processing charges for this traffic.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Gateway endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/gateway-endpoints.html)

A company operates applications across multiple AWS accounts. It uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage all accounts, and the applications run in VPCs that must communicate with one another.  
  
The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection between an on-premises data center and AWS and requires access to the VPCs from the on-premises location. It plans to add more than 100 new applications and VPCs to its AWS environment. The connectivity solution must support future growth and simplify connectivity from the data center to AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Attach all VPCs that host applications to the Direct Connect connection by using private VIFs. Create a virtual private gateway in each application VPC. Connect a hardware VPN in the data center to the virtual private gateway in each VPC. Configure static routes in all VPCs. Use the data center VPN appliance to route traffic.

Create a new AWS account and deploy a network transit VPC. Deploy Amazon EC2 instances that run open source VPN software. Create a virtual private gateway in each application VPC. Configure connections between the instance that runs the VPN software in the network transit VPC and each virtual private gateway, and update the route tables. Connect the open source VPN to a hardware VPN in the data center and configure routing.

Create a transit gateway in a new networking account. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to create a resource share that has the transit gateways source type. Enter the organization ID share the ID with the transit gateway. Create a private IP VPN that connects to a customer gateway in the data center. Attach the VPN to the transit gateway and configure dynamic routing.

Create a Direct Connect gateway and associate it with the Direct Connect connection. Attach all VPCs that host applications to the Direct Connect gateway. Create a public VIF and attach it to the gateway. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection by using the public VIF. Connect to a hardware VPN appliance in the data center and configure dynamic routing.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway provides a centralized routing hub for VPCs and VPN connections, including VPCs in other AWS accounts when the transit gateway is shared through AWS RAM. A private IP Site-to-Site VPN can terminate on the transit gateway and use Direct Connect transport with dynamic routing. This hub-and-spoke design avoids creating and managing separate virtual private gateways, VPNs, and routing configurations for every VPC, so it supports continued multi-account VPC growth.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html) · [Private IP AWS Site-to-Site VPN with Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/private-ip-dx.html)

A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances. A network engineer deploys a NAT gateway in the application’s VPC to replace self-managed NAT instances. After the engineer redirects traffic from the self-managed NAT instances to the NAT gateway, users start reporting problems.  
  
While troubleshooting, the network engineer finds that the connection to the application closes after about 6 minutes of inactivity.  
  
What should the network engineer do to fix this issue?

options.text: Check for increases in the IdleTimeoutCount Amazon CloudWatch metric for the NAT gateway. Configure TCP keepalive on the application EC2 instances.
Check for increases in the ErrorPortAllocation Amazon CloudWatch metric for the NAT gateway. Configure an HTTP timeout value on the application EC2 instances.
Check for increases in the PacketsDropCount Amazon CloudWatch metric for the NAT gateway. Configure an HTTPS timeout value on the application EC2 instances.
Check for decreases in the ActiveConnectionCount Amazon CloudWatch metric for the NAT gateway. Configure UDP keepalive on the application EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC NAT gateways time out connections that have been idle for 350 seconds (about 6 minutes). An increasing `IdleTimeoutCount` indicates these idle expirations, and TCP keepalive configured for less than 350 seconds maintains the connection before the NAT gateway removes its state.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot NAT gateways - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-troubleshooting.html) · [NAT gateway metrics and dimensions - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/metrics-dimensions-nat-gateway.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a highly available, scalable, and resilient application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. A network engineer plans to add IPv6 support to the application deployment in phases. The initial phase is to enable IPv6 service consumption on the public Network Load Balancers (NLBs) deployed throughout the infrastructure. The target groups for the NLBs are configured as the Auto Scaling groups containing the EC2 instances that host the application. The NLBs are configured for dual-stack operation.  
  
During testing of the initial phase, IPv6 application queries are not reaching the backend servers.  
  
What is causing this issue?

options.text: The subnets where the EC2 instances are deployed do not have IPv6 addresses configured.
The route tables for the NLB subnets do not have IPV6 routing configured.
The route tables for the EC2 subnets do not have IPV6 routing configured.
The security groups that are associated with the NLBs do not allow IPv6 traffic.

questions.explanation:
A dualstack Network Load Balancer requires IPv6 routing in the route tables of its load-balancer subnets. Without an IPv6 route there, IPv6 clients cannot reach the NLB. Backend instances do not need IPv6 merely because clients connect through the NLB using IPv6; target communication is determined by the target group IP address type.

**Learn more:** [Update the IP address types for your Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-ip-address-type.html) · [Target groups for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates two on-premises data center sites, **Data Center 1** and **Data Center 2**. Each site has a company-managed customer router. Both data centers have a dedicated AWS Direct Connect connection to the same Direct Connect gateway by using a private VIF. The company enabled Direct Connect SiteLink when it created each private VIF. The company uses SiteLink to transfer data between the two Direct Connect locations while bypassing AWS Regions.  
  
Data Center 2 hosts an application that a partner company must access. The partner wants to reach the application from its own data center by using the Direct Connect network. The company’s network engineer must create a separate, isolated network for the partner to establish connectivity between Data Center 2 and the partner’s data center.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? **(Choose two.)**

options.text: Create a new Direct Connect gateway for the partner in an AWS account. Share the account number with the partner to allow the partner to create a hosted VIF to the account. Accept and associate the partner's hosted VIF with the new Direct Connect gateway.
Provision a separate transit VIF for the partner on the Direct Connect connection at Data Center 2. Connect the transit VIF to the partner-specific Direct Connect gateway.

Share the company's AWS account number with the partner to allow the partner to create a hosted VIF to the account. Accept and associate the partner's hosted VIF with the existing Direct Connect gateway.
Provision a separate private VIF for the partner on the Direct Connect connection at Data Center 2. Connect the private VIF to the partner-specific Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink.
Provision a separate public VIF for the partner on the Direct Connect connection at Data Center 2. Connect the public VIF to the partner-specific Direct Connect gateway. Enable SiteLink.

questions.explanation:
Direct Connect SiteLink enables on-premises connectivity between Direct Connect points of presence when SiteLink-enabled VIFs are associated with the same Direct Connect gateway. A separate Direct Connect gateway isolates the partner network; the partner’s hosted VIF can be accepted and associated with that gateway. The Client VPN endpoint route table contains one entry: `0.0.0.0/0`. The Client VPN endpoint uses a new security group with no inbound rules and one outbound rule that permits all traffic to `0.0.0.0/0`.  
  
Multiple remote users report that web search results display inaccurate geographic location information for them.  
  
Which combination of steps should a network engineer take to resolve this issue with the **LEAST** service interruption? (Choose three.)

options.text: Switch users to AWS Site-to-Site VPNs.
Enable the split-tunnel option on the Client VPN endpoint.
Add routes for the peered VPCs and for the on-premises data center to the Client VPN route table.
Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 outbound rule from the security group that the Client VPN endpoint uses.
Delete and recreate the Client VPN endpoint in a different VPC.
Remove the 0.0.0.0/0 entry from the Client VPN endpoint route table.

questions.explanation:
By default, AWS Client VPN routes all client traffic through the VPN tunnel, which makes Internet services observe the AWS egress location rather than the user’s local location. Split tunneling sends only traffic whose destination matches Client VPN endpoint routes through the tunnel. Specific routes for each peered VPC and the on-premises network preserve access to those private resources. A `0.0.0.0/0` route must be removed because AWS does not recommend that route with split tunneling due to possible connectivity disruption.

A network engineer must configure a DNS solution so employees can access the internal webpage from the office network by using the private domain URL `https://example.com`.  
  
Which combination of steps satisfies this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an alias record that points to the ALB in the Route 53 private hosted zone.
Create a CNAME record that points to the ALB internal domain in the Route 53 private hosted zone.
Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint. On the office DNS server, configure a conditional forwarder to forward the DNS queries to the Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint.
Create a Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint. On the office DNS server, configure a conditional forwarder to forward the DNS queries to the Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint.
On the office DNS server, configure a conditional forwarder for the private domain to the VPC DNS at 172.31.0.2.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 alias record can point the apex record, `example.com`, to an Application Load Balancer. DNS queries originating on the office network must be conditionally forwarded to a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint, which provides the path for on-premises resolvers to query records in a private hosted zone associated with the VPC. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its record-keeping application to the AWS Cloud. During the migration, all traffic between the company’s on-premises data center and AWS must remain encrypted at all times and at every transit device.  
  
The application will run across multiple Availability Zones in one AWS Region. It will use existing 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connections with a MACsec-capable port. A network engineer must ensure that the Direct Connect connection is secured appropriately at every transit device.  
  
The network engineer creates a Connection Key Name and Connectivity Association Key (CKN/CAK) pair for the MACsec secret key.  
  
Which combination of additional steps must the network engineer take to meet the requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the on-premises router with the MACsec secret key.
Update the connection's MACsec encryption mode to must_encrypt. Then associate the CKN/CAK pair with the connection.
Update the connection's MACsec encryption mode to should encrypt. Then associate the CKN/CAK pair with the connection.
Associate the CKN/CAK pair with the connection. Then update the connection's MACsec encryption mode to must_encrypt.
Associate the CKN/CAK pair with the connection. Then update the connection’s MACsec encryption mode to should_encrypt.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect MACsec requires the CKN/CAK-derived secret key to be configured on the on-premises router and associated with the Direct Connect connection. The `must_encrypt` mode requires MACsec encryption for all traffic and prevents transmission if MACsec cannot be established; `should_encrypt` can fall back to unencrypted traffic. Associating the key before enforcing `must_encrypt` ensures the connection has a configured MACsec key when mandatory encryption is enabled.

**Learn more:** [MAC Security in AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html) · [Get started using MACsec on a dedicated Direct Connect connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-macsec-dedicated.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company is moving its on-premises application to the AWS Cloud. At present, the company operates two on-premises data center locations. One data center is on the east coast of the United States, and the other is on the west coast.  
  
Each data center runs four database systems. The largest database system contains 500 GB of data. The data centers are linked by two 10 GbE circuits for data synchronization. Each data center has two independent 1 GbE upstream internet connections. The company plans to use eight total VPCs to support its multiple business units. Four VPCs will be in the us-east-1 Region, and four VPCs will be in the us-west-2 Region.  
  
A network engineer must design a connectivity solution that enables VPC-to-VPC connectivity. The solution must also provide secure connections between the on-premises data centers and AWS during the migration. The company anticipates traffic spikes between the VPCs during database synchronization. The company wants to execute the migration during one weekend and as quickly as technically possible. The company also wants to reduce long-term operational and human-resources costs.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy one transit gateway and attach all VPCs to it. Update the transit gateway and VPC route tables to allow any VPC to connect to any other VPC.
Configure VPC peering between all the VPCs. Update the VPC route tables to allow connectivity.
Provision two AWS Direct Connect connections from two Direct Connect locations that serve us-east-1 and us-west-2 to provide connectivity between the data centers and AWS.
Provision one transit gateway VPN attachment for each data center to build connectivity between the on-premises data centers and AWS VPCs.
Provision one AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection for each data center and for each VPC to build connectivity between the on-premises data centers and AWS VPCs.

questions.explanation:
A single transit gateway with all eight VPCs attached (and inter-Region peering) provides any-to-any VPC connectivity with far less long-term operational overhead than a full VPC-peering mesh (option B), which scales poorly across two Regions. For on-premises connectivity that can be stood up in a single weekend, Direct Connect (option C) is disqualified because provisioning a new Direct Connect connection takes weeks. One transit gateway VPN attachment per data center (option D) can be established immediately, is highly available (dual tunnels), and leaves only two attachments to operate. Option E provisions a VPN per data center per VPC (sixteen connections), which is the opposite of low operational cost.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/what-is-transit-gateway.html) · [Transit gateway VPN attachments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-vpn-attachments.html)

A government contractor is designing a multi-account environment containing multiple VPCs for a customer. A network security policy mandates transparent inspection by a third-party appliance of all traffic between any two VPCs.  
  
The customer requires a solution that uses AWS Transit Gateway. The deployment must be highly available across multiple Availability Zones and support automated failover. In addition, the inspection appliances do not support asymmetric routing.  
  
Which combination of steps is included in a solution that satisfies these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy two clusters that consist of multiple appliances across multiple Availability Zones in a designated inspection VPC. Connect the inspection VPC to the transit gateway by using a VPC attachment. Create a target group, and register the appliances with the target group. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB), and set it up to forward to the newly created target group. Configure a default route in the inspection VPCs transit gateway subnet toward the NLB.

Deploy two clusters that consist of multiple appliances across multiple Availability Zones in a designated inspection VPC. Connect the inspection VPC to the transit gateway by using a VPC attachment. Create a target group, and register the appliances with the target group. Create a Gateway Load Balancer, and set it up to forward to the newly created target group. Configure a default route in the inspection VPC’s transit gateway subnet toward the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint.

Configure two route tables on the transit gateway. Associate one route table with all the attachments of the application VPCs. Associate the other route table with the inspection VPC’s attachment. Propagate all VPC attachments into the inspection route table. Define a static default route in the application route table. Enable appliance mode on the attachment that connects the inspection VPC.

Configure two route tables on the transit gateway. Associate one route table with all the attachments of the application VPCs. Associate the other route table with the inspection VPCs attachment. Propagate all VPC attachments into the application route table. Define a static default route in the inspection route table. Enable appliance mode on the attachment that connects the inspection VPC.
Configure one route table on the transit gateway. Associate the route table with all the VPCs. Propagate all VPC attachments into the route table. Define a static default route in the route table.

questions.explanation:
Gateway Load Balancer transparently sends traffic to registered virtual security appliances and supports flow stickiness, while Gateway Load Balancer endpoints are routable targets from the Transit Gateway attachment subnets. A centralized Transit Gateway inspection design associates application VPC attachments with a route table whose default route points to the inspection VPC attachment, and associates the inspection VPC attachment with a route table that receives propagated application-VPC routes. Enabling appliance mode on the inspection attachment keeps bidirectional stateful flows symmetric through the same Availability Zone and appliance.

**Learn more:** [Using Gateway Load Balancer with Transit Gateway for centralized network security](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-scalable-secure-multi-vpc-network-infrastructure/using-gwlb-with-tg-for-cns.html) · [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html)

A global delivery company is modernizing its fleet-management system. The company has multiple business units. Each business unit designs and maintains applications hosted in its own AWS account, in separate application VPCs within the same AWS Region. The applications for each business unit are designed to retrieve data from a central shared-services VPC.  
  
The company requires a network connectivity architecture that provides granular security controls. The architecture must also scale as additional business units consume data from the central shared-services VPC in the future.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** secure manner?

options.text: Create a central transit gateway. Create a VPC attachment to each application VPC. Provide full mesh connectivity between all the VPCs by using the transit gateway.
Create VPC peering connections between the central shared services VPC and each application VPC in each business unit's AWS account.
Create VPC endpoint services powered by AWS PrivateLink in the central shared services VPCreate VPC endpoints in each application VPC.
Create a central transit VPC with a VPN appliance from AWS Marketplace. Create a VPN attachment from each VPC to the transit VPC. Provide full mesh connectivity among all the VPCs.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink lets the shared-services VPC publish only the required application service as an endpoint service, while each consumer VPC connects through its own interface VPC endpoint. This avoids broad, transitive network access between VPCs and supports granular provider-side permissions for the AWS principals that may connect. Adding a new consumer requires only another endpoint connection, which scales cleanly. [AWS PrivateLink concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/concepts.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/concepts.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

options.text: Disable cross-zone load balancing for the target group.
Disable cross-zone load balancing for the ALB.
Disable cross-zone load balancing for all the targets in the first Availability Zone.
Disable cross-zone load balancing for all the targets in the second Availability Zone.

questions.explanation:
For an Application Load Balancer, cross-zone load balancing is always enabled at the load-balancer level and cannot be disabled there. Disabling it on the target group makes each load balancer node route only to targets in its own Availability Zone. The nodes receive an equal share of traffic across the two Availability Zones, producing a 50%/50% zonal split regardless of the unequal number of targets.

**Learn more:** [Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html) · [How Elastic Load Balancing works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/userguide/how-elastic-load-balancing-works.html)

A company has a hybrid IT environment that includes services running in an on-premises data center and in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Direct Connect to connect its data center to AWS. It uses one AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup and requires a backup connectivity option to be available at all times. The company is moving to IPv6 by implementing dual-stack architectures.  
  
Which combination of steps will migrate the data center's connectivity to AWS in the **LEAST** amount of time? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a new Site-to-Site VPN tunnel for the IPv6 traffic.
Create a new dual-stack Site-to-Site VPN connection between the data center and AWS. Provision routing. Delete the original Site-to-Site VPN connection.
Associate a new dual-stack public VIF with the Direct Connect connection. Migrate the Direct Connect traffic to the new VIF.
Add a new IPv6 peer in the existing VIF. Use the IPv6 address provided by Amazon on the peer router.
Send IPv6 traffic between the data center and AWS in a tunnel inside the existing IPv4 tunnels.

questions.explanation:
For Direct Connect, a single virtual interface can run IPv4, IPv6, or dual-stack BGP sessions, so the fastest path is option D: add an IPv6 BGP peer to the existing VIF using the IPv6 addressing Amazon provides, with no new VIF and no disruption. For the VPN, you cannot enable IPv6 on an existing Site-to-Site VPN connection (each connection's inside tunnels carry either IPv4 or IPv6), so option B is required: create a new IPv6-capable Site-to-Site VPN connection, provision routing, then delete the original, which keeps a backup available throughout. Option E (tunneling IPv6 inside the existing IPv4 tunnels) is a non-native workaround with high overhead, and option A cannot bolt an extra tunnel onto an existing VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [IPv4 and IPv6 traffic in AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/ipv4-ipv6.html) · [Hybrid connectivity design for IPv6](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/ipv6-on-aws/hybrid-connectivity-design.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer must deliver dual-stack connectivity between a company office location and an AWS account. The company’s on-premises router supports dual-stack connectivity, and the VPC is configured for dual-stack support. The company has established two AWS Direct Connect connections to the office location. This connectivity must be highly available and reliable for latency-sensitive traffic.  
  
Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure a single private VIF on each Direct Connect connection. Add both IPv4 and IPv6 peering to each private VIF. Configure the on- premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.

Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.

Configure a single private VIF and IPv4 peering on each Direct Connect connection. Configure the on-premises equipment with this peering to advertise the IPv6 routes in the same BGP neighbor configuration. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.

Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise all IPv4 routes and IPv6 routes on all peering sessions. Keep the Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) configuration unchanged.

Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Reduce the BGP hello timer to 5 seconds on both the on-premises equipment and the Direct Connect configuration.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Direct Connect virtual interface can have one IPv4 BGP peering session and one IPv6 BGP peering session, allowing a single private VIF on each redundant Direct Connect connection to provide dual-stack connectivity. Alternatively, separate IPv4 and IPv6 private VIFs can be provisioned on each connection. In either design, IPv4 prefixes must be advertised on IPv4 peerings and IPv6 prefixes on IPv6 peerings because Direct Connect does not support multiprotocol BGP for a VIF. BFD must be configured on the customer router for the BFD capability already enabled on Direct Connect VIFs to take effect, providing rapid path-failure detection.

**Learn more:** [Add a BGP peer to a Direct Connect virtual interface](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/add-peer-to-vif.html) · [Direct Connect connection options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

An ecommerce company must add security controls to all of its domain names hosted in Amazon Route 53. A new company policy requires data authentication and data-integrity verification for every query to the company’s domain names. The existing Route 53 architecture contains four public hosted zones.  
  
A network engineer must implement DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) signing and validation for the hosted zones. The solution must provide alerting capability.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Enable DNSSEC signing for Route 53 Request that Route 53 create a key-signing key (KSK) based on a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Enable DNSSEC signing for Route 53 Request that Route 53 create a zone-signing key (ZSK) based on a customer managed key in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
Create a chain of trust for the hosted zones by adding a Delegation Signer (DS) record for each subdomain
Create a chain of trust for the hosted zones by adding a Delegation Signer (DS) record to the parent zone.
Set up an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that provides an alert whenever a DNSSECInternalFailure error or DNSSECKeySigningKeysNeedingAction error is detected.
Set up an AWS CloudTrail alarm that provides an alert whenever a DNSSECInternalFailure error or DNSSECKeySigningKeysNeedingAction error is detected.

questions.explanation:
Route 53 DNSSEC signing uses a key-signing key (KSK) that is based on a customer managed AWS KMS key, while Route 53 creates and manages the zone-signing key (ZSK). A DNSSEC chain of trust requires a Delegation Signer (DS) record in the parent zone for each signed hosted zone. Amazon CloudWatch alarms should alert on the `DNSSECInternalFailure` and `DNSSECKeySigningKeysNeedingAction` errors so DNSSEC failures and KSK conditions can be remediated promptly.

**Learn more:** [Configuring DNSSEC signing in Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec.html) · [Enabling DNSSEC signing and establishing a chain of trust](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-configuring-dnssec-enable-signing.html)

A company uses Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall in a VPC to block every domain except those on an approved list. The company is concerned that, if DNS Firewall becomes unresponsive, VPC resources could be affected because the network might be unable to resolve DNS queries. To preserve application service level agreements, the company requires DNS queries to continue resolving even when Route 53 Resolver receives no response from DNS Firewall.  
  
Which change should a network engineer make to meet these requirements?

options.text: Update the DNS Firewall VPC configuration to disable fail open for the VPC.
Update the DNS Firewall VPC configuration to enable fail open for the VPC.
Create a new DHCP options set with parameter dns_firewall_fail_open=false. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.
Create a new DHCP options set with parameter dns_firewall_fail_open=true. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.

questions.explanation:
Enabling fail open in the VPC's DNS Firewall configuration causes Route 53 Resolver to allow DNS queries to proceed when DNS Firewall does not return a response. This prioritizes DNS availability during a DNS Firewall failure.

**Learn more:** [DNS Firewall VPC configuration - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-dns-firewall-vpc-configuration.html) · [UpdateFirewallConfig - Amazon Route 53 Resolver API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/APIReference/API_route53resolver_UpdateFirewallConfig.html)

The company uses AWS Direct Connect to connect its data center to AWS. It uses one AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection as a backup and requires a backup connectivity option to be available at all times. The company is moving to IPv6 by implementing dual-stack architectures."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps will migrate the data center's connectivity to AWS in the ",["$","strong",".1",{"children":"LEAST"}]," amount of time?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new Site-to-Site VPN tunnel for the IPv6 traffic.","B":"Create a new dual-stack Site-to-Site VPN connection between the data center and AWS. Provision routing. Delete the original Site-to-Site VPN connection.","C":"Associate a new dual-stack public VIF with the Direct Connect connection. Migrate the Direct Connect traffic to the new VIF.","D":"Add a new IPv6 peer in the existing VIF. Use the IPv6 address provided by Amazon on the peer router.","E":"Send IPv6 traffic between the data center and AWS in a tunnel inside the existing IPv4 tunnels."},"correctAnswer":"BD","explanation":"For Direct Connect, a single virtual interface can run IPv4, IPv6, or dual-stack BGP sessions, so the fastest path is option D: add an IPv6 BGP peer to the existing VIF using the IPv6 addressing Amazon provides, with no new VIF and no disruption. For the VPN, you cannot enable IPv6 on an existing Site-to-Site VPN connection (each connection's inside tunnels carry either IPv4 or IPv6), so option B is required: create a new IPv6-capable Site-to-Site VPN connection, provision routing, then delete the original, which keeps a backup available throughout. Option E (tunneling IPv6 inside the existing IPv4 tunnels) is a non-native workaround with high overhead, and option A cannot bolt an extra tunnel onto an existing VPN connection.

**Learn more:** [IPv4 and IPv6 traffic in AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/ipv4-ipv6.html) · [Hybrid connectivity design for IPv6](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/ipv6-on-aws/hybrid-connectivity-design.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"606dfa25-d81f-479e-9f18-c0c5fbd00e25","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

The company’s on-premises router supports dual-stack connectivity, and the VPC is configured for dual-stack support. The company has established two AWS Direct Connect connections to the office location. This connectivity must be highly available and reliable for latency-sensitive traffic."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solutions meet these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Configure a single private VIF on each Direct Connect connection. Add both IPv4 and IPv6 peering to each private VIF. Configure the on- premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.","B":"Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.","C":"Configure a single private VIF and IPv4 peering on each Direct Connect connection. Configure the on-premises equipment with this peering to advertise the IPv6 routes in the same BGP neighbor configuration. Enable Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) on all peering sessions.","D":"Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise all IPv4 routes and IPv6 routes on all peering sessions. Keep the Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) configuration unchanged.","E":"Configure two private VIFs on each Direct Connect connection: one private VIF with the IPv4 address family and one private VIF with the IPv6 address family. Configure the on-premises equipment with the AWS provided BGP neighbors to advertise IPv4 routes on the IPv4 peering and IPv6 routes on the IPv6 peering. Reduce the BGP hello timer to 5 seconds on both the on-premises equipment and the Direct Connect configuration."},"correctAnswer":"AB","explanation":"An AWS Direct Connect virtual interface can have one IPv4 BGP peering session and one IPv6 BGP peering session, allowing a single private VIF on each redundant Direct Connect connection to provide dual-stack connectivity. Alternatively, separate IPv4 and IPv6 private VIFs can be provisioned on each connection. In either design, IPv4 prefixes must be advertised on IPv4 peerings and IPv6 prefixes on IPv6 peerings because Direct Connect does not support multiprotocol BGP for a VIF. BFD must be configured on the customer router for the BFD capability already enabled on Direct Connect VIFs to take effect, providing rapid path-failure detection.

**Learn more:** [Add a BGP peer to a Direct Connect virtual interface](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/add-peer-to-vif.html) · [Direct Connect connection options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"05c54522-1846-40da-b130-25ff1a4fbd9a","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

A company has created a new web application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in the us-east-1 Region. The application uses Amazon Route 53 to host the DNS records for the domain. The website primarily serves static images and files that are not updated often. Most end-user traffic to the website will come from the United States. Some traffic will come from Canada and Europe.  
  
A network engineer must design a solution that reduces latency for end users at the lowest cost. The solution must also ensure that all traffic remains encrypted in transit until it reaches the ALB.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the ALB to use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in us-east-1. Create a secure HTTPS listener. Create an alias record in Amazon Route 53 for the custom domain name. Configure the alias record to route to the DNS name that is assigned to the accelerator for the ALB.

Configure the ALB to use a secure HTTPS listener. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the origin domain name to point to the DNS record that is assigned to the ALConfigure the CloudFront distribution to use an SSL certificate. Set all behaviors to force HTTPS. Create an alias record in Amazon Route 53 for the custom domain name. Configure the alias record to route to the DNS name that is assigned to the ALB.

Configure the ALB to use a secure HTTPS listener. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the origin domain name to point to the DNS record that is assigned to the ALB. Configure the CloudFront distribution to use an SSL certificate and redirect HTTP to HTTPS. Create an alias record in Amazon Route 53 for the custom domain name. Configure the alias record to route to the CloudFront distribution.

Configure the ALB to use an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in us-east-1. Create a secure HTTPS listener. Create a second application stack on Amazon ECS on Fargate in the eu-west-1 Region. Create another secure HTTPS listener. Create an alias record in Amazon Route 53 for the custom domain name. Configure the alias record to use a latency-based routing policy to route to the DNS name that is assigned to the accelerator for the ALBs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront caches the mostly static content at edge locations close to users, reducing latency without the expense of operating an additional regional application stack. A CloudFront distribution can use a TLS certificate and redirect HTTP viewers to HTTPS, and the ALB's HTTPS listener preserves encrypted delivery to the origin. The Route 53 alias record must point to the CloudFront distribution so requests use the CDN rather than bypassing it and going directly to the ALB.

**Learn more:** [Routing traffic to an Amazon CloudFront distribution by using your domain name](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-cloudfront-distribution.html) · [Use custom URLs by adding alternate domain names (CNAMEs)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/CNAMEs.html)

A company is rolling out a new application in the AWS Cloud. The company requires a highly available web server behind an Elastic Load Balancer. The load balancer must route requests to multiple target groups according to the URL in each request. All traffic must use HTTPS. TLS processing must be offloaded to the load balancer. The web server must know the user’s IP address so that the company can maintain accurate security logs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener. Use path-based routing rules to forward the traffic to the correct target group. Include the X-Forwarded-For request header with traffic to the targets.

Deploy an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener for each domain. Use host-based routing rules to forward the traffic to the correct target group for each domain. Include the X-Forwarded-For request header with traffic to the targets.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener. Use path-based routing rules to forward the traffic to the correct target group. Configure client IP address preservation for traffic to the targets.

Deploy a Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener for each domain. Use host-based routing rules to forward the traffic to the correct target group for each domain. Configure client IP address preservation for traffic to the targets.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer supports Layer 7 path-based routing to target groups. Its HTTPS listener terminates TLS at the load balancer, and it forwards the client IP address to targets in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. A Network Load Balancer cannot perform path-based routing because it uses Layer 4 listeners.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [HTTP headers and Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/x-forwarded-headers.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has launched a new web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Enterprise customers worldwide will use the application. Employees of these enterprise customers will access the application over HTTPS from office locations.  
  
The company must configure firewalls to permit outbound traffic only to approved IP addresses. The enterprise customers’ employees must be able to reach the application with the lowest possible latency.  
  
Which infrastructure change should a network engineer make to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a new Network Load Balancer (NLB). Add the ALB as a target of the NLB.
Create a new Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the ALB as the distribution’s origin.
Create a new accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Add the ALB as an accelerator endpoint.
Create a new Amazon Route 53 hosted zone. Create a new record to route traffic to the ALB.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that can be added to firewall allowlists and supports Application Load Balancers as standard accelerator endpoints. It accepts client traffic at the nearest AWS edge location and routes it over the AWS global network, improving performance for globally distributed users.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Compare using global static IP addresses to regional static IP addresses](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-accelerators.eip-accelerator.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a web application across two AWS Regions. The company has one VPC in each Region. Each VPC contains three Amazon EC2 instances serving as web servers behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company has already configured an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for `example.com`. Users will access the application by using the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) `app.example.com`.  
  
The company needs a DNS solution that enables global users to access the application. The solution must route users' requests to the Region with the lowest response time. If the application is unavailable in the initially selected Region, the solution must fail over to the Region with the next-lowest response time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: For each ALB, create an A record that has a geolocation routing policy to route app.example.com to the IP addresses of the ALB. Configure a Route 53 HTTP health check that monitors each ALB by IP address. Associate the health check with the A records.

Create an A record that has a geolocation routing policy to route app.example.com to the IP addresses for both ALBs. Configure a Route 53 health check that monitors TCP port 80 for each ALB by IP address. Associate the health check with the A records.

Create an A record that has a latency-based routing policy to route app.example.com as an alias to one of the ALBs. Configure a Route 53 health check that monitors TCP port 80 for each ALB by IP address. Associate the health check with the A records.
For each ALB, create an A record that has a latency-based routing policy to route app.example.com as an alias to the ALB. Set the value for Evaluate Target Health to Yes for the records.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing uses latency measurements to select the AWS Region that provides the lowest latency for a user. Creating one latency-based alias A record per ALB lets both Regional endpoints participate in that selection. With Evaluate Target Health enabled, Route 53 evaluates an Application Load Balancer by the health of its target groups; an unhealthy ALB is not used, so Route 53 can return another healthy latency record.

**Learn more:** [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html) · [Values specific for latency alias records - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-values-latency-alias.html)

A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection between an on-premises data center and a single private VIF in the company’s VPC. The VPC includes resources that the company has secured by using security groups and network ACLs.  
  
During a maintenance period, a network engineer adds a subnet in the company’s data center. After the maintenance activity, the engineer observes that the BGP status for the private VIF is down. The Direct Connect connection was fully operational before the maintenance period. The network team confirms that Layer 2 connectivity is working between the company’s router and the Direct Connect router.  
  
The networking engineer must resolve this issue.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement?

options.text: Use route filters or aggregation on the company's router to limit the routes that are advertised from the company’s router.
Add a route policy to the company's router to ensure that all routes that are advertised from the company's router are tagged with a correct BGP community string that begins in
Revalidate the physical and logical path between the company's router and the Direct Connect router, including any Direct Connect Partner.
Ensure that security groups and network ACLs allow TCP communications to port 179.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect permits up to 100 advertised route prefixes for each IPv4 and IPv6 address family on a private VIF BGP session. Advertising more than that causes the BGP session to enter the idle state with BGP down. Route filters or route aggregation on the customer router reduce the advertised-prefix count, addressing the BGP failure.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/limits.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a VPC containing application workloads that run on Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The company wants to use AWS Local Zones to deploy an extension of the application workloads running in the Region. The extended workloads in the Local Zone must communicate bidirectionally with the workloads in the VPC in the Region.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create a new VPC in the Local Zone. Attach all the VPCs to a transit gateway. Configure routing for the transit gateway and the VPCs. Deploy instances in the new VPC.
Deploy a third-party appliance in a new VPC in the Region. Create a new VPC in the Local Zone. Create VPN connections to the appliance for the VPCs. Deploy instances in the new VPC in the Local Zone.

Create a new subnet in the Local Zone. Deploy a third-party appliance in the VPC with interfaces in each subnet. Configure the new subnet to route the Local Zone through the appliance. Deploy instances in the new subnet.
Create a new subnet in the Local Zone. Configure the new subnet to use a CIDR block that is within the VPC’s CIDR block. Deploy instances in the new subnet in the Local Zone.

questions.explanation:
Creating a subnet in an AWS Local Zone extends the existing VPC to that Local Zone. The subnet must use a CIDR block from the VPC’s CIDR range and functions as a subnet of the same VPC, allowing native bidirectional communication with the Regional workloads without transit gateways, VPN connections, or third-party appliances.

**Learn more:** [Connectivity options for Local Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/local-zones/latest/ug/local-zones-connectivity.html) · [Getting started with AWS Local Zones](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/local-zones/latest/ug/getting-started.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing new features for its ecommerce website. The features will use several microservices that are reached through different paths. The microservices will run on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The company requires HTTPS for all its public websites. The application needs the customers’ source IP addresses.  
  
A network engineer must implement a load-balancing strategy that satisfies these requirements.  
  
Which combination of actions should the network engineer take to achieve this goal? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use a Network Load Balancer
Retrieve client IP addresses by using the X-Forwarded-For header
Use AWS App Mesh load balancing
Retrieve client IP addresses by using the X-IP-Source header
Use an Application Load Balancer.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP/HTTPS and path-based listener rules, allowing requests for different paths to be routed to the appropriate ECS microservice. It adds the client IP address to the X-Forwarded-For header before forwarding the request to the target, enabling the application to obtain the customer’s source address.

**Learn more:** [Use an Application Load Balancer for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/alb.html) · [HTTP headers and Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/x-forwarded-headers.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An ecommerce company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances to accommodate continually changing customer demand. The EC2 instances belong to an Auto Scaling group. The company wants to implement a solution that distributes customer traffic across the EC2 instances. All traffic between customers and the application servers must be encrypted at every stage. Decryption at intermediate points is not permitted.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Add an HTTPS listener to the ALB. Configure the Auto Scaling group to register instances with the ALB's target group.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the distribution with a custom SSL/TLS certificate. Set the Auto Scaling group as the distribution's origin.
Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Add a TCP listener to the NLB. Configure the Auto Scaling group to register instances with the NLB's target group.
Create a Gateway Load Balancer (GLB). Configure the Auto Scaling group to register instances with the GLB's target group.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener can pass TCP traffic on port 443 through to its registered EC2 targets without decrypting it. TLS remains end-to-end between the customer and the application server, so the EC2-hosted application—not the load balancer—performs decryption. AWS specifies that a TCP listener passes encrypted traffic to targets without load-balancer decryption.

**Learn more:** [Listeners for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html) · [Create an HTTPS listener for your Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/create-https-listener.html)

An IoT company sells hardware sensor modules that periodically transmit temperature, humidity, pressure, and location data by using the MQTT messaging protocol. The hardware sensor modules send this data to the company’s on-premises MQTT brokers, which run on Linux servers behind a load balancer. The hardware sensor modules have been hardcoded with public IP addresses to access the brokers.  
  
The company is expanding and acquiring customers worldwide. The current solution can no longer scale and is adding latency because of the company’s global presence. Consequently, the company decides to migrate its entire infrastructure from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The company must migrate without reconfiguring the hardware sensor modules already deployed worldwide. The solution must also minimize latency.  
  
The company migrates the MQTT brokers to run on Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
What should the company do next to meet these requirements?

options.text: Place the EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure TCP listeners. Use Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) from the on-premises network with the NLB.

Place the EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Configure TCP listeners. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the NLUse Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) from the on-premises network with Global Accelerator.

Place the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure TCP listeners. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the ALB. Use Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) from the on-premises network with Global Accelerator
Place the EC2 instances behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Use Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) from the on-premises network with CloudFront.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast entry IP addresses and accepts customer-owned IPv4 addresses through BYOIP, allowing the previously hardcoded addresses to remain the client entry points. It routes TCP traffic onto the AWS global network from an edge location close to each client and can use a Network Load Balancer as a standard accelerator endpoint. An NLB TCP listener supports the MQTT TCP traffic to the EC2 brokers.

A company plans to migrate to AWS by using an AWS Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke architecture. Its current on-premises Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) network has strict controls that enforce network segmentation through MPLS VPNs. The company has provisioned two 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections to deliver resilient, high-speed, low-latency connectivity to AWS.  
  
A security engineer must apply network-segmentation principles in AWS so that virtual routing and forwarding (VRF) is logically isolated for each of the company’s software development environments. The number of MPLS VPNs will grow in the future. The on-premises MPLS VPNs will have overlapping address space. The AWS network design must support overlapping address space for the VPNs.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy a software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) head-end virtual appliance and an SD-WAN controller into a Transit Gateway Connect VPC. Configure the company's edge routers to be managed by the new SD-WAN controller and to use SD-WAN to segment the traffic into the defined segments for each of the company's development environments.

Configure IPsec VPNs on the company edge routers for each MPLS VPN for each of the company's development environments. Attach each IPsec VPN tunnel to a discrete MPLS VPN. Configure AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections that terminate at a transit gateway for each MPLS VPN. Configure a transit gateway route table that matches the MPLS VPN for each Transit Gateway VPN attachment.
Create a transit VPC that terminates at the AWS Site-to-Site VRF-aware IPsec VPN. Configure IPsec VPN connections to each VPC for each of the company's development environment VRFs.

Configure a Transit Gateway Connect attachment for each MPLS VPN between the company's edge routers and Transit Gateway. Configure a transit gateway route table that matches the MPLS VPN for each of the company's development environments.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway route tables create isolated routing domains analogous to VRFs. A separate Transit Gateway Connect attachment for each MPLS VPN, associated with its corresponding Transit Gateway route table, extends each VRF independently over GRE and BGP. This preserves traffic isolation even where the MPLS VPN address spaces overlap, and additional VRFs can be added with additional Connect attachments and peers over the existing Direct Connect underlay.

**Learn more:** [Extend VRFs to AWS by using AWS Transit Gateway Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/extend-vrfs-to-aws-by-using-aws-transit-gateway-connect.html) · [Using AWS Transit Gateway Connect to extend VRFs and increase IP prefix advertisement](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/using-aws-transit-gateway-connect-to-extend-vrfs-and-increase-ip-prefix-advertisement/)

A financial company provides investment forecasts and recommendations to authorized users over the internet. All services are hosted in the AWS Cloud. A new compliance requirement requires that all internet service traffic from every host be logged and retained for 2 years. In the development AWS accounts, the company designed, tested, and verified a solution using Amazon VPC Traffic Mirroring with a Network Load Balancer (NLB) as the traffic mirror target. Although the solution operates in one AWS account, it mirrors traffic to another AWS account.  
  
A network engineer observes that, after deployment to production, some traffic is not mirrored. The network engineer also observes that this behavior is random.  
  
Which statements could explain why not all traffic is mirrored? (Choose two.)

options.text: The security groups are misconfigured on the production AWS account that hosts the company’s services.
The Amazon EC2 instance that is being monitored cannot handle the extra traffic that Traffic Mirroring has introduced.
The IAM policy that allows the creation of traffic mirror sessions is misconfigured
The mirrored traffic has a lower priority than the production traffic and is being dropped when network congestion occurs.
The NLB is experiencing warm-up delay because of sudden and significant increases in traffic.

questions.explanation:
Mirrored traffic counts against the bandwidth and packet-per-second capacity of the monitored EC2 instance, so an instance that cannot accommodate the additional mirrored traffic can lose mirrored packets. When network congestion or instance bandwidth/PPS limits are exceeded, AWS prioritizes production traffic and can drop mirrored traffic. [AWS Traffic Mirroring limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-network-limitations.html)

**Learn more:** [AWS Traffic Mirroring limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-network-limitations.html) · [Understand traffic mirror target concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-targets.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer must provide a list of IP addresses that are sending traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance. VPC Flow Logs are enabled. The EC2 instance has one network interface with two assigned IP addresses. However, the flow logs record traffic only for the primary IP address. The network engineer must determine whether any traffic is being sent to the EC2 instance's second IP address.  
  
What should the network engineer do to find the traffic flow for the second IP address?

options.text: Create a new flow log that includes the pkt-dstaddr field to capture the original destination IP address of the traffic.
Create a new flow log that includes the dstaddr field to capture the original destination IP address of the traffic.
Create a new flow log that includes the pkt-srcaddr field to capture the original destination IP address of the traffic.
Create a new flow log that includes the srcaddr field to capture the original destination IP address of the traffic.

questions.explanation:
For a network interface with multiple IPv4 addresses, VPC Flow Logs can show the primary private IP address in `dstaddr` even when traffic is sent to a secondary private IPv4 address. A custom flow-log format containing `pkt-dstaddr` captures the packet-level original destination IP address, which identifies traffic sent to the secondary address.

**Learn more:** [Flow log limitations - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs-limitations.html) · [Flow log records - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-log-records.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates its production VPC (VPC-A) in the eu-west-1 Region in Account 1. VPC-A is attached to a transit gateway (TGW-A) that connects to an on-premises data center in Dublin, Ireland, through an AWS Direct Connect transit VIF configured for an AWS Direct Connect gateway. The company also has a staging VPC (VPC-B) attached to a different transit gateway (TGW-B) in the eu-west-2 Region in Account 2.  
  
A network engineer needs to implement connectivity between VPC-B and the on-premises data center in Dublin.  
  
Which solutions meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure inter-Region VPC peering between VPC-A and VPC-B. Add the required VPC peering routes. Add the VPC-B CIDR block in the allowed prefixes on the Direct Connect gateway association.
Associate TGW-B with the Direct Connect gateway. Advertise the VPC-B CIDR block under the allowed prefixes.
Configure another transit VIF on the Direct Connect connection and associate TGW-B. Advertise the VPC-B CIDR block under the allowed prefixes.

Configure inter-Region transit gateway peering between TGW-A and TGW-B. Add the peering routes in the transit gateway route tables. Add both the VPC-A and the VPC-B CIDR block under the allowed prefix list in the Direct Connect gateway association.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the transit VIF to TGW-B as a VPN attachment.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect gateway supports associations with transit gateways in different AWS Regions and accounts. Associating TGW-B with the existing Direct Connect gateway and advertising the VPC-B CIDR in the allowed-prefix list provides direct on-premises connectivity. Inter-Region transit gateway peering can instead route VPC-B traffic through TGW-A to its Direct Connect gateway attachment, provided the transit gateway route tables contain the peering routes and the Direct Connect gateway association advertises the required VPC prefixes. VPC peering cannot be used for this transitive path through VPC-A, and a transit VIF attaches to a Direct Connect gateway rather than directly to a transit gateway.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [Allowed prefixes interactions for Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/allowed-to-prefixes.html)
