A global company is designing a hybrid architecture for private access to AWS resources in the `us-west-2` Region. The company’s existing architecture includes a VPC that uses RFC 1918 IP address space. The VPC is connected to an on-premises data center through AWS Direct Connect. Amazon Route 53 supplies name resolution within the VPC. Locally managed DNS servers in the data center provide DNS services to the on-premises hosts.  
  
The company has applications in the data center that must download objects from an Amazon S3 bucket in `us-west-2`.  
  
Which solution can the company use to access Amazon S3 without using public IP address space?

options.text: Create an S3 interface endpoint in the VPC. Update the on-premises application configuration to use the Regional VPC endpoint DNS hostname that is mapped to the S3 interface endpoint.

Create an S3 interface endpoint in the VPC. Configure a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Set up the data center DNS servers to forward DNS queries for the S3 domain from on premises to the inbound endpoint.
Create an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPUpdate the on-premises application configuration to use the hostname that is mapped to the S3 gateway endpoint.

Create an S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC. Configure a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Set up the data center DNS servers to forward DNS queries for the S3 domain from on premises to the inbound endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 interface endpoints use private IP addresses in the VPC and support access from on-premises networks over Direct Connect. A Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint allows the data center DNS servers to forward S3-domain queries into the VPC Resolver, which can return the interface endpoint’s private addresses. S3 gateway endpoints cannot be extended to resources across a Direct Connect connection and therefore cannot provide this on-premises access path.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company securely connects resources in its VPC to a software as a service (SaaS) solution provided by a SaaS provider. The SaaS solution is hosted in the AWS Cloud and uses AWS PrivateLink. The company accesses the SaaS solution, which is behind the SaaS provider's Network Load Balancer (NLB), by using a PrivateLink endpoint.  
  
The company recently added a new Availability Zone and new subnets to its VPC. A network engineer cannot deploy a new interface VPC endpoint for the SaaS solution in the new Availability Zone.  
  
What is causing this issue?

options.text: The CIDR block of the new subnets conflicts with the SaaS provider's CIDR block.
The enableDnsHostnames attribute and enableDnsSupport attribute were not configured on the new subnets in the new Availability Zone.
The SaaS provider does not offer the solution in the new Availability Zone and has not configured cross-zone load balancing for the NLB.
The new subnets are missing a route to the VPC internet gateway.

questions.explanation:
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer is available to consumers only in the Availability Zones enabled by the service provider. A consumer cannot add an interface endpoint subnet in an Availability Zone that the provider has not made available for the endpoint service. Cross-zone load balancing supports traffic to targets in other Availability Zones when needed.

**Learn more:** [Configure an endpoint service - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/configure-endpoint-service.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a NAT gateway to provide internet connectivity for private subnets in a VPC in the us-west-2 Region. Following a security audit, the company must remove the NAT gateway.  
  
Resources in the private subnets use the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent. A network engineer must create a solution so that the unified CloudWatch agent continues to operate after the NAT gateway is removed.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network engineer take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Validate that private DNS is enabled on the VPC by setting the enableDnsHostnames VPC attribute and the enableDnsSupport VPC attribute to true.
Create a new security group with an entry to allow outbound traffic that uses the TCP protocol on port 443 to destination 0.0.0.0/0
Create a new security group with entries to allow inbound traffic that uses the TCP protocol on port 443 from the IP prefixes of the private subnets.
Create the following interface VPC endpoints in the VPC: com.amazonaws.us-west-2.logs and com.amazonaws.us-west-2.monitoring. Associate the new security group with the endpoint network interfaces.
Create the following interface VPC endpoint in the VPC: com.amazonaws.us-west-2.cloudwatch. Associate the new security group with the endpoint network interfaces.
Associate the VPC endpoint or endpoints with route tables that the private subnets use.

questions.explanation:
The unified CloudWatch agent needs private access to both Amazon CloudWatch for metrics and CloudWatch Logs for log delivery. Interface VPC endpoints for `com.amazonaws.us-west-2.monitoring` and `com.amazonaws.us-west-2.logs` provide that access without a NAT gateway. DNS support and DNS hostnames must be enabled in the VPC so service names can resolve to the private endpoint interfaces, and the endpoints’ security group must allow inbound TCP 443 from the private-subnet IP ranges. Interface endpoints are reached through their endpoint network interfaces and do not require route-table associations.

**Learn more:** [Amazon CloudWatch agent prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/prerequisites.html) · [Using CloudWatch with interface VPC endpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/cloudwatch-and-interface-VPC.html)

A company uses Amazon Route 53 to host a public hosted zone for example.com. A network engineer recently lowered the TTL on several records to 60 seconds. The network engineer wants to determine whether this change has increased the number of Route 53 queries beyond the expected levels the company established before the change. The network engineer must obtain the number of queries made to the example.com public hosted zone.  
  
Which solution provides this information?

options.text: Create a new trail in AWS CloudTrail to include Route 53 data events. Send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Set up a CloudWatch metric filter to count the number of queries and create graphs.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to access the AWS/Route 53 namespace and to check the DNSQueries metric for the public hosted zone.
Use Amazon CloudWatch to access the AWS/Route 53 Resolver namespace and to check the InboundQueryVolume metric for a specific endpoint.
Configure logging to Amazon CloudWatch for the public hosted zone. Set up a CloudWatch metric filter to count the number of queries and create graphs.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 automatically sends the query count for every public hosted zone to Amazon CloudWatch. The `DNSQueries` metric in the `AWS/Route53` namespace reports the number of DNS queries Route 53 responds to for a hosted zone, using the `HostedZoneId` dimension. A shorter TTL can cause resolvers to forward more queries after cached records expire, which this metric can be used to assess. [Monitoring hosted zones using Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/monitoring-hosted-zones-with-cloudwatch.html)

**Learn more:** [Monitoring hosted zones using Amazon CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/monitoring-hosted-zones-with-cloudwatch.html) · [Viewing DNS query metrics for a public hosted zone](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/hosted-zone-public-viewing-query-metrics.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a 2 Gbps AWS Direct Connect hosted connection from its office to a VPC in the ap-southeast-2 Region. A network engineer adds a 5 Gbps Direct Connect hosted connection from a separate Direct Connect location in the same Region. The hosted connections connect to different routers at the office, with an iBGP session running between the routers.  
  
The network engineer needs to ensure that the VPC uses the 5 Gbps hosted connection to route traffic to the office. Failover to the 2 Gbps hosted connection must occur if the 5 Gbps hosted connection goes down.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure an outbound BGP policy from the router that is connected to the 2 Gbps connection. Advertise routes with a longer AS_PATH attribute to AWS.
Advertise a longer prefix route from the router that is connected to the 2 Gbps connection.
Advertise a less specific route from the router that is connected to the 5 Gbps connection.
Configure an outbound BGP policy from the router that is connected to the 5 Gbps connection. Advertise routes with a longer AS_PATH attribute to AWS.

questions.explanation:
For private or transit Direct Connect virtual interfaces, AWS uses AS_PATH length to select a route when prefix length and local preference are equal. Advertising the office routes over the 2 Gbps connection with a longer AS_PATH makes that connection the passive path; AWS prefers the shorter AS_PATH through the 5 Gbps connection. When that connection fails and its routes are withdrawn, the 2 Gbps route becomes the available path.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect routing policies and BGP communities](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/routing-and-bgp.html) · [AWS Direct Connect private virtual interface routing example](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/private-transit-vif-example.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances in two production VPCs across every Availability Zone in the `us-east-1` Region. The production VPCs are named VPC A and VPC B.  
  
A new security regulation requires inspection of all traffic between the production VPCs before it is routed to its ultimate destination. The company deploys a new shared VPC containing a stateful firewall appliance and a transit gateway with a VPC attachment across all VPCs, routing traffic between VPC A and VPC B through the firewall appliance for inspection. During testing, the company finds that the transit gateway drops traffic whenever it travels between two Availability Zones.  
  
What should a network engineer do to resolve this issue with the **LEAST** management overhead?

options.text: In the shared VPC, replace the VPC attachment with a VPN attachment. Create a VPN tunnel between the transit gateway and the firewall appliance. Configure BGP.
Enable transit gateway appliance mode on the VPC attachment in VPC A and VPC B.
Enable transit gateway appliance mode on the VPC attachment in the shared VPC.
In the shared VPC, configure one VPC peering connection to VPC A and another VPC peering connection to VPC B.

questions.explanation:
A stateful firewall must receive both directions of a flow through the same Availability Zone and appliance instance so it can maintain connection state. Enabling Transit Gateway appliance mode on the shared VPC attachment provides flow stickiness for the VPC that contains the firewall, preventing asymmetric cross-Availability-Zone routing that causes stateful inspection traffic to be dropped.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html) · [Amazon VPC attachments in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-vpc-attachments.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates multiple VPCs with subnets that use IPv4. VPC traffic to the internet passes through a NAT gateway. The company wants to migrate to IPv6.  
  
A network engineer creates several IPv6-only subnets in an existing testing VPC. The engineer deploys a new Amazon EC2 instance with an IPv6 address into one of those subnets. During testing, the engineer finds that the new EC2 instance cannot communicate over the internet with an IPv4-only service. The engineer must enable the IPv6 EC2 instance to communicate with that IPv4-only service.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Enable DNS64 for the IPv6-only subnets. Update the route tables for the IPv6-only subnets to send traffic through the NAT gateway.
Enable NAT64 for the testing VPC. Reconfigure the existing NAT gateway to support IPv6.
Enable DNS64 for the new EC2 instance. Create a new egress-only internet gateway that supports IPv6.
Enable NAT64 for each route table. Create a new NAT gateway that supports both IPv4 and IPv6.

questions.explanation:
DNS64 on an IPv6-only subnet causes Route 53 Resolver to synthesize an IPv6 address for an IPv4-only DNS destination. Routing that synthesized IPv6 traffic through a NAT gateway lets the gateway perform NAT64, translating the IPv6 traffic to IPv4 for communication with the internet service. NAT64 is automatically available on existing and new NAT gateways.

**Learn more:** [DNS64 and NAT64 - Amazon Virtual Private Cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-nat64-dns64.html)

options.text: Configure the EC2 instances to be VPC traffic mirror sources. Deploy software on the traffic mirror target to forward the data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Analyze the data by using CloudWatch Logs Insights
Configure the NAT gateway to be a VPC traffic mirror source. Deploy software on the traffic mirror target to forward the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Analyze the data by using Amazon Athena.
Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the EC2 instances. Specify the default format and set Amazon CloudWatch Logs as the log destination. Analyze the flow log data by using CloudWatch Logs Insights.
Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the EC2 instances. Specify a custom format and set Amazon S3 as the log destination. Analyze the flow log data by using Amazon Athena.

questions.explanation:
VPC Traffic Mirroring copies inbound and outbound traffic from an EC2 instance’s elastic network interface to a monitoring appliance. The appliance can inspect the original packet headers and TCP payload, including the requested first 8 bytes, and forward the extracted data to CloudWatch Logs for analysis with CloudWatch Logs Insights. VPC Flow Logs provide flow-level metadata rather than TCP segment contents, so they cannot meet the payload-capture requirement.

**Learn more:** [How Traffic Mirroring works - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-how-it-works.html) · [Understanding traffic mirror packet format - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-packet-formats.html)

A company has set up an AWS Cloud WAN core network with edge locations in the `us-east-1` and `us-west-1` Regions. Each edge location contains two segments: development and staging. The segments use the default core network policy.  
  
The company has attached VPCs to the core network. A development VPC is attached to the development segment in `us-east-1` and uses the `10.0.0.0/16` CIDR block. A staging VPC is attached to the staging segment in `us-west-1` and uses the `10.5.0.0/16` CIDR block. The company has updated both VPC route tables with a route that sends all `0.0.0.0/0` traffic to the core network.  
  
The company’s network team must establish communication between the two VPCs by using the AWS Cloud WAN core network. The team receives no response when testing communication between the VPCs. The team has confirmed that security groups and network ACLs are not blocking the traffic.  
  
What should the network team do to establish this communication?

options.text: Update both VPC route tables to have a new static route. Configure a route on the development VPC to direct the traffic for 10.0.0.0/16 to the development VPC attachment. Configure a route on the staging VPC to direct the traffic for 10.5.0.0/16 to the staging VPC attachment.
Update the segment filter to allow traffic on the development and staging segments.
Set the isolate-attachments parameter to False for the development and staging segments.

Update the core network policy to add a static route for each segment. Configure a route to direct the traffic for 10.0.0.0/16 to the development VPC attachment. Configure a route to direct the traffic for 10.5.0.0/16 to the staging VPC attachment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cloud WAN segments are separate routing domains, and attachments in different segments cannot communicate by default. Adding static routes in the core network policy for `10.0.0.0/16` and `10.5.0.0/16`, each targeting the applicable VPC attachment, provides the required inter-segment routes. A segment filter only controls routes that have already been shared, while `isolate-attachments` affects attachments within the same segment.

**Learn more:** [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html) · [Add segment actions in an AWS Cloud WAN core network policy version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policy-network-actions-routes.html)

A company runs business applications on AWS. The company uses 50 AWS accounts, thousands of VPCs, and 3 AWS Regions across the United States and Europe.  
  
A network engineer must establish network connectivity between an on-premises data center and the Regions. The network engineer must also establish connectivity between the VPCs. On premises, users and applications must be able to connect to applications running in the VPCs.  
  
The company has an existing AWS Direct Connect connection that the network engineer can use. The network engineer creates a transit gateway in each Region and configures the transit gateways as inter-Region peers.  
  
Which solution will provide network connectivity from the on-premises data center to the Regions and provide inter-VPC communications across the different Regions?

options.text: Create a private VIF with a gateway type of virtual private gateway. Configure the private VIF to use a virtual private gateway that is associated with one of the VPCs.
Create a private VIF to a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate the new Direct Connect gateway with a virtual private gateway in each VPC.
Create transit VIF with a gateway association to a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate each transit gateway with the new Direct Connect gateway.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection that uses a public VIF for the Direct Connect connection. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateways.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Direct Connect gateway can be associated with transit gateways, and a transit virtual interface connects the Direct Connect connection to that Direct Connect gateway. This enables the on-premises network to reach VPCs attached to each Regional transit gateway, while the inter-Region transit gateway peering carries communication between VPCs in different Regions.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [Create a transit virtual interface to the Direct Connect gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-transit-vif-for-gateway.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses a 4 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection in a link aggregation group (LAG) bundle to connect to five VPCs deployed in the us-east-1 Region. Each VPC supports a separate business unit and uses its own private VIF for connectivity to the on-premises environment. Users report slowness when accessing resources hosted on AWS.  
  
A network engineer observes sudden throughput increases, with the Direct Connect connection becoming saturated at the same time for approximately 1 hour each business day. The company needs to determine which business unit is responsible for the sudden throughput increase. The network engineer must obtain this information and implement a solution to resolve the issue.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Create a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection. Shift traffic from the existing dedicated connection to the new dedicated connection.

Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Upgrade the bandwidth of the existing dedicated connection to 10 Gbps.

Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for ConnectionBpsIngress and ConnectionPpsEgress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Upgrade the existing dedicated connection to a 5 Gbps hosted connection.

Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for ConnectionBpsIngress and ConnectionPpsEgress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Create a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection. Shift traffic from the existing dedicated connection to the new dedicated connection.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudWatch VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress and VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress report bitrate for an individual Direct Connect virtual interface, allowing the high-throughput business unit to be identified. Connection-level metrics report aggregate connection traffic and cannot isolate a VIF. AWS Direct Connect dedicated connections have fixed supported port speeds; moving traffic to a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection provides the required additional capacity.

**Learn more:** [Monitor with Amazon CloudWatch — AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-cloudwatch.html) · [Direct Connect connection options — AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)

A company is rolling out an application implemented as a set of containers in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The company will use the Fargate launch type for its tasks. The containers will run workloads that need connectivity initiated through an SSL connection. Traffic must be able to reach the application from other AWS accounts through private connectivity. The application must scale in a manageable manner as more consumers use it.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Choose a Gateway Load Balancer (GLB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create a lifecycle hook to add new tasks to the target group from Amazon ECS as required to handle scaling. Specify the GLB in the service definition. Create a VPC peer for external AWS accounts. Update the route tables so that the AWS accounts can reach the GLB.

Choose an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create path-based routing rules to allow the application to target the containers that are registered in the target group. Specify the ALB in the service definition. Create a VPC endpoint service for the ALB Share the VPC endpoint service with other AWS accounts.

Choose an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create path-based routing rules to allow the application to target the containers that are registered in the target group. Specify the ALB in the service definition. Create a VPC peer for the external AWS accounts. Update the route tables so that the AWS accounts can reach the ALB.

Choose a Network Load Balancer (NLB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Specify the NLB in the service definition. Create a VPC endpoint service for the NLB. Share the VPC endpoint service with other AWS accounts.

questions.explanation:
An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service requires a Network Load Balancer or Gateway Load Balancer; an Application Load Balancer cannot directly back the endpoint service. A Network Load Balancer can use a TLS listener for SSL/TLS connections, routes traffic to the ECS service’s registered Fargate task IP targets, and provides a PrivateLink endpoint service that can be shared with other AWS accounts. Gateway Load Balancers are designed for virtual network appliances rather than application workloads.

**Learn more:** [Create an endpoint service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html) · [Listeners for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html)

3f:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company needs to analyze TCP internet traffic that originates from Amazon EC2 instances in its VPC. The EC2 instances establish connections through a NAT gateway."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to capture traffic data, including source and destination IP addresses, ports, and the first 8 bytes of the TCP segments. It must collect, store, and analyze every required data point."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Configure the EC2 instances to be VPC traffic mirror sources. Deploy software on the traffic mirror target to forward the data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Analyze the data by using CloudWatch Logs Insights","B":"Configure the NAT gateway to be a VPC traffic mirror source. Deploy software on the traffic mirror target to forward the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Analyze the data by using Amazon Athena.","C":"Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the EC2 instances. Specify the default format and set Amazon CloudWatch Logs as the log destination. Analyze the flow log data by using CloudWatch Logs Insights.","D":"Turn on VPC Flow Logs for the EC2 instances. Specify a custom format and set Amazon S3 as the log destination. Analyze the flow log data by using Amazon Athena."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"VPC Traffic Mirroring copies inbound and outbound traffic from an EC2 instance’s elastic network interface to a monitoring appliance. The appliance can inspect the original packet headers and TCP payload, including the requested first 8 bytes, and forward the extracted data to CloudWatch Logs for analysis with CloudWatch Logs Insights. VPC Flow Logs provide flow-level metadata rather than TCP segment contents, so they cannot meet the payload-capture requirement.

**Learn more:** [How Traffic Mirroring works - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-how-it-works.html) · [Understanding traffic mirror packet format - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-packet-formats.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c68b0372-89f4-4ee2-b4a9-fda571a53f08","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company’s network team must establish communication between the two VPCs by using the AWS Cloud WAN core network. The team receives no response when testing communication between the VPCs. The team has confirmed that security groups and network ACLs are not blocking the traffic."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"What should the network team do to establish this communication?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Update both VPC route tables to have a new static route. Configure a route on the development VPC to direct the traffic for 10.0.0.0/16 to the development VPC attachment. Configure a route on the staging VPC to direct the traffic for 10.5.0.0/16 to the staging VPC attachment.","B":"Update the segment filter to allow traffic on the development and staging segments.","C":"Set the isolate-attachments parameter to False for the development and staging segments.","D":"Update the core network policy to add a static route for each segment. Configure a route to direct the traffic for 10.0.0.0/16 to the development VPC attachment. Configure a route to direct the traffic for 10.5.0.0/16 to the staging VPC attachment."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"AWS Cloud WAN segments are separate routing domains, and attachments in different segments cannot communicate by default. Adding static routes in the core network policy for `10.0.0.0/16` and `10.5.0.0/16`, each targeting the applicable VPC attachment, provides the required inter-segment routes. A segment filter only controls routes that have already been shared, while `isolate-attachments` affects attachments within the same segment.

**Learn more:** [Core network policy version parameters in AWS Cloud WAN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policies-json.html) · [Add segment actions in an AWS Cloud WAN core network policy version](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/cloudwan/cloudwan-policy-network-actions-routes.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"3eea65fd-8294-4935-8af1-05fc93e71f60","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"A network engineer must establish network connectivity between an on-premises data center and the Regions. The network engineer must also establish connectivity between the VPCs. On premises, users and applications must be able to connect to applications running in the VPCs."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company has an existing AWS Direct Connect connection that the network engineer can use. The network engineer creates a transit gateway in each Region and configures the transit gateways as inter-Region peers."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will provide network connectivity from the on-premises data center to the Regions and provide inter-VPC communications across the different Regions?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a private VIF with a gateway type of virtual private gateway. Configure the private VIF to use a virtual private gateway that is associated with one of the VPCs.","B":"Create a private VIF to a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate the new Direct Connect gateway with a virtual private gateway in each VPC.","C":"Create transit VIF with a gateway association to a new Direct Connect gateway. Associate each transit gateway with the new Direct Connect gateway.","D":"Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection that uses a public VIF for the Direct Connect connection. Attach the Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateways."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"An AWS Direct Connect gateway can be associated with transit gateways, and a transit virtual interface connects the Direct Connect connection to that Direct Connect gateway. This enables the on-premises network to reach VPCs attached to each Regional transit gateway, while the inter-Region transit gateway peering carries communication between VPCs in different Regions.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [Create a transit virtual interface to the Direct Connect gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/create-transit-vif-for-gateway.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"8a4a9ec1-2bdd-4e2f-9b28-d126c5e143e4","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
51:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company uses a 4 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection in a link aggregation group (LAG) bundle to connect to five VPCs deployed in the us-east-1 Region. Each VPC supports a separate business unit and uses its own private VIF for connectivity to the on-premises environment. Users report slowness when accessing resources hosted on AWS."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"A network engineer observes sudden throughput increases, with the Direct Connect connection becoming saturated at the same time for approximately 1 hour each business day. The company needs to determine which business unit is responsible for the sudden throughput increase. The network engineer must obtain this information and implement a solution to resolve the issue."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Create a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection. Shift traffic from the existing dedicated connection to the new dedicated connection.","B":"Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress and VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Upgrade the bandwidth of the existing dedicated connection to 10 Gbps.","C":"Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for ConnectionBpsIngress and ConnectionPpsEgress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Upgrade the existing dedicated connection to a 5 Gbps hosted connection.","D":"Review the Amazon CloudWatch metrics for ConnectionBpsIngress and ConnectionPpsEgress to determine which VIF is sending the highest throughput during the period in which slowness is observed. Create a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection. Shift traffic from the existing dedicated connection to the new dedicated connection."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon CloudWatch VirtualInterfaceBpsIngress and VirtualInterfaceBpsEgress report bitrate for an individual Direct Connect virtual interface, allowing the high-throughput business unit to be identified. Connection-level metrics report aggregate connection traffic and cannot isolate a VIF. AWS Direct Connect dedicated connections have fixed supported port speeds; moving traffic to a new 10 Gbps dedicated connection provides the required additional capacity.

**Learn more:** [Monitor with Amazon CloudWatch — AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/monitoring-cloudwatch.html) · [Direct Connect connection options — AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/connection_options.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"e16fa531-325b-4971-8e21-c944a771d290","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is rolling out an application implemented as a set of containers in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The company will use the Fargate launch type for its tasks. The containers will run workloads that need connectivity initiated through an SSL connection. Traffic must be able to reach the application from other AWS accounts through private connectivity. The application must scale in a manageable manner as more consumers use it."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L53",null,{"choices":{"A":"Choose a Gateway Load Balancer (GLB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create a lifecycle hook to add new tasks to the target group from Amazon ECS as required to handle scaling. Specify the GLB in the service definition. Create a VPC peer for external AWS accounts. Update the route tables so that the AWS accounts can reach the GLB.","B":"Choose an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create path-based routing rules to allow the application to target the containers that are registered in the target group. Specify the ALB in the service definition. Create a VPC endpoint service for the ALB Share the VPC endpoint service with other AWS accounts.","C":"Choose an Application Load Balancer (ALB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Create path-based routing rules to allow the application to target the containers that are registered in the target group. Specify the ALB in the service definition. Create a VPC peer for the external AWS accounts. Update the route tables so that the AWS accounts can reach the ALB.","D":"Choose a Network Load Balancer (NLB) as the type of load balancer for the ECS service. Specify the NLB in the service definition. Create a VPC endpoint service for the NLB. Share the VPC endpoint service with other AWS accounts."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"An AWS PrivateLink endpoint service requires a Network Load Balancer or Gateway Load Balancer; an Application Load Balancer cannot directly back the endpoint service. A Network Load Balancer can use a TLS listener for SSL/TLS connections, routes traffic to the ECS service’s registered Fargate task IP targets, and provides a PrivateLink endpoint service that can be shared with other AWS accounts. Gateway Load Balancers are designed for virtual network appliances rather than application workloads.

**Learn more:** [Create an endpoint service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html) · [Listeners for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-listeners.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"d77ae978-22df-4ffb-9cb1-96efa522ca73","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-advanced-networking-specialty-ans-c01","mode":"default"}}]]
A company operates an internal web-based application for employee use. The company hosts the application through a VPN in its on-premises network. The application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in a private subnet behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in that same subnet. The instances belong to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group.  
  
During a recent security incident, the application experienced SQL injection. A network engineer must implement a solution that prevents future SQL injection attacks.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an AWS WAF web ACL that includes rules to block SQL injection attacks.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Specify the EC2 instances as the origin.
Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer.
Associate the AWS WAF web ACL with the NLB.
Associate the AWS WAF web ACL with the Application Load Balancer.
Associate the AWS WAF web ACL with the Amazon CloudFront distribution.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF web ACL rules can detect and block requests containing malicious SQL code. AWS WAF supports association with an Application Load Balancer, but not with a Network Load Balancer. Replacing the NLB with an ALB and associating the SQL-injection-blocking web ACL with that ALB places WAF inspection in front of the EC2 application fleet.

A company has established a new AWS Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud. The company created a new private VIF on that connection, but the VIF status is **DOWN**.  
  
A network engineer confirms from the AWS Management Console that the physical connection status is **UP** and **RUNNING**. The engineer checks the customer Direct Connect router and finds the ARP entry for the VLAN interface created for the private VIF at AWS.  
  
What might be causing the private VIF to show a **DOWN** status?

options.text: ICMP is blocked on the customer Direct Connect router.
TCP port 179 is blocked on the customer Direct Connect router.
The IEEE 802.1Q VLAN identifier is misconfigured on the customer Direct Connect router.
The company has configured IEEE 802.1ad instead of 802.1Q on the customer Direct Connect router.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect virtual interface reports DOWN when its BGP session is down. An ARP entry for the AWS VLAN interface demonstrates Layer 2 connectivity, so the VLAN encapsulation is working. BGP establishes its peer connection over TCP port 179; a customer-router firewall or ACL that blocks this port prevents BGP from establishing.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot layer 3/4 (Network/Transport) issues - AWS Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/ts-layer-3.html) · [VirtualInterface - AWS Direct Connect API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/APIReference/API_VirtualInterface.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has established connectivity between its on-premises data center in Paris, France, and the AWS Cloud by using an AWS Direct Connect connection. The company uses a transit VIF that connects the Direct Connect connection to a transit gateway hosted in the Europe (Paris) Region. The company hosts workloads in private subnets in several VPCs attached to the transit gateway.  
  
The company recently acquired another corporation that hosts workloads on premises in an office building in Tokyo, Japan. The company must migrate the workloads from the Tokyo office to AWS. These workloads must be able to access the company’s existing workloads in Paris. The company must also establish connectivity between the Tokyo office building and the Paris data center.  
  
In the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region, the company creates a new VPC with private subnets for migrating the workloads. The workload migration must be completed in 5 days. The workloads cannot be directly accessible from the internet.  
  
Which set of steps should a network engineer take to meet these requirements?

options.text: 1. Create public subnets in the Tokyo VPC to migrate the workloads into.2. Configure an internet gateway for the Tokyo office to reach the Tokyo VPC.3. Configure security groups on the Tokyo workloads to only allow traffic from the Tokyo office and the Paris workloads.4. Create peering connections between the Tokyo VPC and the Paris VPCs.5. Configure a VPN connection between the Paris data center and the Tokyo office by using existing routers.

1. Configure a transit gateway in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region. Associate this transit gateway with the Tokyo VPC.2. Create peering connections between the Tokyo transit gateway and the Paris transit gateway.3. Set up a new Direct Connect connection from the Tokyo office to the Tokyo transit gateway.4. Configure routing on both transit gateways to allow data to flow between sites and the VPCs.

1. Configure a transit gateway in the Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region. Associate this transit gateway with the Tokyo VPC.2. Create peering connections between the Tokyo transit gateway and the Paris transit gateway.3. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the Tokyo office. Set the Tokyo transit gateway as the target.4. Configure routing on both transit gateways to allow data to flow between sites and the VPCs.

1. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the Tokyo office to the Paris transit gateway.2. Create an association between the Paris transit gateway and the Tokyo VPC.3. Configure routing on the Paris transit gateway to allow data to flow between sites and the VPC.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Site-to-Site VPN can provide the rapidly deployable private connection from the Tokyo office to a Tokyo transit gateway. Attaching the Tokyo VPC to that transit gateway and peering it with the Paris transit gateway enables routing between the Tokyo VPN and VPC, and the Paris transit gateway’s VPC and Direct Connect attachments. Transit gateway peering supports routing traffic between the peer gateways’ attachments when the required routes are configured. This design keeps the migrated workloads in private subnets without direct internet access.

A logistics company operates multiple VPCs in an AWS Region and uses a transit gateway to interconnect the VPCs. Several on-premises offices connect to the transit gateway through AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections over the internet. The company has configured one transit gateway VPN attachment for each office.  
  
Route propagation is enabled for all route tables. Each Site-to-Site VPN connection has two tunnels configured as active-passive. The company configured appropriate static routes on both the Site-to-Site VPN connection and each office’s customer gateway.  
  
The company wants to use both IPsec tunnels for every office to maximize aggregate VPN connection bandwidth.  
  
Which design changes are required to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Transit Gateway Connect attachment for each office Use the existing VPN attachments as the transport for the new Connect attachments. Set up a Generic RoutingEncapsulation (GRE) tunnel on each customer gateway that terminates on the Connect attachment for each office. Move the static routes from the transit gateway VPN attachment to the customer gateway for the transit gateway Connect attachment.

Enable equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing on the transit gateway. Ensure ECMP is supported by and enabled on the customer gateways. Enable ECMP on the Site-to-Site VPN connection. Ensure static routes on the customer gateways have equal metrics and administrative distance.

Enable equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing on the transit gateway. (Ensure ECMP is supported by and enabled on the customer gateways. Change the routing configuration between the transit gateway and the customer gateways from static routing to BGP. Remove related static routes from the customer gateways.

Enable equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing on the transit gateway. Ensure ECMP is supported by and enabled on the customer gateways. Change the routing configuration between the transit gateway and the customer gateways from static routing to BGP. Ensure the customer gateway applies the correct community strings to give the transit gateway the ability to perform ECMP forwarding.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway uses ECMP to distribute traffic across equal VPN paths and aggregate tunnel bandwidth, but ECMP requires Site-to-Site VPN connections configured with dynamic BGP routing; VPN connections using static routing do not support ECMP. ECMP must be enabled on the transit gateway and supported and enabled on the customer gateway, while BGP replaces the related static routing.

A company's application is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in a single VPC within an AWS Region. The EC2 instances run in two Availability Zones. The company decides to use a fleet of traffic-inspection instances from AWS Marketplace to inspect traffic between the VPC and the internet. The company is conducting tests before deploying the architecture to production.  
  
The fleet is in a shared inspection VPC behind a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). To minimize solution cost, the company deployed only one inspection instance in each Availability Zone used by the application.  
  
During testing, a network engineer observes that traffic inspection functions as expected while the network is stable. However, when the inspection instances undergo maintenance, internet sessions time out for some application instances. The application instances cannot establish new sessions.  
  
Which combination of steps will remediate these issues? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy one inspection instance in the Availability Zones that do not have inspection instances deployed.
Deploy one additional inspection instance in each Availability Zone where the inspection instances are deployed.
Enable the cross-zone load balancing attribute for the GWLB.
Deploy inspection instances in an Auto Scaling group. Define a scaling policy that is based on CPU load.
Attach the GWLB to all Availability Zones in the Region.

questions.explanation:
Gateway Load Balancer uses flow stickiness, so an existing flow remains associated with its original appliance even after that appliance becomes unhealthy. New flows are routed only to healthy targets. Adding another inspection instance to each application Availability Zone supplies local healthy-target redundancy during maintenance. Gateway Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing is disabled by default; enabling it lets each GWLB node route new flows to healthy targets in all enabled Availability Zones, preventing a maintenance event in one zone from leaving that node without a healthy appliance.

**Learn more:** [Health checks for Gateway Load Balancer target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/health-checks.html) · [Target groups for your Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/target-groups.html)

A network engineer is designing a hybrid networking environment to link a company’s corporate network with the company’s AWS environment. The AWS environment includes 30 VPCs across 3 AWS Regions.  
  
The network engineer must implement a solution that centrally filters traffic by using a firewall approved by the company’s security team. The solution must allow every VPC to connect to every other VPC. Connectivity between AWS and the corporate network must satisfy a minimum bandwidth requirement of 2 Gbps.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an IPsec VPN connection between the corporate network and a new transit gateway. Connect all VPCs to the transit gateway. Associate the approved firewall with the transit gateway.

Deploy a single 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the corporate network and virtual private gateway of each VPC. Connect the virtual private gateways to a Direct Connect gateway. Build an IPsec tunnel to a new transit VPC. Deploy the approved firewall to the transit VPC.

Deploy two 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections in different Direct Connect locations to connect to the corporate network. Build a transit VIF on each connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the Direct Connect gateway with a new transit gateway for each Region. Configure the VIFs to use equal-cost multipath (ECMP) routing. Connect all the VPCs in the three Regions to the transit gateway. Configure the transit gateway route table to route traffic to an inspection VPDeploy the approved firewall to the inspection VPC.

Deploy four 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connections in different Direct Connect locations to connect to the corporate network. Build a transit VIF on each connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Associate the Direct Connect gateway with a new transit gateway for each Region. Connect the transit gateways by using a transit gateway peering attachment. Configure the VIFs to use equal-cost multipath (ECMP) routing. Configure transit gateway route tables to route traffic to an inspection VPC. Deploy the approved firewall to the inspection VPC.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is a Regional service; transit gateway peering attachments provide the required routing between transit gateways in different Regions so VPCs attached in all three Regions can communicate. Routing transit gateway traffic through an inspection VPC centralizes firewall inspection. Direct Connect transit VIFs attached to a Direct Connect gateway can connect the corporate network to associated transit gateways, and ECMP across the Direct Connect connections provides the necessary aggregate bandwidth.

The company accidentally deletes the route to the `eu-central-1` VPCs from the `us-west-2` transit gateway route table. It also accidentally deletes the route to the `us-west-2` VPCs from the `eu-central-1` transit gateway route table.  
  
How can a network engineer identify this misconfiguration with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use the Route Analyzer feature for AWS Transit Gateway Network Manager.
Use the AWSSupport-SetupIPMonitoringFromVPC AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Push network telemetry data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for analysis.
Use VPC flow logs in eu-central-1 and us-west-2 to analyze the missing routes.
Use Amazon VPC Traffic Mirroring in eu-central-1 or us-west-2 to take packet captures and troubleshoot the connectivity issues.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway Network Manager Route Analyzer analyzes the routing path and the associated transit gateway route tables between chosen source and destination attachments. It can analyze the return path as well, directly revealing missing forward and reverse transit gateway routes without deploying telemetry, reviewing flow logs, or capturing packets.

**Learn more:** [Route Analyzer for AWS Network Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/tgwnm/route-analyzer.html) · [Example: Route analysis for peered transit gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-manager/latest/tgwnm/example-route-analyzer.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A network engineer manages a company's AWS infrastructure. The engineer used AWS Transit Gateway to establish a hub-and-spoke architecture and created a shared services VPC to centralize access to interface VPC endpoints.  
  
The company uses AWS Organizations to manage AWS accounts for multiple teams in one organization. Each team has a separate account and VPC, and all team accounts need access to the interface VPC endpoints.  
  
The network engineer needs a solution that grants every account the minimum necessary access. Each team's account must be able to access only an authorized list of interface VPC endpoints. The solution must have minimal impact on the existing architecture.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a separate shared services VPC for each team account. Include the interface VPC endpoints that the team is authorized to use in each VPC. Use a unique transit gateway route table to connect each team's spoke VPC to the team's shared services VPC.

Apply security groups to the interface VPC endpoints that are in the shared services VPC. Configure each security group to allow only the CIDR block of the team spoke VPCs that are authorized to use the endpoints included in the security group.

Create a unique interface VPC endpoint for each team that is authorized to access a service. Update routing for the shared services VPC so that the CIDR block for each team can access only the set of endpoints the team is authorized to access.
Associate an endpoint policy with each interface VPC endpoint. In each policy, deny all the traffic except for traffic from accounts that are authorized to access the corresponding service.

questions.explanation:
Security group rules on interface endpoint network interfaces control which source networks can connect to each endpoint. Using endpoint-specific security groups that permit only the CIDR ranges of authorized team spoke VPCs restricts each team to its approved endpoints while retaining the existing shared services VPC and Transit Gateway architecture.

A financial company located in the us-east-1 Region must establish secure connectivity to AWS. The company operates two on-premises data centers, both within the same Region. Its network team must establish hybrid connectivity to the AWS environment with reliable, consistent connectivity.  
  
The connection must provide access to the company’s private resources in its AWS environment. These resources are in the us-east-1 and us-west-2 Regions. The connection must also allow resources from the corporate networks to send large volumes of data to Amazon S3 over that same connection. To satisfy compliance requirements, the connection must be highly available and encrypt all packets sent between the on-premises location and any AWS services.  
  
Which combination of steps should the network team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Set up a private VIF to send data to Amazon S3. Use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the private VIF to encrypt data in transit to the VPCs in us-east-1 and us-west-2.
Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection to each of the company's data centers.
Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection from one of the company's data centers to us-east-1 and us-west-2.

Direct Connect supports access to remote-Region VPCs, and AWS documents the public-VIF-plus-VPN pattern for VPN connectivity to a VPC in a remote Region.

A company recently moved its Amazon EC2 instances into VPC private subnets to meet a security-compliance requirement. The EC2 instances now access the internet through a NAT gateway. Following the migration, some long-running database queries from private EC2 instances to a publicly accessible third-party database no longer receive responses. Database query logs show that the queries completed successfully after 7 minutes, but the client EC2 instances never received the response.  
  
Which configuration change should a network engineer make to resolve this issue?

options.text: Configure the NAT gateway timeout to allow connections for up to 600 seconds.
Enable enhanced networking on the client EC2 instances.
Enable TCP keepalive on the client EC2 instances with a value of less than 300 seconds.
Close idle TCP connections through the NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
Amazon VPC NAT gateways time out TCP connections that have been idle for 350 seconds or longer. A long-running query can leave the TCP flow inactive while the database processes it, causing the NAT gateway to remove the translation before the response returns. Enabling TCP keepalive with an interval below 300 seconds generates traffic before the idle timeout and preserves the connection.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot NAT gateways - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-troubleshooting.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its critical workloads from an on-premises data center to Amazon EC2 instances. The plan includes a new 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect dedicated connection from the on-premises data center to a VPC attached to a transit gateway. The migration must take place over encrypted paths between the on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements while delivering the **HIGHEST** throughput?

options.text: Configure a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the transit gateway as a VPN attachment.
Configure a transit VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Configure an IPsec VPN connection to an EC2 instance that is running third-party VPN software.
Configure MACsec for the Direct Connect connection. Configure a transit VIF to a Direct Connect gateway that is associated with the transit gateway.
Configure a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Configure two AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections to the transit gateway. Enable equal-cost multi-path (ECMP) routing.

questions.explanation:
MACsec provides Layer 2 encryption on supported 10 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connections, avoiding the lower per-tunnel throughput constraints of IPsec Site-to-Site VPN. A transit virtual interface connected to a Direct Connect gateway associated with a transit gateway provides the required Direct Connect path to the VPCs reachable through that transit gateway.

**Learn more:** [MAC Security in Direct Connect](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/MACsec.html) · [AWS Direct Connect virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a VPC in the AWS Cloud. The company recently acquired a competitor that also has a VPC in the AWS Cloud. A network engineer identifies overlapping IP address ranges between the two VPCs. Both VPCs need access to an AWS Marketplace partner service.  
  
Which solution will ensure interoperability between the VPC-hosted services and the AWS Marketplace partner service?

options.text: Configure VPC peering with static routing between the VPCs. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with static routing to the partner service.

Configure a NAT gateway in the VPCs. Configure default routes in each VPC to point to the local NAT gateway. Attach each NAT gateway to a transit gateway. Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection with static routing to the partner service.

Configure AWS PrivateLink to facilitate connectivity between the VPCs and the partner service. Use the DNS name that is created with the associated interface endpoints to route traffic between the VPCs and the partner service.

Configure a NAT instance in the VPCs. Configure default routes in each VPC to point to the local NAT instance. Configure an interface endpoint in each VPC to connect to the partner service. Use the DNS name that is created with the associated interface endpoints to route traffic between the VPCs and the partner service.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink supports private access to supported AWS Marketplace partner services through interface VPC endpoints. The endpoints place private network interfaces in each consumer VPC, and their DNS names direct traffic to the service without requiring routable connectivity between the two VPC CIDR ranges. This design accommodates overlapping VPC IP address ranges.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink - Amazon VPC Connectivity Options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-privatelink.html) · [AWS PrivateLink concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/concepts.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has users who work remotely from home. The company wants to migrate these users to Amazon WorkSpaces to gain additional security visibility.  
  
The company has deployed WorkSpaces in its own AWS account in VPC A. A network engineer decides to provide the security visibility by using two firewall appliances behind a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB). The network engineer provisions a separate VPC, VPC B, in another account and deploys the two firewall appliances across separate Availability Zones.  
  
What should the network engineer do to configure network connectivity for this solution?

options.text: Create a GWLB in VPC A with the firewall appliance instances as targets. Use the GWLB to create a GWLB endpoint. Add the AWS principal ARN of the WorkSpaces account to the principal allow list of the GWLB endpoint. In the WorkSpaces account, create a VPC endpoint and specify the service name that the AWS Management Console provides for the GWLB endpoint. Modify the route tables of VPC A to point the default route to the VPC endpoint.

Create a GWLB in VPC B with the firewall appliance instances as targets. Use the GWLB to create a GWLB endpoint. Add the AWS principal ARN of the WorkSpaces account to the principal allow list of the GWLB endpoint. In the WorkSpaces account, create a VPC endpoint and specify the service name that the AWS Management Console provides for the GWLB endpoint. Modify the route tables of VPC A to point the default route to the GWLB endpoint.

Create a GWLB in VPC B with the firewall appliance instances as targets. Use the GWLB to create a GWLB endpoint. Add the AWS principal ARN of the WorkSpaces account to the principal allow list of the GWLB endpoint. In the WorkSpaces account, create a VPC endpoint and specify the service name that the AWS Management Console provides for the GWLB endpoint. Modify the route tables of VPC A to point the WorkSpaces subnet to the VPC endpoint.

Create a GWLB in VPC B with the firewall appliance instances as targets. Use the GWLB to create a GWLB endpoint. Add the AWS principal ARN of the account that contains the firewall appliances to the principal allow list of the GWLB endpoint. In the WorkSpaces account, create a VPC endpoint and specify the service name that the AWS Management Console provides for the GWLB endpoint. Modify the route tables of VPC A to point the default route to the VPC endpoint.

questions.explanation:
A Gateway Load Balancer is deployed in the service provider VPC with the firewall appliances registered as targets. The WorkSpaces account is the service consumer, so its AWS principal must be permitted to create an endpoint to the GWLB endpoint service. The consumer VPC creates the Gateway Load Balancer endpoint and routes the WorkSpaces subnet’s default route (`0.0.0.0/0`) to that endpoint, directing outbound traffic through the firewall appliances for inspection.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/getting-started.html) · [What is a Gateway Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)

A global company operates business applications in the us-east-1 Region within a VPC. One of the company’s regional offices in London uses a virtual private gateway for an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the VPC. The company has configured a transit gateway and established peering between the VPC and other VPCs that different departments in the company use.  
  
Employees in the London office are experiencing latency problems when connecting to the business applications.  
  
What should a network engineer do to reduce this latency?

options.text: Create a new Site-to-Site VPN connection. Set the transit gateway as the target gateway. Enable acceleration on the new Site-to-Site VPN connection. Update the VPN device in the London office with the new connection details.
Modify the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection by setting the transit gateway as the target gateway. Enable acceleration on the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection.

Create a new transit gateway in the eu-west-2 (London) Region. Peer the new transit gateway with the existing transit gateway. Modify the existing Site-to-Site VPN connection by setting the new transit gateway as the target gateway.
Create a new AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has an endpoint of the Site-to-Site VPN connection. Update the VPN device in the London office with the new connection details.

questions.explanation:
An accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN uses AWS Global Accelerator to route traffic from the on-premises network through a nearby AWS edge location and across the AWS global network. Acceleration is supported only for VPN connections attached to a transit gateway, not a virtual private gateway, and it cannot be enabled on an existing VPN connection. A new accelerated transit gateway VPN connection must therefore be created and its tunnel configuration applied to the customer gateway device.

**Learn more:** [Accelerated AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/accelerated-vpn.html) · [Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/create-vpn-connection.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has built a web service for language translation. The web service application runs on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The instances operate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are deployed in a private subnet. The web service can handle requests containing hundreds of megabytes of data.  
  
The company must allow some customers to access the web service. Each customer has a separate AWS account. The company must make the web service available to approved customers without exposing the web service to every customer.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create VPC peering connections with the approved customers only.
Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Configure the endpoint service to require acceptance that will be granted to approved customers only.
Configure an authentication action for the endpoint service's load balancer to allow customers to log in by using their AWS credentials. Provide only approved customers with the URL.
Configure a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and a listener with the ALB as a target. Associate the NLB with the endpoint service.
Associate the ALB with the endpoint service.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink lets a service provider expose a private endpoint service to selected AWS principals and require acceptance of endpoint connection requests, so access can be limited to approved customer accounts. PrivateLink endpoint services require a Network Load Balancer or Gateway Load Balancer. A Network Load Balancer can use an Application Load Balancer as a target, enabling the existing ALB to continue routing requests to the EC2 Auto Scaling fleet while the NLB serves as the PrivateLink front end.

**Learn more:** [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html) · [Use an Application Load Balancer as a target of a Network Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/application-load-balancer-target.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global company runs all non-production environments in three AWS Regions: `eu-west-1`, `us-east-1`, and `us-west-1`. The company hosts all production workloads in two on-premises data centers. The company has 60 AWS accounts, and each account has two VPCs in every Region. Each VPC has a virtual private gateway on which two VPN connections terminate to provide resilient connectivity to the data centers. The company has 360 VPN tunnels to each data center, creating substantial management overhead. Total VPN throughput for each Region is 500 Mbps.  
  
The company wants to migrate the production environments to AWS. It needs a solution that simplifies the network architecture and supports future growth. The production environments will create an additional 2 Gbps of traffic per Region back to the data centers. This traffic will grow over time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection from each data center to AWS in each Region. Create and attach private VIFs to a single Direct Connect gateway. Attach the Direct Connect gateway to all the VPCs. Remove the existing VPN connections that are attached directly to the virtual private gateways.

Create a single transit gateway with VPN connections from each data center. Share the transit gateway with each account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Attach the transit gateway to each VPC. Remove the existing VPN connections that are attached directly to the virtual private gateways.

Create a transit gateway in each Region with multiple newly commissioned VPN connections from each data center. Share the transit gateways with each account by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). In each Region, attach the transit gateway to each VPRemove the existing VPN connections that are attached directly to the virtual private gateways.

Peer all the VPCs in each Region to a new VPC in each Region that will function as a centralized transit VPC. Create new VPN connections from each data center to the transit VPCs. Terminate the original VPN connections that are attached to all the original VPCs. Retain the new VPN connection to the new transit VPC in each Region.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway provides a regional hub that can connect VPCs and on-premises networks through Site-to-Site VPN attachments. A transit gateway can be shared across AWS accounts through AWS RAM so each account can attach its VPCs. Creating one transit gateway per Region centralizes connectivity while preserving the regional architecture. Multiple dynamically routed VPN connections can use ECMP to aggregate VPN bandwidth beyond the 1.25 Gbps available from a single VPN connection, meeting the added 2 Gbps regional requirement and allowing growth.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html) · [AWS Transit Gateway + AWS Site-to-Site VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-transit-gateway-vpn.html)
